definition_zh: 气候变化；气候变迁；大环境的转变
definition_en: a lasting change in the patterns of temperature, rainfall and wind, especially the change caused by human emissions
core_image: 一本翻了几十年的气象记录，雨量与温度两行都慢慢改了模样
scene: 老农翻着祖父留下的雨量簿，发现同一块田的雨季一年年往后推。 Climate change had shifted the rains so far that the sowing calendar no longer matched the sky.
sceneCN: 这里指「气候型态在长期尺度上的改变」（第 1 个义项：气温、降水、风等气候统计特征持续改变）；句意为气候变化把雨季推得太远，播种日历已对不上天时。图中可辨识物件：雨量簿、日历、田垄、云层。

senses.title: A lasting shift in climate statistics
senses.titleCN: 气候统计特征的长期改变
senses.definition: a lasting change in the statistical patterns of temperature, precipitation and wind over decades or longer
senses.definitionCN: 气温、降水与风等统计型态在数十年或更长时间尺度上的持续改变
senses.example: Climate change had shifted the rains so far that the sowing calendar no longer matched the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化把雨季推得太远，播种日历已对不上天时。
senses.why: Climate is from Greek klima 'slope, zone', the belt of weather a place is inclined toward; change adds Latin cambiare 'to exchange', so the phrase names an exchange of one pattern for another.
senses.whyCN: climate 来自希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」，指某地倾向的天气带；change 添上拉丁 cambiare「交换」，因此短语指一种型态换成了另一种。

senses.title: The present human-driven change
senses.titleCN: 当代人为驱动的气候变化
senses.definition: the current global change in climate attributed mainly to greenhouse gas emissions
senses.definitionCN: 当前全球气候的改变，主要归因于温室气体排放
senses.example: Climate change is now the default reading of the phrase in news reports.
senses.exampleCN: 在新闻报道中，气候变化如今是这个短语的默认读法。
senses.why: Because one instance of the general phenomenon became urgent, the bare phrase came to mean that instance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个一般现象中的某一例变得紧迫，光秃秃的短语便转而指那一例。

senses.title: Change on a geological timescale
senses.titleCN: 地质尺度上的气候变迁
senses.definition: climate shifts reconstructed over thousands or millions of years from ice, rock and sediment
senses.definitionCN: 从冰芯、岩石与沉积物重建的数千至数百万年尺度的气候改变
senses.example: Ice cores record climate change across the last glacial cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 冰芯记录了上一个冰期旋回中的气候变迁。
senses.why: The phrase is older than the current concern: geology used it for any lasting shift, with no human agent implied.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语比当下的忧患更早：地质学用它指任何持久改变，并不含人为施动者。

senses.title: A regional shift in a single climate
senses.definition: a change in the climate of one region, such as a wetter monsoon or a shorter cold season
senses.definitionCN: 某个地区气候的改变，如更湿的季风或更短的冷季
senses.example: Climate change in the highlands has shortened the frost season.
senses.exampleCN: 高原地区的气候变化缩短了霜期。
senses.why: The phrase works at any scale, since climate itself is a regional notion before it is a planetary one.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语适用于任何尺度，因为气候在被当作行星概念之前，先是地区性的概念。

senses.title: The object of mitigation policy
senses.titleCN: 减缓政策所针对的对象
senses.definition: the change as something to be slowed by cutting emissions and by managing land and industry
senses.definitionCN: 作为需要通过削减排放、管理土地与工业来减缓的变化
senses.example: Climate change mitigation costs less than repeated disaster relief.
senses.exampleCN: 减缓气候变化的成本低于反复的灾害救助。
senses.why: Policy split the topic in two: mitigation acts on the cause, and the phrase names what is being slowed.
senses.whyCN: 政策把议题一分为二：减缓作用于原因，而这个短语指被减缓的那个变化。

senses.title: The object of adaptation policy
senses.titleCN: 适应政策所针对的对象
senses.definition: the change as something to be lived with through new crops, defences and planning
senses.definitionCN: 作为需要通过新作物、防护与规划来共处的变化
senses.example: Climate change adaptation built the new sea wall higher than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 为适应气候变化，新海堤修得比旧堤更高。
senses.why: The other half of policy treats the change as a condition rather than a cause, and the same phrase serves both halves.
senses.whyCN: 政策的另一半把这个变化当作条件而非原因，而同一个短语同时服务这两半。

senses.title: A heading in international law
senses.titleCN: 国际法律框架中的用语
senses.definition: the formal label used in treaties and institutions for the issue as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 条约与机构中用来指整个议题的正式标签
senses.example: The protocol fixed climate change as a matter of common concern.
senses.exampleCN: 该议定书把气候变化定为一件事关共同关切的事项。
senses.why: Legal language needs a stable label that covers causes, impacts and obligations at once, which the bare phrase provides.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言需要一个能同时覆盖原因、影响与义务的稳定标签，而这个简洁短语正好提供。

senses.title: A shift in the wider environment
senses.definition: a broad shift in conditions surrounding an activity, group or market
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动、群体或市场所处条件的广泛转变
senses.example: The industry felt a climate change of its own as tariffs fell.
senses.exampleCN: 关税下降时，这个行业感到了自己的气候变化。
senses.why: Climate had long been used figuratively for the prevailing mood, so the compound transfers whole to any atmosphere that alters.
senses.whyCN: climate 早已被比喻使用，指当下流行的氛围，因此这个复合词整体转指任何改变中的环境。

intro.en: Climate change joins Greek klima 'slope, zone' with Latin cambiare 'to exchange'. Both parts entered English through French. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climate change 把希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」与拉丁 cambiare「交换」组合在一起，两个成分都经法语进入英语。复合词是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Klima meant 'a slope, an inclination', and from that 'a zone of the earth' defined by the sun's angle. The word came to mean the weather typical of such a zone.
items.cn: klima 意为「倾斜、倾向」，由此指按太阳角度划分的「地带」，再引申为这一带典型的天气。

items.en: Klima was formed on klinein 'to slope, lean'. The verb belongs to a well-attested Greek family; the noun's shift from slope to zone to weather is a chain of metaphors.
items.cn: klima 由 klinein「倾斜、倚靠」构成。这个动词属于证据充分的希腊词族；名词从「倾斜」到「地带」再到「天气」，是一串比喻的推移。

items.en: Cambiare 'to exchange, barter' is the source of change. Its own origin is uncertain; the suggestion of a Gaulish loan is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: cambiare「交换、以物易物」是 change 的来源。它自身的来源不确定；「借自高卢语」的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Climate entered English in the fourteenth century meaning a zone or region; the weather sense grew through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: climate 在十四世纪进入英语，意为地带或地区；天气义在十六、十七世纪逐步形成。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology used climate change for shifts read from strata, with no reference to human causes.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学用 climate change 指从地层读出的变迁，不涉及人为原因。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of cambiare is unsettled, and its link to a Celtic form is a hypothesis. The compound's first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：cambiare 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，与某种凯尔特语形式的联系只是假说。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and phrases built on climate that are easily swapped; group two holds the neighbouring terms for warming and for long-term shifts.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 climate 构成、容易互换的复合词与短语；第二组是变暖与长期变迁方面的近邻术语。

entries.definition: Short-term or periodic fluctuation around a mean, which happens without the mean itself moving.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕均值的短期或周期波动，均值本身并未移动。

entries.definition: A numerical simulation of the climate; a model is what scientists use to project change.
entries.definitionCN: 气候的数值模拟；模式是科学家用来预估变化的工具。

entries.definition: The set of measures adopted in response to the issue; the phrase names actions, not the change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为应对该议题而采取的一套措施；它指行动而非变化本身。

entries.definition: A shift in day-to-day conditions; weather changes hourly while climate change lasts decades.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日条件的改变；天气逐时变化，而气候变化持续数十年。

entries.definition: The rise in mean temperature alone; climate change also covers rain, ice, sea level and wind.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指平均气温的上升；climate change 还涵盖雨、冰、海平面与风。

entries.definition: A neutral term for a move from one climate state to another, common in geology and palaeontology.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一种气候状态转到另一种的中性说法，常用于地质学与古生物学。

entries.definition: Change in any earth system, including biodiversity and land use; climate is one component.
entries.definitionCN: 任何地球系统的变化，包括生物多样性与土地利用；气候只是其中一项。

entries.definition: The radiative process that drives part of the change; the effect is a cause, the change is a result.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动部分变化的辐射过程；效应是原因，变化是结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Klima was a slope: the sun's angle gave each zone its weather, and the zone took the name of its weather.
normal.cn: klima 原指斜面：太阳角度给了每个地带天气，而地带便取了天气之名。

normal.en: Change is cambiare 'to exchange', so the phrase says one climate pattern has been exchanged for another.
normal.cn: change 是 cambiare「交换」，因此短语是说一种气候型态被换成了另一种。

normal.en: The family runs climate, climatic, change, changeable, exchange and exchangeable.
normal.cn: 同族词有 climate、climatic、change、changeable、exchange 与 exchangeable。

normal.en: The two policy halves are fixed phrases: climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation.
normal.cn: 政策的两半是固定搭配：气候变化减缓与气候变化适应。

normal.en: In geology the phrase needs no human cause; in the news it almost always implies one.
normal.cn: 在地质学中这个短语不含人为原因；在新闻中它几乎总暗示人为原因。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer's notebook whose rain columns drift year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农人的账簿，雨量那一栏逐年漂移。

abstract.en: Picture a market whose weather changes while the stalls stay in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，摊位没动而天气变了。

abstract.en: Picture a house where the rules slowly change and nobody announces it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子，规矩慢慢改变而无人宣告。

examples.en: Climate change is altering the timing of spring floods in the Alps.
examples.cn: 气候变化正在改变阿尔卑斯山春汛的时间。

examples.en: The course separates natural climate change from the human-driven kind.
examples.cn: 这门课把自然的气候变迁与人为驱动的那一类分开。

examples.en: Adaptation to climate change costs less than rebuilding after each storm.
examples.cn: 适应气候变化的成本低于每场风暴后的重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「climate（气候）+ change（改变）」——气候的型态换了模样 → 气候变化

root: 英语复合词：climate 来自希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」（出自 klinein「倾斜」），经拉丁与法语入英语；change 来自拉丁 cambiare「交换」，其更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pattern being exchanged for another: the statistical shift, the present human case, the geological record, the regional version, the two policy faces, the legal label, and finally any surrounding atmosphere that alters.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「一种型态被换成另一种」展开：统计上的改变，当下的自人为个案，地质记录，地区版本，政策的两个面向，法律标签，最后指任何改变中的周遭氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old rain ledger whose columns no longer match the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧雨量簿，上面的数字已与天色对不上。

branches.en: STATISTICS AT ANY SCALE: a region or a planet can shift its averages.
branches.cn: 任何尺度的统计：一个地区或一颗行星都能改变均值。

branches.en: THE PRESENT CASE: one urgent instance takes over the bare phrase.
branches.cn: 当下的个案：一个紧迫的例子占据了这简洁短语。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: geology reads the same phrase without a human agent.
branches.cn: 深时：地质学用同一短语而不含人为施动者。

branches.en: TWO POLICY FACES: slow the cause, or live with the condition.
branches.cn: 政策的两个面向：减缓原因，或与条件共处。

branches.en: LABEL AND METAPHOR: law fixes the phrase, and ordinary speech borrows it for any altered atmosphere.
branches.cn: 标签与比喻：法律固定这个短语，日常言语借它指任何改变的氛围。

intro.en: Both halves are borrowings that became productive English words, so the compound can be read through either family.
intro.cn: 两半都是借入后成为能产英语词的成分，因此复合词可从任一词族来读。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima yields climate, climatic and acclimatize; Latin cambiare yields change, changeable, exchange and interchange.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 衍生 climate、climatic 与 acclimatize；拉丁 cambiare 衍生 change、changeable、exchange 与 interchange。

items.example: The zone had a mild klima.

items.meaning: the weather typical of a region

items.example: The team acclimatized before the climb.
items.exampleCN: 队伍在登山前适应了气候。

items.meaning: to trade one thing for another

items.example: The two routes interchange at the bridge.

items.meaning: naming the issue before a noun
items.exampleCN: 气候变化政策涵盖两个面向。

latinEntries.structure: cambiare, cambiavi, cambiatum (verb, first conjugation, Late Latin)
clima, climatis (n., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 发展过程；开发流程（事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形或成熟的一连串阶段）
definition_en: the sequence of stages through which something grows, is built, or is brought to a finished form
core_image: 一面长墙上钉着排成一列的图纸，从潦草草图、分解图到能开动的样机，每一格都按着一枚进度图钉
scene: 实验室的长墙上钉着一排图纸，从最初的潦草草图一直排到成型的样机。 The development process moved from a rough sketch to a working prototype in eighteen months.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形的连续阶段」（第 1 个义项：从初步构想到成形的整体推进过程）；句意为这一推进过程在十八个月里从粗草图走到了能运转的原型。可辨识物件：长墙、图纸、进度图钉、样机。

pos.zh: 发展过程；开发流程（可数）

collocations.phrase: the development process of a vaccine

senses.title: Growth from an early to a mature state
senses.titleCN: 从初期到成熟的整体生长过程
senses.definition: the whole sequence by which something grows from an early condition to a mature one
senses.definitionCN: 事物从早期状态走向成熟状态的全过程
senses.example: The development process of a coral reef spans centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的生长过程跨越数百年。
senses.why: development began as the act of unfolding something rolled up, so the word naturally names a thing opening out over time.
senses.whyCN: 发展一词本指把卷起之物摊开，因此天然用来指事物随时间展开。

senses.title: The staged work of making a product
senses.titleCN: 制造产品时按阶段推进的工作
senses.definition: the ordered stages of designing, building and testing a new product before it reaches users
senses.definitionCN: 新产品在交付使用之前，依次经历设计、制造与测试的有序阶段
senses.example: The engineers shortened the development process by testing parts earlier.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提前测试部件，从而缩短了产品开发流程。
senses.why: once industry needed a word for work that unfolds in steps, the older idea of unfolding was applied to factories.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要指称按步骤展开的工作，于是「展开」的旧义被移用到厂房里。

senses.title: The lifecycle of a piece of software
senses.titleCN: 软件从需求到维护的完整生命周期
senses.definition: the cycle of specifying, coding, testing, releasing and maintaining a program
senses.definitionCN: 程序从确定需求、编写代码、测试、发布到维护的循环
senses.example: Their development process includes a review before every release.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开发流程在每次发布前都包含一次评审。
senses.why: software projects made the stages explicit and repeatable, so the phrase became a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 软件项目把各阶段明确化、可重复化，这个短语于是成了技术标签。

senses.title: Structural change in an economy or region
senses.titleCN: 经济或地区长期的结构性变化
senses.definition: the long sequence of changes by which an economy, city or region alters its structure
senses.definitionCN: 经济、城市或地区改变自身结构的长期变化序列
senses.example: Road building was one step in the region's development process.
senses.exampleCN: 修路是这个地区发展过程中的一步。
senses.why: economists borrowed the word because a region is said to grow much as a living thing does.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用了这个词，因为一个地区也被说成像生物那样生长。

senses.title: A child's course of maturing
senses.definition: the course through which a child's body, speech and understanding mature
senses.definitionCN: 儿童的身体、语言与理解力逐步成熟的历程
senses.example: Teachers record each child's development process in a portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用成长档案记录每个孩子的发展过程。
senses.why: psychology kept the biological reading of unfolding and applied it to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学保留了「展开」的生物学含义，并把它用于心智。

senses.title: The steps by which a plan is worked out
senses.titleCN: 计划或协议逐步成形所经过的步骤
senses.definition: the series of talks and revisions through which a plan or agreement takes shape
senses.definitionCN: 计划或协议通过一连串商谈与修改而逐步成形
senses.example: The peace talks were a slow development process with many drafts.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判是一个经过许多草案的缓慢推进过程。
senses.why: the phrase extends the factory image to any piece of work that is built rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把工厂图景扩展到一切需要「做出来」而非「现成得到」的工作。

senses.title: A repeating cycle of drafting and revision
senses.titleCN: 起草、试用、修改的反复循环
senses.definition: a loop in which a draft is tried, criticized and improved until it is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 草稿经过试用、批评与改进直到被接受的循环
senses.example: The handbook went through three rounds of the development process.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册经历了三轮反复修改的流程。
senses.why: modern design treats the process as a loop rather than a line, which the phrase easily accommodates.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把过程看成循环而非直线，这个短语正好容纳这种理解。

senses.title: Building the capacity of an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织逐步建立规则与能力的过程
senses.definition: the staged work of giving an organization the rules, staff and habits it needs to last
senses.definitionCN: 让一个组织获得长期存续所需的规则、人员与习惯的分阶段工作
senses.example: Donors funded the development process of the local health office.
senses.exampleCN: 捐助方资助了当地卫生机构的建设过程。
senses.why: development aid made the word common for institutions, not only for things.
senses.whyCN: 发展援助使这个词不只用于物件，也用于机构建设。

intro.en: Development process joins development, from Old French desveloper 'to unwrap, unfurl', and process, from Latin processus 'a going forward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「发展」与表「过程」的两个名词组合而成：前者出自古法语 desveloper「解开、展开」，后者出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Desveloper meant 'to unwrap, unfurl, disclose'. It was built with a negative prefix plus a verb probably meaning 'to wrap', and that second element is the uncertain part.
items.cn: desveloper 意为「解开、展开、显露」，由否定前缀加一个大概意为「包裹」的动词构成，不确定的正是后一部分。

items.en: Processus 'a going forward, advance' came from procedere, pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go, to yield'.
items.cn: processus「向前行进、推进」出自 procedere，即 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走、让」。

items.en: English took process in the fourteenth century and development in the sixteenth, at first meaning the act of unfolding or disclosing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入「过程」一词，十六世纪借入「发展」一词，后者最初指展开或显露的动作。

items.en: From the nineteenth century development was applied to land, resources and industry, where growth is planned rather than natural.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，「发展」一词被用于土地、资源与工业，那里的成长是被规划的而非自然的。

items.en: The two nouns were joined in the twentieth century, when project management needed a name for work that advances in ordered stages.
items.cn: 两个名词在二十世纪合为一体，当时项目管理需要一个名称来指按有序阶段推进的工作。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-French origin of the 'wrap' element is not established, and any Frankish or Germanic form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「包裹」的成分在法语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的法兰克或日耳曼语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stems that are easily mistaken; group two holds near neighbours that name a sequence without naming growth.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一词干构成、容易看错的词；第二组是语义相近、但只说顺序不说生长的词。

entries.definition: Names growth or the built result; it lacks the explicit step-by-step frame that the full phrase supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 单指生长或建设成果，缺少完整短语所提供的分步框架。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to grow or to build up; the process is what the verb produces over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指生长或逐步建成的动词；过程正是这个动词随时间产生的产物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to development', common in biology and psychology, not a synonym of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与发育有关的」形容词，常用于生物学与心理学，并非该短语的同义词。

entries.definition: Names the person or company that carries out building work, so it is an agent rather than a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施建设的人或公司，是施动者而不是一个序列。

entries.definition: A prescribed order for doing something; it stresses rules, while the phrase stresses growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指办事的规定顺序，强调规则，而该短语强调生长。

entries.definition: The full span from birth or launch to end; it is close but usually names a closed loop.
entries.definitionCN: 指从诞生或推出到终结的全程，意思接近，但通常指闭合循环。

entries.definition: A forward movement through stages, without implying that the thing itself is being built.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐阶段向前推进，不含「事物本身被建造」的意思。

entries.definition: Slow change over a long time, often without a planner; the phrase usually implies deliberate work.
entries.definitionCN: 指长时间内的缓慢变化，常无规划者；该短语通常含有刻意推动之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real nouns sit inside the phrase: one for growth, one for a forward march.
normal.cn: 短语里含两个真实名词：一个表生长，一个表向前推进。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: product development, software development.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：产品开发、软件开发。

normal.en: The family runs develop, developer, developmental, developmentally.
normal.cn: 同族包括「发展」「开发者」「发育的」「在发育方面」。

normal.en: The second noun shares its root with proceed and procedure.
normal.cn: 第二个名词与「继续进行」「程序」共享同一词根。

normal.en: A wall chart with dated pins is the clearest picture of the phrase.
normal.cn: 钉着日期图钉的墙面进度图，是这个短语最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a rolled carpet slowly opened across a floor, room by room.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷地毯在地板上慢慢展开，一个房间接一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that must pass through soil, shoot and leaf before it is a plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子必须经过土、芽、叶，才成为一株植物。

abstract.en: Picture a relay race where each runner may not start before the last hand-off.
abstract.cn: 想象一场接力赛，每一棒都必须等上一棒交完才能起跑。

examples.en: The development process for the new battery took four years and three prototypes.
examples.cn: 新电池的开发过程历时四年，做了三台原型。

examples.en: Reviewers are invited into the development process before the design is frozen.
examples.cn: 评审者会在设计定稿之前被引入开发流程。

examples.en: A region's development process rarely follows a single straight line.
examples.cn: 一个地区的发展过程很少沿着一条直线走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「底外乐普门特」加「破塞斯」——底下外面都乐着进门，一步一步把东西做出来。

root: development 出自古法语 desveloper「展开」，其表「包裹」的成分来源不确定；process 出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」，由 pro-「向前」与 cedere「走」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: something is opened out step by step, and the same shape is then given to products, software, economies, children, plans, repeated drafts and organizations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：某物被一步一步摊开，这个形状随后被赋予产品、软件、经济、儿童、计划、反复草稿与组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart whose dated pins march from a rough sketch to a finished machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张墙面进度图，日期图钉从潦草草图一路排到成型的机器。

branches.en: GROWTH ITSELF: the phrase first names a thing opening out over time, with no factory in sight.
branches.cn: 生长本身：这个短语先指事物随时间展开，画面里还没有工厂。

branches.en: MAKING THINGS: product work and software work turn the sequence into a managed pipeline.
branches.cn: 制造物件：产品工作与软件工作把序列变成可管理的流水线。

branches.en: WHOLE REGIONS: an economy or city is said to grow the way a living body grows.
branches.cn: 整片地区：经济或城市被说成像生物体那样生长。

branches.en: MINDS AND PLANS: a child and a draft both move forward by steps that can be observed.
branches.cn: 心智与计划：孩子与草稿都按可观察的步骤向前。

branches.en: LOOPS AND BODIES: revision repeats the steps, and an organization acquires them as habits.
branches.cn: 循环与机构：修改让步骤重复，而一个组织把步骤沉淀为习惯。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two ordinary English nouns, so its parts can be read through the prefixes and roots that also build a large family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个普通英语名词构成，其各部分可通过同样构成一大族词的前缀与词根来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere 'to go, yield' supplies proceed, procedure and process; the first noun goes back to a French verb whose second element is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cedere「走、让」衍生出「继续进行」「程序」与「过程」；第一个名词则上溯到一个法语动词，其后一成分来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix turns a wrapping action into an unwrapping one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包裹」的动作变成「解开」。

items.example: Its origin is not established, so no older form can be quoted as fact.
items.exampleCN: 其来源未获证明，因此不能把任何更早的形式当作事实引用。

items.example: The team developed the sensor over three winters.
items.exampleCN: 团队用了三个冬天研发出这个传感器。

items.example: Housing development changed the edge of the town.
items.exampleCN: 住宅建设改变了小镇的边缘。

items.meaning: a person or firm that builds
items.example: The developer kept the old trees on the site.
items.exampleCN: 开发商保留了地块上的老树。

items.example: The process takes six working days.
items.exampleCN: 这个流程需要六个工作日。

items.example: Work proceeded in stages after the permit.
items.exampleCN: 拿到许可后，工程分阶段推进。

definition_zh: 熟练的；灵巧的；机敏的
definition_en: clever and skillful, especially in using the hands or the mind
core_image: 一只手在窄口瓶里稳稳夹出一枚硬币，稳、准、不慌
scene: 钟表铺里老师傅戴着放大镜调校游丝，手一点不抖。 The adroit watchmaker fixed the tiny spring in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 adroit 是「熟练的、手艺灵巧的」（第 1 个义项：手艺或动作上的灵巧）；句意为技艺娴熟的钟表匠几秒钟就修好了细小的游丝。

collocations.zh: 一步妙棋；一次机敏的举动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「熟练；机敏」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「熟练地；巧妙地」

senses.title: Skillful with hands or in craft
senses.definition: physically skillful, especially with the hands or in a craft
senses.definitionCN: 手上的或手艺上的灵巧熟练，尤其指动手能力
senses.example: The adroit surgeon sewed the delicate vessel closed.
senses.exampleCN: 技艺娴熟的外科医生把纤细的血管缝合好了。
senses.why: French à droit means 'according to the right hand', and the right hand is the traditional image of manual skill.
senses.whyCN: 法语 à droit 意为「按右手」，右手传统上就是手艺灵巧的象征，所以本义落在手上的功夫。

senses.title: Clever in handling situations
senses.definition: showing cleverness and resourcefulness in dealing with people or problems
senses.definitionCN: 在待人处事上表现出的机智与干练
senses.example: She was adroit at turning hostile questions back on the reporter.
senses.exampleCN: 她很老练，能把记者的刁钻问题原样抛回去。
senses.why: Skill of the hand extends by metaphor to skill of the mind: steering a conversation like steering a tool.
senses.whyCN: 手上的本领经隐喻引申为头脑的本领：像操控工具一样操控局面与谈话。

intro.en: Adroit comes from French adroit, literally 'according to the right', from the phrase à droit.
intro.cn: adroit 来自法语 adroit，字面意思是「按右手」，源自短语 à droit。

items.en: Latin directus meant 'straight, right, set upright', the past participle of dirigere, 'to set straight'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 directus 意为「直的、正的」，是动词 dirigere（摆正）的过去分词。

items.en: Old French droit meant 'right, straight', later also 'the right hand'.
items.cn: 古法语 droit 意为「正、直」，后来也指「右手」。

items.en: The phrase à droit, 'by the right (hand)', became the adjective adroit.
items.cn: 短语 à droit（用右手）凝固成形容词 adroit。

items.en: English borrowed adroit first for manual dexterity, then for mental quickness.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 adroit，先指手上的灵巧，再引申为头脑的机敏。

items.en: Today adroit covers both physical deftness and tactical cleverness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 adroit 同时涵盖手脚利索与手腕高明两重意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar sound or same Latin family; the second gathers near synonyms of skillfulness.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写发音相近或同属拉丁词族的词；第二组收表示「熟练、灵巧」的近义词。

entries.definition: Skillful with the hands; from Latin dexter, 'right hand', a parallel image not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灵巧的」；来自拉丁语 dexter（右手），意象相同但词源不同，并非同源。

entries.definition: To decorate; only the spelling is close, the root has nothing to do with adroit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装饰」；只是拼写与 adroit 相近，词源毫无关系。

entries.definition: From Latin directus, the same participle that gave adroit its droit element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「直接的；指挥」；与 adroit 共享拉丁语 directus 这一来源。

entries.definition: Quick and neat in movement, usually on a small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灵巧的、麻利的」，多指小动作上的利落。

entries.definition: Highly skilled through practice, often in a field of expertise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内行的、擅长的」，强调经练习达到的专精。

entries.definition: Shrewd and careful in dealing with practical matters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精明的、谨慎的」，偏重处世的算计。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the right-hand root and the craftsman scene; the abstract hooks picture steady hands and quick minds.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「右手」词根与匠人场景；抽象记忆点想象稳的手与快的脑。

normal.en: French à droit literally means 'to the right (hand)'.
normal.cn: 法语 à droit 字面是「往右手」.

normal.en: The right hand is the old symbol of skill.
normal.cn: 右手自古是灵巧的象征。

normal.en: Adroit and direct share Latin directus.
normal.cn: adroit 与 direct 同享拉丁语 directus。

normal.en: The adverb adroitly marks a clever move.
normal.cn: 副词 adroitly 标记一次机敏的行动。

normal.en: The noun adroitness names the quality itself.
normal.cn: 名词 adroitness 指这份灵巧本身。

abstract.en: Picture fingers lifting a coin from a narrow bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象手指从窄瓶里稳稳夹出一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a debater turning the question around like a tool.
abstract.cn: 想象辩手把问题像工具一样转了个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a right hand leading, the left following.
abstract.cn: 想象右手引路、左手跟随。

examples.en: The adroit watchmaker fixed the tiny spring in seconds.
examples.cn: 技艺娴熟的钟表匠几秒钟就修好了细小的游丝。

examples.en: An adroit reply saved the interview from disaster.
examples.cn: 一句机敏的回答把访谈从尴尬里救了回来。

examples.en: She is adroit at defusing arguments with humor.
examples.cn: 她擅长用幽默化解争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额准」——额头上写着「准」字，手稳心细，出手就是又快又准的熟练。

root: 拉丁语 dirigere（摆正）→ directus（直的、正的）→ 古法语 droit（正、右手）→ 法语短语 à droit（用右手）；核心义是「像用惯用的右手那样顺手」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from skill of the hands to cleverness in handling people and situations.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从手上的灵巧，走到待人接物上的机敏老练。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady right hand that never fumbles
core.cn: 核心意象：一只从不失手的右手

branches.en: The hand that works neatly and fast.
branches.cn: 干得又利落又快的那双手。

branches.en: The mind that steers talk like a tool.
branches.cn: 像使工具一样驾驭谈话的头脑。

branches.en: Both senses mean doing the right thing with ease.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指轻松做对事情。

branches.en: Politics rewards the adroit above the honest.
branches.cn: 政治场上老练比老实更吃香。

branches.en: Surgeons and watchmakers typify this sense.
branches.cn: 外科医生与钟表匠是这个义项的典型。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin right-root direct/droit with the French phrase frame à, and the family gives direct and dirge-free relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「正、直」词根 direct/droit 与法语短语框 à，同族词还有 direct。

latinIntro.en: Latin directus and dirigere are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 directus 与 dirigere 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 波动；起伏；变动；来回变化
definition_en: to rise and fall or change irregularly in level, amount, or quality
core_image: 水面一起一伏的波浪线
scene: 菜市场的价格牌早晚各换一次，蔬菜筐旁的箭头一上一下。 Because of supply and demand, vegetable prices fluctuated a lot this week, and the labels changed morning and evening.
sceneCN: 这里 fluctuate 是「上下波动、起伏不定」（第 1 个义项：价格不规则地涨落）；句意：受供需影响，这周蔬菜价格波动很大，标价早晚都在变。

collocations.zh: 在 A 与 B 之间来回变动

derivatives.zh: 波动的；起伏的（医学中也指可移动的）

senses.title: Prices rise and fall
senses.definition: of prices or values, to go up and down repeatedly and irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或价值反复而不规则地涨落
senses.example: Oil prices fluctuated all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天油价都在波动。
senses.why: Latin fluctuare is 'to move in waves', from fluctus 'a wave'. A price that rises and falls draws the same up-and-down line as a wave.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fluctuare 意为“像波浪一样运动”，来自 fluctus“波浪”。涨落的价格画出的正是波浪一样的上下曲线。

senses.title: Levels vary over time
senses.definition: of a level such as temperature or water, to keep changing within a range
senses.definitionCN: 指温度、水位等水平在一定范围内持续变化
senses.example: The lake level fluctuates with the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面水位随季节起伏。
senses.why: Water is the literal source of the image, so a level that rises and falls is the most natural application of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 水是这个意象的字面来源，因此水位的升降是这个动词最自然的用法。

senses.title: Numbers swing
senses.definition: of figures such as rates or sales, to change repeatedly in either direction
senses.definitionCN: 指利率、销量等数字反复朝两个方向变化
senses.example: Sales fluctuate from month to month.
senses.exampleCN: 销量逐月波动。
senses.why: A rate or a sales figure is plotted as a line, and a line that keeps swinging looks like a wave.
senses.whyCN: 利率或销量被画成一条线，反复摆动的线看起来就像波浪。

senses.title: Quality or attendance varies
senses.titleCN: 质量或出勤率时好时坏
senses.definition: of a non-numeric quality, to be uneven from one time or case to another
senses.definitionCN: 指非数字性的质量在不同时间或情形下不均衡
senses.example: The quality of the meals fluctuates.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜的质量时好时坏。
senses.why: Anything measured on a scale can be plotted as a wave, even when the scale is subjective, like quality or turnout.
senses.whyCN: 任何按尺度衡量的东西都能画成波浪，即使尺度是主观的，如质量或出席人数。

senses.title: Opinions and moods shift
senses.definition: of feelings or opinions, to change back and forth
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或意见来回改变
senses.example: Public opinion fluctuated during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 竞选期间公众意见摇摆不定。
senses.why: The wave image moves from water to the mind: feelings rise and fall without settling at one level.
senses.whyCN: 波浪意象从水面移向心智：情绪起起伏伏，不停在某一水平。

senses.title: Fluctuate between two states
senses.definition: to move repeatedly from one condition to another, as in 'fluctuate between hope and fear'
senses.definitionCN: 反复从一种状态转到另一种，如“在希望与恐惧之间摇摆”
senses.example: He fluctuated between hope and despair.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与绝望之间摇摆。
senses.why: A wave has a crest and a trough; to fluctuate between two things is to keep moving from one extreme to the other.
senses.whyCN: 波浪有波峰和波谷；在两者之间 fluctuate，就是在两个极端之间不断移动。

senses.title: Move like a wave
senses.definition: in literary or technical use, to move in a wavelike way
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或技术用法中，像波浪一样运动
senses.example: The surface of the pool fluctuated in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 池面在风中起伏。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense, now rarer in English but still present in technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的物理义项，现代英语中较少见，但仍存在于技术写作中。

senses.title: Economic activity varies
senses.definition: of an economy, currency, or market, to expand and contract irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指经济、货币或市场不规则地扩张与收缩
senses.example: The currency fluctuated against the dollar.
senses.exampleCN: 该货币对美元的汇率起伏不定。
senses.why: Markets are described as waves in economics, so the verb naturally covers currencies and activity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把市场描述为波浪，因此这个动词自然覆盖货币与经济活动。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb built on fluctus 'a wave', from fluere 'to flow'. The etymology is clear and the 'wave' image is the key to every sense.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus“波浪”之上的拉丁动词，来自 fluere“流动”。词源清楚，“波浪”意象是理解所有义项的关键。

items.en: First recorded in English, from Latin fluctuatus, past participle of fluctuare 'to undulate, move in waves'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 17 世纪 30 年代，来自拉丁语 fluctuatus，即 fluctuare“起伏、像波浪般运动”的过去分词。

items.en: Fluctuare is from fluctus 'a wave, billow, surge, a flowing', which comes from the past-participle stem of fluere 'to flow'.
items.cn: fluctuare 来自 fluctus“波浪、巨浪、涌动、流动”，后者来自 fluere“流动”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Fluere comes from an extended form of PIE *bhleu- 'to swell, well up, overflow', itself an extension of *bhel- (2) 'to blow, swell'.
items.cn: fluere 来自原始印欧语 *bhleu-“膨胀、涌起、溢出”的扩展形式，后者又是 *bhel-（第 2 义）“吹、膨胀”的扩展。

items.en: The same root gives fluent, fluid, flux, influence, influx, superfluous and mellifluous; all carry the image of flowing.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、influx、superfluous、mellifluous；它们都带着“流动”的意象。

items.en: The verb extends from water to prices, rates, moods, currencies and economies. The noun fluctuation keeps the wave image explicit.
items.cn: 这个动词从水面延伸到价格、比率、情绪、货币和经济。名词 fluctuation 保留了明确的波浪意象。

note.en: Look-alikes share the flowing root; near meanings differ in whether the movement is up and down, back and forth, or simply changing.
note.cn: 形近词共享“流动”词根；近义词的区别在于运动是上下、来回，还是单纯变化。

entries.definition: an instance of rising and falling. It is fluctuate + -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 一次起伏、波动。它是 fluctuate + -ion。

entries.definition: flowing easily, especially of speech. It shares fluere 'to flow' but has nothing to do with rising and falling.
entries.definitionCN: 流畅的，尤指言语。它共享 fluere“流动”，但与上下起伏无关。

entries.definition: a substance that flows; also 'changeable'. The adjective sense overlaps with fluctuating but does not imply repeated rise and fall.
entries.definitionCN: 流体；也指“易变的”。其形容词义与 fluctuating 重叠，但不含反复升降之意。

entries.definition: continuous change; also a flow or discharge. It names the flow itself rather than the up-and-down movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不断变化；也指流动或通量。它指流动本身，而不是上下运动。

entries.definition: to change or differ. It is broader and does not require a repeated up-and-down pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；不同。它更宽泛，不要求反复上下波动。

entries.definition: to swing regularly between two points. It is more mechanical and regular than fluctuate.
entries.definitionCN: 在两点之间规律摆动。它比 fluctuate 更机械、更规则。

entries.definition: to be uncertain or unsteady, especially in opinion. It stresses hesitation, while fluctuate stresses changing level.
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决；动摇，尤指意见。它强调迟疑，而 fluctuate 强调水平变化。

entries.definition: to move back and forth in a wide arc. It is more physical and usually larger than a fluctuation.
entries.definitionCN: 大幅度来回摆动。它更物理，幅度通常比 fluctuation 大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real fluere / fluctus wave image and the real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 fluere / fluctus 波浪意象和相关词。

normal.en: fluctus means 'wave': anything that rises and falls like water fluctuates.
normal.cn: fluctus 意为“波浪”：任何像水一样起落的东西都在 fluctuate。

normal.en: Fluent, fluid, flux and fluctuate all come from fluere 'to flow'; the wave is the shape the flow makes.
normal.cn: fluent、fluid、flux、fluctuate 都来自 fluere“流动”；波浪是流动形成的形状。

normal.en: Fluctuation is the noun: a price chart with peaks and troughs shows fluctuation.
normal.cn: fluctuation 是名词：有峰有谷的价格图显示的就是波动。

normal.en: Fluctuate between hope and fear is to move from one crest to the other without settling.
normal.cn: 在希望与恐惧之间 fluctuate，就是从一个波峰移到另一个波峰，始终不停定。

normal.en: A fluctuating demand curve is one that will not stay flat.
normal.cn: fluctuating demand 就是无法保持平直的需求曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a cork on water: it rises, falls, rises again, never resting at one height. That cork is fluctuating.
abstract.cn: 想象水面上的软木塞：升起、落下、再升起，从不停在一个高度。这个软木塞就在 fluctuate。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line that looks like a wave: every peak and trough is one fluctuation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条像波浪的图表线：每个峰和谷都是一次 fluctuation。

abstract.en: Picture a mood that lifts and drops with the day: feelings fluctuate like weather.
abstract.cn: 想象随一天起落的情绪：心情像天气一样 fluctuate。

examples.en: Demand for the product fluctuates with the seasons.
examples.cn: 该产品的需求随季节波动。

examples.en: Her weight fluctuated by only two kilos.
examples.cn: 她的体重只在两公斤内波动。

examples.en: The exchange rate has fluctuated sharply since the announcement.
examples.cn: 自公告以来汇率剧烈波动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “弗拉克图埃特”——弗拉克图像波浪一样上上下下 → fluctuate 波动、起伏

root: 拉丁 fluere“流动”→ fluctus“波浪”→ fluctuare“像波浪般起伏”，核心是“上下波动”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fluctuate all keep the shape of a wave: something rises, falls, and rises again without settling. Prices, water, numbers, moods and markets can all draw that line.
sensesIntro.cn: fluctuate 的八个义项都保留波浪的形状：某物升起、落下、再升起，始终不定。价格、水位、数字、情绪和市场都能画出这条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave line that goes up and down and never stays flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上下起伏、始终不平的波浪线。

branches.en: MARKETS AND NUMBERS: prices, rates, sales and currencies are plotted as lines that swing.
branches.cn: 市场与数字：价格、比率、销量和货币被画成摆动的线。

branches.en: MEASURED LEVELS: water, temperature, quality and attendance all move within a range.
branches.cn: 可测水平：水位、温度、质量和出勤率都在一定范围内变动。

branches.en: INNER LIFE: opinions and moods rise and fall without any number attached.
branches.cn: 内心：意见与情绪的起落，并不附着于任何数字。

branches.en: LITERAL WAVE: the original physical movement of a water surface.
branches.cn: 字面波浪：水面原本的物理运动。

branches.en: BETWEEN TWO POLES: the crest and trough of one wave become hope and fear, or one policy and another.
branches.cn: 两极之间：一个波浪的峰与谷变成希望与恐惧，或两种政策。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb in -ate built on fluctus. English adds -ion, -ing, -ant, -al and -ly, but the root does the work.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus 上的拉丁 -ate 动词。英语加 -ion、-ing、-ant、-al、-ly，但主要靠词根表义。

latinIntro.en: The fluere family is large: fluctus 'wave', fluere 'flow', fluvius 'river', fluentum 'stream'. English has fluent, fluid, flux, influence and superfluous from the same source.
latinIntro.cn: fluere 词族庞大：fluctus“波浪”、fluere“流动”、fluvius“河流”、fluentum“水流”。英语的 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、superfluous 同出一源。

items.meaning: to move in waves; to rise and fall
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（fluctus“波浪”+ -ate 动词后缀）

items.meaning: a rise and fall; an irregular change
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Small fluctuations in temperature are normal.
items.exampleCN: 温度的小幅波动是正常的。

items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏不定的（-ing 构成形容词）
items.example: A fluctuating supply makes planning hard.
items.exampleCN: 供给波动让规划变得困难。

items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏的（-ant 构成形容词，医学中也指可移动的）
items.example: The fluctuant mass shifted under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 那个可移动的肿块在按压下移位。

items.meaning: caused by or relating to fluctuation
items.meaningCN: 波动引起的；涨落性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Fluctuational noise is hard to filter.

items.meaningCN: 波动地；起伏不定地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The signal fluctuatedly dropped and rose.
items.exampleCN: 信号起伏不定地下降又上升。

items.example: She is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能流利地说三种语言。

items.meaning: a substance that flows; able to change

items.meaningCN: 不断变化；流动；通量（拉丁 fluxus“流动”）
items.example: The system is in a state of flux.
items.exampleCN: 这个系统处于不断变化之中。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 流动；流泻；奔流（fluctuate 的最终词根）
波浪；巨浪；涌动（英语 fluctuate 的直接来源）
起伏；像波浪般运动（英语 fluctuate 的直接拉丁动词）
河流；溪流（同根词，英语 fluvial 的来源）

definition_zh: 位移；取代；流离失所；排水量；（心理）置换；（引擎）排量
definition_en: the act of moving something from its place, the amount moved, or the replacement of one thing by another
core_image: 把一本书从书架的固定位置抽走，留下一个空的缺口，旁边的人把另一本书塞了进去
scene: 书架上，管理员抽走一本书，留下空位，又把另一本放进同一格： the displacement of one volume by another。
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 displacement 是「移走、取代」（第 1、2 个义项：离开原位与取代）；句意：一本被移走，另一本占了它的位置。图中可辨识物件：书架、空出的格位、两本书、梯凳。

pos.zh: 位移；取代；流离失所；排水量；置换

derivatives.zh: 放置；安置（同词根，方向相反）

senses.title: Moving something out of its place
senses.definition: the act of moving an object from the position it occupied
senses.definitionCN: 把物体从其占据的位置移开的行为
senses.example: The displacement of the statue required a crane.
senses.exampleCN: 移动这座雕像需要起重机。
senses.why: Dis- removes and place holds the position. Displacement is the undoing of placement: what was set here is now somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: dis- 表示移走，place 表示位置。displacement 是对 placement 的撤销：原本安放在此的东西现在在别处。

senses.title: Taking someone's role or place
senses.definition: the replacement of one person or thing by another that takes over its function
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或事物被另一个接管其功能的替换
senses.example: The displacement of hand tools by machines changed the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 机器对手工工具的取代改变了作坊。
senses.why: Here the thing moved is not the object but the occupant. One occupant is pushed out and another takes the slot, so the word describes replacement through eviction.
senses.whyCN: 这里被移走的不是物体，而是占据者。一个占据者被挤出，另一个占了格子，因此这个词描述的是“通过逐出实现的替换”。

senses.title: A change of position in physics
senses.definition: in physics, the vector distance and direction from an initial to a final position
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中从初始位置到末位置的距离与方向矢量
senses.example: The displacement is zero when the runner returns to the start.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者回到起点时位移为零。
senses.why: Physics separates distance travelled from displacement achieved. The word measures where you ended relative to where you began, not how far you walked.
senses.whyCN: 物理学区分走过的距离与达成的位移。这个词衡量的是你相对起点落在哪里，而不是你走了多远。

senses.title: Water pushed aside by a body
senses.definition: the volume or weight of fluid moved out of the way by a floating or submerged object
senses.definitionCN: 浮体或浸没物体排开的流体体积或重量
senses.example: The ship has a displacement of forty thousand tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船的排水量为四万吨。
senses.why: An object cannot enter water without water leaving. Displacement names that forced removal, and Archimedes turned it into a measure of the object.
senses.whyCN: 物体进入水中，水必然离开。displacement 命名这种被迫的移走，阿基米德把它变成对物体的度量。

senses.title: Redirecting a feeling onto a safer target
senses.definition: in psychoanalysis, the transfer of an emotion from its original object to a substitute
senses.definitionCN: 精神分析中把情感从原对象转移到替代对象
senses.example: Anger at the boss found displacement onto a colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 对上司的怒气被置换到同事身上。
senses.why: The feeling is moved out of its proper place and lodged somewhere else. The word keeps its spatial sense while the thing displaced becomes an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 情感被移离其应在的位置，安放到别处。这个词在空间义不变的情况下，被移动的东西变成了情感。

senses.title: Language about what is not here
senses.definition: in linguistics, the capacity of language to refer to things absent in time or space
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中语言指称时间或空间中不在场之物的能力
senses.example: Displacement lets a speaker discuss last winter in June.
senses.exampleCN: 位移性让说话者在六月谈论去年冬天。
senses.why: Words travel away from the here and now. This sense treats the whole language system as the thing displaced from its immediate setting.
senses.whyCN: 词语离开此时此地。这个义项把整个语言系统看作从当下情境中被移走的东西。

senses.title: Rock moved along a fault
senses.definition: in geology, the relative movement of rock on either side of a fault
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中断层两侧岩石的相对移动
senses.example: The fault shows a displacement of several metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这条断层显示出数米的位移。
senses.why: The ground itself has been moved out of place. The sense is literal: two blocks that once matched no longer line up.
senses.whyCN: 地面本身被移离了原位。这个义项是字面的：原本对得上的两块岩石不再对齐。

senses.title: One element pushing another out
senses.definition: in chemistry, a reaction in which one element displaces another from a compound
senses.definitionCN: 化学中一种元素把另一种元素从化合物中置换出来
senses.example: Zinc displacement of copper turns the solution colourless.
senses.exampleCN: 锌置换铜使溶液褪色。
senses.why: An atom is evicted from its place in a molecule by a more reactive rival. The competition for a position is the same image as sense 02.
senses.whyCN: 一个原子被更具反应性的对手从分子中的位置挤出。为位置而竞争，与第 2 义项是同一个意象。

senses.title: The swept volume of an engine
senses.definition: the total volume swept by the pistons of an engine in one complete cycle
senses.definitionCN: 发动机活塞在一个完整循环中扫过的总体积
senses.example: A larger displacement gives more torque but uses more fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的排量带来更大扭矩，但更费油。
senses.why: Each piston pushes air out of the space it occupies, exactly as a body pushes water aside. Engine displacement is the same measure applied to cylinders.
senses.whyCN: 每个活塞把它占据的空间里的空气推出去，正如物体排开水。发动机排量就是把同一度量用在气缸上。

intro.en: Displacement is displace plus -ment. Place goes back to Latin platea, 'broad street', from Greek plateia, from platys 'broad'. Displace means to remove from a place, and the noun names that removal and its measure.
intro.cn: displacement 是 displace 加 -ment。place 上溯拉丁 platea“宽阔的街道”，再上溯希腊 plateia，词根 platys“宽阔”。displace 意为移离某处，名词命名这种移离及其度量。

items.en: Platys meant 'broad, flat'. The feminine plateia named a broad way or square. The same root gives plate, plateau and platypus, literally 'flat-foot'.
items.cn: platys 意为“宽阔、扁平”。阴性形式 plateia 指宽路或广场。同一词根给出 plate、plateau，以及字面为“扁足”的 platypus。

items.en: Latin platea took the Greek word for a broad street. It was used for open squares in Roman towns and passed into the everyday speech of the provinces.
items.cn: 拉丁 platea 借入这个表示宽街的希腊词。它用于罗马城镇的广场，并进入各行省的日常口语。

items.en: Old French place meant 'open space, position'. English borrowed it twice: once through French, once directly from Latin in learned words such as plaza.
items.cn: 古法语 place 意为“开阔空间、位置”。英语两次借用：一次经法语，一次在 plaza 等学术词中直接借自拉丁。

items.en: English place settles as 'a particular position or locality'. The verb to place, 'to put in a position', follows, and with it the noun placement.
items.cn: 英语 place 稳定为“特定位置或地点”。动词 to place“安置”随之而来，名词 placement 也一并出现。

items.en: Displace is formed with dis- to mean 'remove from its place, put out of office'. The nautical sense of a ship's displacement appears in the 18th century.
items.cn: displace 由 dis- 构成，意为“移离原位、撤职”。船舶排水量的航海义在 18 世纪出现。

items.en: Physics fixes displacement as a vector; geology and chemistry adopt the term; psychoanalysis borrows it for a defence mechanism in the early 20th century.
items.cn: 物理学把 displacement 固定为矢量；地质学与化学采用该词；精神分析在 20 世纪初借它指一种防御机制。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective of people and the noun of putting in place. The meaning group contrasts displacement with replacement, migration and substitution.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、描述人的形容词与“安放”名词；词义组把 displacement 与替换、迁徙、代替区分开。

entries.definition: to move out of place, or to take over the role of. The noun adds -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 移离原位，或取代某物的角色。名词加 -ment。

entries.definition: forced to leave home or position. It describes the people affected, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 被迫离开家园或职位的。它描述受影响的人，而非过程。

entries.definition: the act of putting someone or something in a position. Displacement undoes it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到某位置的行为。displacement 撤销它。

entries.definition: the act of putting something new in the place of another. It stresses the newcomer; displacement stresses the one pushed out.
entries.definitionCN: 把新物放到另一物位置的行为。它强调新来者，displacement 强调被挤出者。

entries.definition: movement from one region to another, often seasonal or voluntary. Displacement usually implies compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个地区到另一个地区的移动，常为季节性或自愿。displacement 通常含被迫之意。

entries.definition: the legal removal of a tenant from property. It is one concrete mechanism of displacement.
entries.definitionCN: 依法把租户从房产中逐出。它是 displacement 的一种具体机制。

entries.definition: the use of one thing in place of another. It is neutral about whether anyone was pushed out.
entries.definitionCN: 用一物代替另一物。它对是否有人被挤出保持中立。

entries.definition: a turning aside from a straight path. It describes a change of direction, while displacement describes a change of position.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离直线路径。它描述方向改变，而 displacement 描述位置改变。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold the image of a vacated slot, then apply it to objects, people, water, feelings and atoms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩抓住“空出的格子”这个意象，再把它用到物体、人、水、情感与原子上。

normal.en: See dis- + place: the thing is taken out of its place.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 place：东西被拿出原位。

normal.en: Picture the empty shelf slot, then someone else filling it. That is replacement by displacement.
normal.cn: 想象书架上空出的格位，随后被别人填上。这就是通过移走实现的替换。

normal.en: In physics, ask only two questions: where did it start, where did it end?
normal.cn: 物理方面只问两个问题：从哪开始，在哪结束？

normal.en: For ships, the hull cannot enter without water leaving. That leaving water is the displacement.
normal.cn: 船方面，船体进不去水不出去。离开的那些水就是排水量。

normal.en: For psychology, the feeling is moved to a safer chair in the room.
normal.cn: 心理学方面，情感被挪到房间里更安全的一把椅子上。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one operation: something occupies a slot, then does not.
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个操作：某物占据一个格子，然后不再占据。

abstract.en: Notice the double edge: displacement is both a move and a loss of position.
abstract.cn: 注意它的双刃：displacement 既是移动，也是失去位置。

abstract.en: Ask of each use: is the thing moved, or is the thing taking its place the focus?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：焦点是被移走的东西，还是接替它的那个？

examples.en: The war caused the displacement of millions of people.
examples.cn: 战争造成数百万人流离失所。

examples.en: Measure the displacement of the trolley from its starting mark.
examples.cn: 测量小车相对起始标记的位移。

examples.en: Automation has displaced many routine jobs.
examples.cn: 自动化取代了许多常规工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯普雷斯门特”：地斯普雷斯（displace）的门被移走了，门一移、位置一空，就是位移与取代。

root: 希腊语 platys“宽阔”，阴性 plateia 指宽路；拉丁 platea“宽街、广场”；经古法语 place 进入英语作 place“位置”，加 dis- 构成 displace“移离原位”，再加 -ment 构成 displacement。同根词有 place、plate、plateau、plaza。

sensesIntro.en: Displacement is the negative of placement: something that was put here is no longer here. The thing removed can be an object, an occupant, a body of water, an emotion, a reference in time, a block of rock, an atom or a volume of air. In each case the word measures the same event, a slot that is now occupied differently or left empty.
sensesIntro.cn: displacement 是 placement 的反面：原本放在这里的东西不再在这里。被移走的可以是物体、占据者、一团水、一种情感、一个时间指称、一块岩石、一个原子或一团空气。每一种情况下，这个词衡量的都是同一件事：一个格子如今被别样占据，或空了出来。

core.en: A vacated slot: what was in place is moved or replaced.
core.cn: 空出的格子：本在位的东西被移走或替换。

branches.en: SPACE: objects moved, vectors measured, rock offset along a fault.
branches.cn: 空间：物体被移、矢量被量、岩石沿断层错动。

branches.en: COMPETITION: an occupant evicted by a rival, in work or in chemistry.
branches.cn: 竞争：占据者被对手挤出，在职场或在化学中。

branches.en: VOLUME: water pushed aside, air swept by pistons.
branches.cn: 体积：被推开的水，被活塞扫过的空气。

branches.en: MIND: a feeling lodged on a substitute target.
branches.cn: 心理：情感被安放到替代目标上。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: words referring beyond the here and now.
branches.cn: 语言：词语指称此时此地之外。

intro.en: Displacement is dis- plus place plus -ment. The items show both directions of the place family: placement puts in, displacement takes out, replacement puts back.
intro.cn: displacement 是 dis- 加 place 再加 -ment。下列条目展示 place 词族的两个方向：placement 放进去，displacement 拿出来，replacement 放回去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and Greek entries show that place was originally a broad street, not an abstract point. The word still carries that sense of an open space someone can occupy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁与希腊语条目说明 place 原本是一条宽街，而不是抽象的点。这个词仍带着“可供占据的开阔空间”之意。

items.meaning: the act or amount of moving out of place
items.example: The displacement of the population was sudden.

items.meaning: to move out of position; to supplant
items.example: The new system displaced the old one.

items.meaning: forced out of home or position
items.meaningCN: 被迫离开家园或职位的
items.exampleCN: 援助送到了流离失所的家庭。

items.meaning: the act of putting in position
items.example: The placement of the sign was poor.
items.exampleCN: 这块牌子的位置放得不好。

items.meaning: to put back; to take the place of
to put in the wrong place; to lose temporarily

items.structure: Old French plate, from Latin platea

items.meaning: a flat raised area of land
items.example: The herd grazed on the plateau.
The market fills the plaza on Sundays.

definition_zh: 复制；重复实验；复现研究；复制品；自我复制
definition_en: the act of copying something, or of repeating an experiment to see whether the result holds
core_image: 一只模具压出两件相同的零件，旁边一张卡片记着两次相同的测量值
scene: 工作台上摆着一只模具和两件刚压出的零件，检验员用卡尺量过两件，把同样的读数记在卡片上。 The replication failed to confirm the original result, so the team repeated the whole procedure.
sceneCN: 这里指为验证原结果而重复整项研究或实验（第 1 个义项：重复实验以检验原结果是否成立）；句意为这次重复未能确认原结果，于是团队又把整套步骤重做了一遍。图中可辨识物件：模具、两件零件、卡尺、记录卡。

pos.zh: 复制；重复实验；复现研究；复制品

senses.title: Repeating a study to test it
senses.definition: the act of repeating an experiment or study to see whether its result holds
senses.definitionCN: 重复一项实验或研究，以检验其结果是否成立
senses.example: The replication failed to confirm the original result, so the team repeated the whole procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 这次重复未能确认原结果，于是团队又把整套步骤重做了一遍。
senses.why: Replicare meant to fold back, and a replication folds the same procedure back onto itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为折回，而一次重复就是把同一套步骤折回到自己身上。

senses.title: Copying in general
senses.definition: the act of making something that matches an original
senses.definitionCN: 制造与原件相符之物的行为
senses.example: Careful replication of the method is easier when the protocol is public.
senses.exampleCN: 当研究方案公开时，仔细复制这套方法会更容易。
senses.why: The general sense is older than the scientific one: any copy is a folding back of the original.
senses.whyCN: 一般义比科学义更早：任何复制品都是原件的折回。

senses.title: A copy of an object
senses.definition: an object made to look like another object
senses.definitionCN: 造得与另一件物件相像的物品
senses.example: The museum displayed a replication of the ancient vase.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了那只古代花瓶的复制品。
senses.why: Museums need a word for a stand-in that is honest about being a copy.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆需要一个词来指一个坦承自己是复制品的替身。

senses.title: Copying inside a living cell
senses.definition: the process by which genetic material or a cell makes a copy of itself
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质或细胞制造自身副本的过程
senses.example: Cell replication is the process by which one cell becomes two.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞复制就是一个细胞变成两个的过程。
senses.why: Biology uses the word for a molecule folding out a copy of itself.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个词指分子展开出一个自身副本。

senses.title: A duplicate legal document
senses.definition: a copy of a document kept for legal or official use
senses.definitionCN: 为法律或官方用途保存的文件副本
senses.example: The lawyer kept a replication of the signed deed.
senses.exampleCN: 律师保存了一份已签署契据的副本。
senses.why: Law has long needed exact copies, and the word covers the paper as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 法律早就需要精确副本，这个词既指行为也指那张纸。

senses.title: Copying data across systems
senses.definition: the process of keeping an identical copy of data on another system
senses.definitionCN: 在另一个系统上保存同一份数据的过程
senses.example: Data replication keeps a second copy on another server.
senses.exampleCN: 数据复制在另一台服务器上保留第二份副本。
senses.why: Computing borrows the biological and legal idea of an exact second copy.
senses.whyCN: 计算借用了生物与法律里「精确第二份」的想法。

senses.title: A published repeat study
senses.definition: a study published specifically to repeat and check an earlier study
senses.definitionCN: 专门为重复并核对早先研究而发表的论文
senses.example: The journal published a replication of the famous experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家期刊发表了那项著名实验的重复研究。
senses.why: The scientific sense became a genre of paper, and the word names the genre.
senses.whyCN: 科学义变成了一种论文类型，这个词也就命名这一类型。

senses.title: Reproducing an image layer
senses.titleCN: 图像或版画的复制过程
senses.definition: the process of reproducing an image, colour layer or print from an original
senses.definitionCN: 从原件复制图像、色层或版画的过程
senses.example: The printmaker checked the replication of each colour layer.
senses.exampleCN: 版画家检查了每一层颜色的复制效果。
senses.why: Printmaking made replication a craft, with each layer folded back onto the sheet.
senses.whyCN: 版画使复制成为一门手艺，每一层都折回到纸上。

intro.en: Replication comes from Latin replicatio, a folding back, from replicare, re- back plus plicare to fold. The source is clear; the date of its first English record is uncertain, and the scientific sense is much later.
intro.cn: 这个词源自拉丁 replicatio「折回」，来自 replicare（前缀意为「回」加词根意为「折」）。词源清楚，最早英语记录的年代不确定，科学义出现得晚得多。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and it gives the physical picture inside replication.
items.cn: plicare 意为折，提供这个词内部的身体画面。

items.en: Replicare joined re- back to plicare, meaning to fold back or turn over.
items.cn: replicare 把意为「回」的前缀加到 plicare 上，意为折回、翻转。

items.en: Replicatio named a folding back; in later Latin it also served as a term in replies and legal answers.
items.cn: replicatio 命名「折回」；在后来的拉丁语里也用于答复与法律答辩。

items.en: French replication carried the word into English, where it first meant a reply or a copy.
items.cn: 法语 replication 把词带进英语，最初指答复或副本。

items.en: English replication is recorded with copying and answering senses; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语里这个词的复制义与答复义都有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century science made replication the standard name for repeating a study, and biology gave it the sense of self-copying.
items.cn: 二十世纪科学使这个词成为重复研究的标准说法，生物学又赋予它自我复制的义项。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like replication; the second names nearby acts of copying or repeating.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是附近表示复制或重复的说法。

entries.definition: The verb for copying or repeating.
entries.definitionCN: 复制或重复的动词。

entries.definition: Able to be copied or repeated.
entries.definitionCN: 可被复制或重复的。

entries.definition: The quality of being replicable.
entries.definitionCN: 可复制或可重复的性质。

entries.definition: A copy of an object, often made to look exact.
entries.definitionCN: 物件的复制品，常做得外观精确。

entries.definition: Something that copies itself, or a person who replicates.
entries.definitionCN: 自我复制之物，或进行复制的人。

entries.definition: The broader word for producing a copy or offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 产生副本或后代的更宽说法。

entries.definition: Doing the same thing again, without necessarily copying an original.
entries.definitionCN: 再做一遍同样的事，不必然复制原件。

entries.definition: The act of making an exact second copy.
entries.definitionCN: 制造精确第二份副本的行为。

entries.definition: A reproduction of an original, or the act of making one.
entries.definitionCN: 原件的复制品，或复制的行为。

entries.definition: A study run again to check an earlier one.
entries.definitionCN: 为核对早先研究而再做一次的研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real folding source, the real copy senses and real scientific terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「折」来源、真实的复制义与真实科学术语。

normal.en: Replication comes from replicare, to fold back: a copy is the original folded over itself.
normal.cn: replication 来自 replicare「折回」：复制品就是原件折回到自己身上。

normal.en: The same word covers a museum copy, a cell copying itself and a second experiment.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖博物馆复制品、细胞自我复制与第二次实验。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include replication study, replication crisis and data replication.
normal.cn: 固定说法有重复研究、复现危机与数据复制。

normal.en: A replication is not the same as a reproduction: the first repeats a study, the second produces a copy.
normal.cn: 重复研究与复制并不相同：前者重做研究，后者产出副本。

normal.en: Science made replication a genre of paper, not just an act.
normal.cn: 科学使重复研究成为一种论文类型，而不只是一个动作。

abstract.en: Replication is the second voice that asks whether the first voice told the truth.
abstract.cn: 重复研究是第二个声音，问第一个声音有没有说真话。

abstract.en: A copy can be exact and still prove nothing about the original's claim.
abstract.cn: 复制品可以很精确，却仍证明不了原结果的结论。

abstract.en: The fold is the picture: the same path taken again, back onto itself.
abstract.cn: 「折」就是画面：同一条路再走一次，折回到自身。

examples.en: The replication used a larger sample than the original.
examples.cn: 这次重复研究用了比原研究更大的样本。

examples.en: A failed replication is information, not an insult.
examples.cn: 一次失败的重复是信息，不是侮辱。

examples.en: The lab keeps a replication of every signed record.
examples.cn: 实验室保存每一份已签记录的副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来复利一份」——把原样再折回来一份：复制

root: 这个词源自拉丁 replicatio「折回」，来自 replicare（前缀意为「回」加词根意为「折」），经法语进入英语；原义与答复、折回相关，后发展出复制与重复义。生物自我复制义与科学研究复现义为近现代专门化；词源清楚，最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one fold: a repeated study, copying in general, a museum copy, a cell copying itself, a legal duplicate, data mirroring, a published repeat study, and the copying of an image layer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个「折」：重复研究、一般复制、博物馆复制品、细胞自我复制、法律副本、数据镜像、公开发表的重复研究，以及图像色层的复制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one mould presses out two identical parts, and a card records the same measurement twice.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只模具压出两件相同的零件，一张卡片记下两次相同的测量。

branches.en: THE SECOND STUDY: repeating a procedure, and publishing the repeat as a study.
branches.cn: 第二次研究：重复一套步骤，并把这次重复作为论文发表。

branches.en: THE ACT OF COPYING: any copy made by hand or by a printing layer.
branches.cn: 复制的动作：靠手或靠印版色层做出的任何副本。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL DUPLICATE: a museum vase and a signed deed both have stand-ins.
branches.cn: 实物副本：博物馆花瓶与已签契据都有替身。

branches.en: THE CELL: genetic material folds out a copy of itself.
branches.cn: 细胞：遗传物质展开出一个自身副本。

branches.en: THE SERVER: an identical second copy of data lives on another machine.
branches.cn: 服务器：同一份数据的第二副本活在另一台机器上。

intro.en: Replication is a Latin noun built on re- plus plicare, with the abstract ending -atio.
intro.cn: replication 是拉丁名词，建立在 re- 加 plicare 上，并用抽象后缀 -atio。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare, replicare and replicatio supply the word, and -atio became English -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare、replicare 与 replicatio 提供这个词，-atio 变成英语 -ation。

items.example: The verb gives the physical picture of folding.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出「折」的身体画面。

items.example: The prefix turns folding into folding back.
The verb supplies the act behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
The suffix builds replication, duplication and creation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示「复制」「加倍」「创造」的三个名词。

items.example: The noun names the copy itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名复制品本身。
这个形容词标出可能性。

definition_zh: 界面；接口；接触面；相互作用；连接
definition_en: a surface or point where two things meet, or the means by which a user or system communicates with another
core_image: 两块不同的材料在一条清晰的分界线上贴合，一侧是金属，一侧是液体，交界处微微泛起反应的光
scene: 设计师把按钮、搜索框和图标排在一屏之内，用户手指一点就能完成操作。 A clear interface makes the software feel simple.
sceneCN: 这里指用户与软件之间交互的屏幕层（第 1 个义项：人机界面）；句意：清晰的界面让软件用起来很简单。

pos.zh: 界面；接口；接触面；相互作用

derivatives.zh: 由该名词加表示「属于」的形容词尾构成，义为「界面的、界面上的」
由该动词加动作词尾构成，义为「对接；对接的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已对接的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在界面层面」

senses.title: The screen between user and machine
senses.titleCN: 用户与机器之间的屏幕层
senses.definition: the part of a system that a person sees and operates, such as buttons, menus and windows
senses.definitionCN: 系统中被人看见并操作的部分，如按钮、菜单与窗口
senses.example: The interface puts the search box at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个界面把搜索框放在页面顶部。
senses.why: The word names the meeting surface, and in software that surface is what the user touches.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名相接的表面，在软件中那个表面就是用户所触的部分。

senses.title: The point where two systems join
senses.definition: a standard connection through which one system or component talks to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个系统或组件与另一个对话时所依据的标准连接
senses.example: The two programs share a narrow interface.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个程序共用一个窄接口。
senses.why: Two systems meet at a defined boundary, and the standards at that boundary are called the interface.
senses.whyCN: 两个系统在一条明确的边界相接，边界上的标准就称为接口。

senses.title: The boundary between two materials
senses.titleCN: 两种材料之间的分界面
senses.definition: the surface where two substances or phases meet
senses.definitionCN: 两种物质或物相相接的表面
senses.example: Water and oil form a sharp interface.
senses.exampleCN: 水与油形成清晰的界面。
senses.why: In physics the word keeps its literal sense: a surface where one phase ends and another begins.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学中这个词保留字面义：一种物相结束、另一种开始的表面。

senses.title: The joint between two parts
senses.titleCN: 两个部件之间的接合处
senses.definition: the place where two machine parts or structures meet and act on each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个机械部件或结构相接并相互作用的位置
senses.example: Engineers checked the interface for wear.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了接合处是否磨损。
senses.why: Machines also have meeting surfaces where force is transferred, so the word extends to mechanical joints.
senses.whyCN: 机器同样有传递力的相接表面，因此这个词扩展到机械接合处。

senses.title: The channel of interaction
senses.definition: the means by which two parties or fields interact and exchange influence
senses.definitionCN: 两方或两个领域相互作用、交换影响的方式
senses.example: The conference became an interface between research and industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这场会议成了研究与产业之间的交流通道。
senses.why: If two worlds meet, the meeting surface can be social or institutional, not only physical.
senses.whyCN: 若两个世界相遇，相接的表面可以是社会的或机构的，而不只是物理的。

senses.title: The agreed protocol
senses.definition: a documented set of rules that lets independently built systems work together
senses.definitionCN: 一套成文规则，使独立构建的系统能够协同工作
senses.example: The interface is published so other teams can build on it.
senses.exampleCN: 接口规范已公布，其他团队可以据此开发。
senses.why: A boundary needs rules if both sides are built separately, and the rules themselves take the name.
senses.whyCN: 若两侧分别构建，边界就需要规则，而这些规则本身也沿用这个名称。

senses.title: The graphical front end
senses.definition: a visual interface built from windows, icons and pointers rather than typed commands
senses.definitionCN: 由窗口、图标与指针构成、而非键入命令的视觉界面
senses.example: The graphical interface replaced the command line for most users.
senses.exampleCN: 对多数用户而言，图形界面取代了命令行。
senses.why: Drawing rather than typing changes the meeting surface, so the graphical kind gets its own label.
senses.whyCN: 用画而不是打字改变了相接的表面，因此图形化的那一类有了自己的标签。

senses.title: To join two systems
senses.titleCN: 作为动词：使两系统对接
senses.definition: to connect one system or device to another so that they can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把一个系统或设备接到另一个上，使它们协同工作
senses.example: The clinic interface the new records system with the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把新的病历系统与旧系统对接起来。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to create such a meeting surface, a common shift in technical English.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词转为动词，意为建立这样一个相接表面，这是技术英语中常见的转类。

intro.en: Interface is Latin inter, between, plus English face from Latin facies, a form or surface; the computing sense is twentieth-century.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「在……之间」与英语「面」（源自拉丁语「外形、表面」）构成；计算机义项是二十世纪的。

items.en: Inter meant between, and it marks the word as naming something that lies between two sides.
items.cn: 这个词素意为「在……之间」，标记该词命名位于两侧之间的东西。

items.en: Facies meant form, appearance or surface, and it is the source of English face.
items.cn: 这个词意为外形、外观或表面，是英语「面」的来源。

items.en: The noun was coined for the surface where two bodies or phases meet, a sense still used in chemistry and physics.
items.cn: 这个名词最初指两个物体或物相相接的表面，这一义项至今仍用于化学与物理。

items.en: In the 1960s the word was applied to the boundary between hardware and software, and then to what a user sees.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代，这个词被用于硬件与软件的边界，随后又指用户所看到的部分。

items.en: Engineers turned the noun into a verb meaning to connect systems at such a boundary.
items.cn: 工程师把这个名词转为动词，意为在这样的边界上连接系统。

items.en: The first use of the computing sense is often dated to the 1960s, but the exact paper and author are not settled.
items.cn: 计算机义项的首见常被定在二十世纪六十年代，但确切文献与作者尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the face or boundary idea; the second group names other meeting points between systems.
note.cn: 第一组共享「面」或「边界」的概念；第二组是系统之间其他类型的相接点。

entries.definition: Relating to a boundary between phases; it describes the surface rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 与物相之间的边界有关的；描述该表面，而不是命名它。

entries.definition: The outer face of a body; the target word adds the idea of lying between two bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 物体的外表面；目标词加上「位于两物之间」的意思。

entries.definition: The front or outer side; it is the English descendant of the Latin word inside interface.
entries.definitionCN: 正面或外侧；是目标词内部那个拉丁词的英语后裔。

entries.definition: The act of joining systems; it names the process rather than the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 把系统连接起来的动作；命名过程而不是边界。

entries.definition: A line that separates two regions; it is wider and does not imply interaction.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两个区域的界线；范围更宽，且不暗示相互作用。

entries.definition: A point that admits traffic into another network; a functional kind of interface.
entries.definitionCN: 让流量进入另一网络的入口；是一种功能性的接口。

entries.definition: A single page that gathers access to many services; it is a user-facing entry point, not a boundary standard.
entries.definitionCN: 汇集多种服务入口的单一页面；是面向用户的入口，而非边界标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Latin pieces and the modern technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实拉丁成分与现代技术搭配。

normal.en: Inter means between and face means surface: the surface between two sides.
normal.cn: 「之间」加「面」，就是两侧之间的那个面。

normal.en: The family runs interface, interfacial, interfacing and interfaced.
normal.cn: 同族词有界面、界面的、对接与已对接的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the user side: user interface and graphical user interface.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用户一侧：用户界面与图形用户界面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system side: application programming interface, interface design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出系统一侧：应用程序编程接口、界面设计。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the oldest sense: the sharp line where water meets oil.
normal.cn: 化学保留了最古老的义项：水与油相接的那条清晰界线。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that belongs to neither room but serves both.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，不属于任何一个房间，却为两边服务。

abstract.en: Picture two languages agreeing on a single hand signal at a border.
abstract.cn: 想象两种语言在边境约定同一个手势。

abstract.en: Picture a membrane through which two liquids exchange a single colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一层薄膜，两种液体隔着它交换一种颜色。

examples.en: The interface hides the complexity of the database behind simple buttons.
examples.cn: 界面用简单的按钮把数据库的复杂性藏了起来。

examples.en: A well-documented interface lets two teams work independently.
examples.cn: 一个有良好文档的接口让两个团队可以独立工作。

examples.en: The study examined the interface between climate and agriculture.
examples.cn: 这项研究考察了气候与农业之间的相互作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特面」——互联网之间的那个面 → 界面、接口

root: 拉丁语「在……之间」加拉丁语「外形、表面」；十九世纪末指两物的交界面。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a meeting surface: user screen, system boundary, material boundary, mechanical joint, channel of interaction, agreed protocol, graphical front end, and the verb of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指一个相接表面：用户屏幕、系统边界、材料分界、机械接合、交流通道、约定规范、图形前端，以及表示连接的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear line where two different sides touch and exchange something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条清晰的界线，两侧不同的事物在此相触并交换某物。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE MEETING SURFACE: what a user sees, including the graphical version built from windows and icons.
branches.cn: 可见的相接表面：用户所见的部分，包括由窗口与图标构成的图形版本。

branches.en: THE RULED BOUNDARY: the standard connection and the documented rules that let separate systems work together.
branches.cn: 有规则的边界：标准连接与成文规则，使彼此独立的系统协同工作。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BOUNDARY: where two materials or machine parts meet.
branches.cn: 物理边界：两种材料或机械部件相接之处。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL CHANNEL: a meeting surface between fields, institutions or groups.
branches.cn: 社会通道：领域、机构或群体之间的相接表面。

branches.en: THE ACT OF JOINING: turning the meeting surface into a working connection.
branches.cn: 连接的动作：把相接表面变成可工作的连接。

intro.en: Interface is a hybrid of a Latin prefix and an English noun of Latin origin; both parts still build words.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀与源自拉丁语的英语名词的混合体；两部分至今都在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix inter and the noun facies behind face, so real cognates appear in the list.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了前缀「之间」与「面」背后的名词，因此列表中列出真实同族词。

items.example: The prefix places the surface between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该表面放在两侧之间。

items.example: The second half supplies the surface in the image.
items.exampleCN: 后半提供了画面中的那个表面。

items.example: The Latin noun stands behind the English face.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语「面」的来源。

items.example: The noun first named a physical boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指物理边界。

items.example: Interfacial describes what happens at the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 「界面的」描述边界上发生的事。

items.example: Interfacing is the work of making systems talk.
The interfaced modules share one clock.
items.exampleCN: 已对接的模块共享一个时钟。

items.meaning: the outer face of a body
items.example: Surface is the everyday word for one side of the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 「表面」是边界一侧的日常说法。

derivatives.zh: 由该名词加表示「属于」的形容词尾构成，义为「界面的、界面上的」
由该动词加动作词尾构成，义为「对接；对接的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已对接的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在界面层面」

definition_zh: 酸性的；酸味的；尖刻的；酸绿的
definition_en: having the properties of an acid, tasting sour, or sharply critical in tone
core_image: 舌尖被柠檬刺了一下，金属表面冒出细密气泡
scene: 实验台上，一片石灰石被滴上醋，表面冒出细密气泡，试纸转成红色。 Vinegar on limestone bubbles and turns the paper red, and the cut lemon beside it is acidic too.
sceneCN: 这里 acidic 是「酸性的」（第 1 个义项：具有酸的化学性质）；句意：醋滴在石灰石上起泡、试纸变红，旁边切开的柠檬也是酸性的。图中可辨识物件：石灰石、滴管、气泡、pH 试纸、柠檬。

senses.title: Having the chemistry of an acid
senses.definition: in chemistry, having a pH below 7 and able to react with a base
senses.definitionCN: 化学中指 pH 低于 7，能与碱反应
senses.example: The solution turned acidic after the gas was added.
senses.exampleCN: 通入气体后，溶液变成酸性。
senses.why: Acid comes from Latin acidus 'sour', from acere 'to be sour'. Chemistry keeps the taste word but replaces the tongue with a scale: acidic now means a pH reading, not a sensation.
senses.whyCN: acid 来自拉丁语 acidus“酸的”，再上溯 acere“发酸”。化学保留了味觉词，却用刻度取代了舌头：acidic 现在指 pH 读数，而不是感觉。

senses.title: Sour to the taste
senses.definition: having a sharp sour taste, like lemon or vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 具有尖锐的酸味，如柠檬或醋
senses.example: The unripe fruit is too acidic to eat raw.
senses.exampleCN: 未熟的果实太酸，不能生吃。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: acidus is literally 'sour'. Before chemistry, the word named what the mouth does when it tightens, and the suffix -ic simply makes the quality an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：acidus 字面就是“酸的”。在化学之前，这个词命名的是嘴收紧时的反应，而后缀 -ic 只是把这个性质变成形容词。

senses.title: Corrosive or etching
senses.definition: able to dissolve metal, stone, or other material through chemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 能通过化学反应溶解金属、石头或其他材料
senses.example: Acidic cleaners can damage marble surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 酸性清洁剂会损伤大理石表面。
senses.why: Sourness and corrosion are the same chemical power seen at two scales: the tongue feels it, the stone gives way. The adjective extends from taste to damage because acids remove material.
senses.whyCN: 酸味与腐蚀是同一种化学力量在两个尺度上的表现：舌头感觉到它，石头则为它让路。形容词从味觉扩展到破坏，因为酸会移走材料。

senses.title: Sharp in tone
senses.definition: of speech or writing, sharply critical and biting
senses.definitionCN: 指言辞尖锐批评、带刺
senses.example: Her acidic review of the novel spared nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这部小说的尖刻评论毫不留情。
senses.why: A sour taste makes the face contract; a sour remark makes the listener contract. The metaphor is old and physical: acidity in the mouth becomes acidity in the voice.
senses.whyCN: 酸味让脸皱起来；酸话让听者皱眉。这个比喻古老而身体化：嘴里的酸变成声音里的酸。

senses.title: Low-pH soil
senses.definition: of soil, having a low pH that affects which plants can grow
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤 pH 偏低，影响可生长的植物种类
senses.example: Blueberries grow best in acidic soil.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝莓在酸性土壤中长得最好。
senses.why: Agriculture turns the chemical scale into a land quality. Acidic soil is not merely sour; it is a habitat with a restricted list of possible crops, so the word becomes agronomic.
senses.whyCN: 农业把化学刻度变成土地品质。酸性土壤不只是“酸”，它是一种只容许有限作物生存的生境，因此这个词成了农学词。

senses.title: Acid deposition in the environment
senses.definition: of rain, fog, or deposition, containing acids formed from pollution
senses.definitionCN: 指雨、雾或沉降物含有污染形成的酸
senses.example: Acidic rain slowly leached nutrients from the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 酸性雨水慢慢淋失了林地养分。
senses.why: Environmental science compounds the adjective with weather. The phrase keeps the chemical sense but adds a source: pollution turns ordinary rain into an acidic agent that works over decades.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这个形容词与天气组合。这个短语保留化学义，又加上来源：污染把普通雨水变成一种以数十年为尺度起作用的酸性介质。

senses.title: Acid-forming in the body
senses.definition: of food or metabolism, tending to produce acid rather than alkaline conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指食物或代谢倾向产生酸，而非碱性环境
senses.example: High-protein diets are described as acidic.
senses.exampleCN: 高蛋白饮食被描述为偏酸性。
senses.why: Nutrition uses the adjective for a net effect rather than a taste: a food can be alkaline in the mouth and acidic after metabolism. The word now measures a process, not a flavour.
senses.whyCN: 营养学用这个形容词表示净效应，而不是味道：一种食物入口可以是碱性，代谢后却偏酸。这个词此时衡量过程，而不是风味。

senses.title: A bright, synthetic colour
senses.definition: of a colour, unnaturally bright and sharp, especially a vivid green or yellow
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色不自然地鲜亮刺眼，尤指鲜绿或鲜黄
senses.example: The poster used an acidic green that hurt the eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 海报用了一种刺眼的酸绿，看得眼睛发痛。
senses.why: Twentieth-century colour writing borrows the mouth's reaction for the eye's: an acidic shade is one that seems to sting. The metaphor is synaesthetic, but it keeps the original 'sharp' core.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的色彩写作把嘴的反应借给眼睛：酸色就是看起来会刺人的颜色。这个比喻是通感的，但仍保留最原始的“尖锐”核心。

intro.en: Acidic is a derived adjective: acid plus the Latin suffix -ic. Acid goes back to Latin acidus 'sour', from acere 'to be sour', and the deeper root is the PIE word for 'sharp'.
intro.cn: acidic 是派生形容词：acid 加拉丁后缀 -ic。acid 上溯拉丁语 acidus“酸的”，来自 acere“发酸”，更深的词根是原始印欧语中表示“尖锐”的词。

items.en: Acidus 'sour, tart' comes from acere 'to be sour, to be sharp'. The same family gives acer 'sharp' and acies 'edge'.
items.cn: acidus“酸的、尖酸的”来自 acere“发酸、尖锐”。同一词族还给出 acer“尖锐的”与 acies“刃”。

items.en: The root is generally reconstructed as PIE *ak- 'sharp, pointed', seen in Latin acer and Greek akis 'point'. The asterisk marks a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 其词根一般重构为原始印欧语 *ak-“尖锐、带尖”，见于拉丁语 acer 与希腊语 akis“尖”。星号表示重构形式。

items.en: The suffix -ic comes from Latin -icus and Greek -ikos, meaning 'pertaining to'. It turns the noun acid into an adjective describing its quality.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 来自拉丁语 -icus 与希腊语 -ikos，意为“与……有关的”。它把名词 acid 变成描述其性质的形容词。

items.en: Chemistry adopts acid for the class of sour substances, and acidic appears for the quality. The taste sense is now backed by reactions and, later, by pH.
items.cn: 17 世纪，化学用 acid 指一类酸味物质，acidic 则指其性质。味觉义此时有了反应作为依据，后来又有 pH。

items.en: The adjective spreads to soil, rain, metabolism, and finally to colour and tone. Each extension keeps the 'sharp, biting' core rather than the laboratory definition.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到土壤、雨水、代谢，最后到颜色与语气。每次扩展保留的都是“尖锐、刺人”的核心，而不是实验室定义。

note.en: The first group shares the acid- shape or the same 'sharp' root; the second compares words for sour and biting qualities.
note.cn: 第一组共享 acid- 外形或同一“尖锐”词根；第二组比较表示“酸与尖刻”的词。

entries.definition: a sour chemical substance. It is the noun behind acidic and names the class.
entries.definitionCN: 一种酸味化学物质。它是 acidic 背后的名词，命名这一类物质。

entries.definition: the degree of acid strength. It is the abstract noun of the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 酸的程度。它是同一形容词的抽象名词。

entries.definition: sharp, severe, or sudden. It comes from the same 'sharp' root but describes severity, not sourness.
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐的、严重的或急性的。它来自同一“尖锐”词根，但描述严重程度，而非酸味。

entries.definition: bitter or pungent in smell or taste. It shares the sharp root but stresses a harsh, stinging quality.
entries.definitionCN: 气味或味道苦涩刺鼻。它共享尖锐词根，但强调刺人的 harsh 感。

entries.definition: having a tart taste, or turned bad. It is the everyday taste word, while acidic is technical or literary.
