entries.definitionCN: 有酸味，或变坏。它是日常味觉词，而 acidic 更技术化或文学化。

entries.definition: pleasantly sharp in taste. It is milder and often approving, unlike acidic which can imply damage.
entries.definitionCN: 味道清爽地酸。它更温和，常带赞许，而 acidic 可暗示损害。

entries.definition: able to eat away material. It stresses the destructive effect, while acidic names the chemical quality.
entries.definitionCN: 能侵蚀材料。它强调破坏效果，而 acidic 命名化学性质。

entries.definition: sharply critical or cold. It is used of wind and remarks, while acidic often keeps a flavour metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 尖刻批评或寒冷刺骨。它用于风与言语，而 acidic 常保留味道比喻。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the 'sharp' root and the pH scale, then three abstract images about a quality that stings.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕“尖锐”词根与 pH 刻度的挂钩，再用三个关于“会刺人的性质”的抽象画面。

normal.en: acid, acute, acrid all share 'sharp': acid is sharp on the tongue, acute is sharp in severity, acrid is sharp in the nose.
normal.cn: acid、acute、acrid 都共享“尖锐”：acid 尖在舌上，acute 尖在程度上，acrid 尖在鼻子里。

normal.en: -ic means 'pertaining to': acidic is simply 'of the nature of acid'.
normal.cn: -ic 意为“与……有关”：acidic 就是“具有酸的性质”。

normal.en: pH below 7 is the modern definition; the tongue's contraction is the old one.
normal.cn: pH 低于 7 是现代定义；舌头皱起是古老定义。

normal.en: Acidic soil is a chemical fact that becomes a farming constraint.
normal.cn: 酸性土壤是一个化学事实，随后变成农业限制。

normal.en: An acidic remark and an acidic green both sting, one the ear and one the eye.
normal.cn: 尖刻的话与刺眼的酸绿都会刺人，一个刺耳，一个刺眼。

abstract.en: Acidity is a scale, but the word never quite forgets the face it makes.
abstract.cn: 酸性是一个刻度，但这个词从未完全忘记它让人做出的表情。

abstract.en: The same property that flavours food can dissolve stone: intensity is a matter of dose.
abstract.cn: 给食物调味的同一性质也能溶解石头：强度只是剂量问题。

abstract.en: Borrowing a taste word for a tone shows how quickly the body becomes a metaphor.
abstract.cn: 把味觉词借给语气，说明身体多快就变成了比喻。

examples.en: The lake became acidic after decades of industrial fallout.
examples.cn: 经过数十年工业沉降，湖水变酸了。

examples.en: Add lime to acidic soil before planting.
examples.cn: 种植前要在酸性土壤中加石灰。

examples.en: His acidic wit made even his targets laugh.
examples.cn: 他尖刻的机智连被他调侃的人都笑了。

dict_mnemonic.note: acid（酸）+ -ic（形容词）→ 酸性的。词根 ac- 是“尖锐”：酸在舌上尖，酸话在耳里尖。
dict_mnemonic.text: acid（酸）+ -ic（与……有关的）→ 有酸的性质 → 酸性的、酸味的、尖刻的

root: 拉丁 acidus“酸的”＝acere“发酸、尖锐”（原始印欧语 *ak-“尖锐”）→ 英语 acid + 拉丁-希腊后缀 -ic → acidic。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the pH scale, then return to the tongue, move to corrosion, to a biting tone, to soil and rain, to metabolism, and finally to a colour that seems to sting the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从 pH 刻度开始，回到舌头，再转到腐蚀、尖刻语气、土壤与雨水、代谢，最后落到一种似乎会刺眼的颜色。

core.en: A drop of vinegar on limestone, the surface hissing into foam
core.cn: 一滴醋落在石灰石上，表面嘶嘶起泡

branches.en: THE SCALE: a pH reading below seven.
branches.cn: 刻度：pH 读数低于七。

branches.en: Damage at two scales: a cleaner eating marble, and rain eating a forest floor.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的损害：清洁剂侵蚀大理石，雨水侵蚀林地。

branches.en: Synaesthetic bite: a sour remark and a sour green.
branches.cn: 通感的刺：酸话与酸绿。

branches.en: Acidity as a condition: soil that limits crops, and a diet that shifts the body's balance.
branches.cn: 作为条件的酸性：限制作物的土壤，与改变身体平衡的饮食。

branches.en: THE TONGUE: sourness is chemistry’s first blow to taste.
branches.cn: 舌头：酸味是化学打给味觉的第一记。

intro.en: Acidic's family is built on acid: the abstract noun of degree, the verb and process of making acid, and the negative form.
intro.cn: acidic 的词族建立在 acid 上：程度抽象名词、使酸化的动词与过程，以及否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin acidus 'sour' plus the suffix -icus gives the adjective pattern behind acidic. The same 'sharp' root produces acer, acute, and acrid, so the family is wider than the chemistry lab.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acidus“酸的”加后缀 -icus 给出 acidic 背后的形容词模式。同一个“尖锐”词根还产生 acer、acute、acrid，因此这个词族比化学实验室更广。

items.exampleCN: 酿酒师会仔细测量酸度。

items.example: Use a nonacidic cleaner on stone.
items.exampleCN: 石材上要用非酸性清洁剂。

latinEntries.example: Acidus is the source of acid.
latinEntries.exampleCN: acidus 是 acid 的来源。
acere 连接 acid 与 acute。

latinEntries.example: Acer is behind acrid and acerbic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: acer 是 acrid 与 acerbic 背后的词。

definition_zh: 粗鲁的；唐突的；生硬无礼的
definition_en: abrupt and offhand in speech or manner, to the point of being rude
core_image: 一句话没说完就把门关上
scene: 柜台后的老店员头也不抬，答话只有两个字。 His brusque reply made the customer feel unwelcome.
sceneCN: 这里 brusque 是「生硬无礼的、唐突的」（第 1 个义项：言谈举止 abrupt 且近乎无礼）；句意是他生硬的回话让顾客觉得不受欢迎。

pos.zh: 粗鲁的；唐突的；生硬无礼的

collocations.phrase: brusque to the point of rudeness

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「粗鲁地，唐突地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「粗鲁，生硬」
借自法语，义为「粗鲁的举止」

senses.title: Abrupt and rude in manner
senses.definition: speaking or behaving in a curt, blunt way that seems rude
senses.definitionCN: 言谈举止简短生硬，显得粗鲁无礼
senses.example: The doctor was brusque but thorough.
senses.exampleCN: 医生态度生硬，检查却很仔细。
senses.why: The French source means brushwood-like, rough; rough manner reads as curtness.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义近于「如灌木丛般毛糙」，毛糙的做派读起来就是简慢无礼。

senses.title: Offhand in speech
senses.definition: giving short, ungracious answers without warmth or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 回答简短冷淡，不带温度也不作解释
senses.example: Her brusque "no comment" ended the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她生硬的一句「无可奉告」结束了采访。
senses.why: When words are trimmed to the bone, the missing courtesies themselves offend.
senses.whyCN: 话语被削到只剩骨头，缺失的客套本身就成了冒犯，义项由举止落到言语。

senses.title: Bluntly dismissive
senses.titleCN: 断然打发的，不容分说的
senses.definition: curtly rejecting a request or person without ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 干脆利落地回绝请求或冷落来人，不讲情面
senses.example: He gave the proposal a brusque brush-off.
senses.exampleCN: 他把提案一口回绝，毫不客气。
senses.why: Curtness pushed further becomes dismissal: the door closes before the sentence ends.
senses.whyCN: 简慢再进一步便是不容分说的打发，话没说完门已关上，义项继续加深。

intro.en: Brusque came into English from French brusque, which probably traces to an Italian word for brushwood.
intro.cn: brusque 经由法语 brusque 进入英语，一般追溯到意大利语中表示「柴薪、毛糙」的词。

items.en: brusco meant rough, sharp-tasting; older forms pointed to brussa, brushwood prepared for dyeing.
items.cn: 意大利语 brusco 义为粗砺、涩口；更早形式 brussa 指用于染色的荆柴。

items.en: brusque took the meaning brisk and rough in manner, said of wine, then of people.
items.cn: 法语 brusque 先形容气味冲、性子急，继而形容人粗鲁唐突。

items.en: brusque entered English with the sense of blunt, forbidding manner.
items.cn: 十七世纪 brusque 进入英语，表示生硬冷峻的态度。

items.en: derivatives brusquely and brusqueness settled beside the adjective.
items.cn: 派生词 brusquely、brusqueness 随形容词定型。

items.en: brusque now labels any curtness that shades into rudeness.
items.cn: 如今 brusque 泛指一切近乎无礼的简慢生硬。

note.en: Brusque resembles French borrowings of roughness and sits beside a row of curtness words.
note.cn: brusque 与一批源自法语的「粗砺」词形近，并置身一排表简慢的近义词之间。

entries.definition: an alternative spelling of brusque
entries.definitionCN: brusque 的异体拼法

entries.definition: Italian source word meaning rough
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语源词，义为粗砺，brusque 的前身

entries.definition: the quality of being brusque
entries.definitionCN: brusque 的名词形式，粗鲁生硬

entries.definition: an implement with bristles; a skirmish
entries.definitionCN: 刷子；小冲突，只是拼形相近，词源不同

entries.definition: rudely brief in speech
entries.definitionCN: （言辞）简短失礼的

entries.definition: plain and direct to the point of rudeness
entries.definitionCN: 直截了当到近乎冒犯的

entries.definition: sudden and unpleasantly terse
entries.definitionCN: 突兀而生硬的

entries.definition: rough and surly in voice or manner
entries.definitionCN: （嗓音、态度）粗鲁冷淡的

entries.definition: casual without thought or courtesy
entries.definitionCN: 随口敷衍的，漫不经心的

normalIntro.en: Hear the French flavor: a brusque man speaks in one brusk syllable.
normalIntro.cn: 听出法语腔：粗鲁人说话只有一个生硬音节。

normal.en: Brusque ends like the French words casque and masque.
normal.cn: brusque 的结尾同法语词 casque、masque 一个路数。

normal.en: The silent -que hides the sound /k/.
normal.cn: 不发音的 -que 藏着 /k/ 音。

normal.en: The variant spelling brusk says the sound out loud.
normal.cn: 异体拼法 brusk 把音直接写出来。

normal.en: Root image: brushwood, prickly and rough to touch.
normal.cn: 词根意象：荆柴，扎手而毛糙。

normal.en: Pair it with curt: both cut words short.
normal.cn: 与 curt 对记：两者都把话剪短。

abstract.en: Feel a door shut on your half-finished sentence.
abstract.cn: 感受半句话被一扇门硬生生截断。

abstract.en: See a hand wave you away without a glance.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手头也不抬地把你挥开。

abstract.en: Hear three clipped words where a paragraph should be.
abstract.cn: 本该一段话的地方只落下三个硬邦邦的词。

examples.en: His brusque phone manner scared off new clients.
examples.cn: 他接电话时生硬的态度吓跑了不少新客户。

examples.en: Behind the brusque exterior, she was kind to interns.
examples.cn: 生硬的外表之下，她对实习生其实很和善。

examples.en: The waiter apologized for the brusque service.
examples.cn: 侍者为粗鲁的服务道了歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不汝客」——他说话「不」把「汝」当「客」待，三言两语就把人打发，粗鲁唐突。

root: brusque 一般认为借自法语 brusque（毛糙、唐突），更早上溯意大利语 brusco（粗砺、涩口），其源或为 brussa（染料用荆柴），与「刷子」一族的日耳曼借词相关；词形属法语系统，非拉丁古典词。

sensesIntro.en: A rough, brushwood manner reads first as curtness, then as graceless speech, and finally as outright dismissal.
sensesIntro.cn: 如荆柴般毛糙的做派，先读作简慢，再落到生硬的言语，最终成为毫不客气的打发。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closing on a half-spoken sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门在半句话上砰然关上。

branches.en: a brusque headmaster
branches.cn: 态度生硬的校长

branches.en: a brusque phone manner
branches.cn: 接电话时的简慢语气

branches.en: a brusque written reply
branches.cn: 措辞生硬的书面答复

branches.en: a brusque brush-off
branches.cn: 毫不客气的回绝

branches.en: brusque treatment of visitors
branches.cn: 对来访者的冷遇

intro.en: Brusque is a whole-word borrowing; its shape is French, its core Italian.
intro.cn: brusque 是整词借入：词形属法语，词核出自意大利语。

latinIntro.en: No classical Latin root exists; the trail runs through medieval trade Italian.
latinIntro.cn: 并无古典拉丁词根可循，词迹经由中世纪意大利商贸语汇。

items.meaning: plain to the point of rudeness

latinEntries.meaningCN: 缩短的，残缺的（curt 之源）

definition_zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的；知觉心理学的；与概念相对的；视觉感知的；言语感知的；知觉障碍的；知觉阶段的
definition_en: relating to perception, to the way the senses take in and organize information, as opposed to abstract reasoning or conceptual thought
core_image: 地图的绘制方式本身，而不是地图上写着的那些地名
scene: 同一张格子图，有人先看见整体轮廓，有人先数清小方块。 One sees the whole shape first, the other counts the squares: this is a perceptual difference.
sceneCN: 这里 perceptual 是「知觉层面的」（第 1 个义项：与感官如何接收并组织信息有关）；句意：有人先看见整体轮廓、有人先数清小方块，这是知觉层面的差异。

pos.zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Of the perceiving process
senses.definition: relating to perception as a process, especially how sensory information is received, selected, and organized
senses.definitionCN: 与知觉这一过程有关，尤指感官信息如何被接收、筛选与组织
senses.example: Perceptual processing begins before conscious attention arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉加工在有意识的注意到来之前就开始了。
senses.why: Percept- is the thing taken in, and -ual (Latin -alis) means 'belonging to'. Perceptual therefore names the belonging: not the object seen, but the way it is taken in.
senses.whyCN: percept- 是被拿进来之物，-ual（拉丁 -alis）意为“属于……的”。所以 perceptual 命名的是这种归属：不是被看见的对象，而是看见它的方式。

senses.title: Of the senses rather than the mind
senses.definition: relating to sensory experience as distinct from reasoning, memory, or abstract thought
senses.definitionCN: 与感官经验有关，以区别于推理、记忆或抽象思维
senses.example: The task measured perceptual speed, not verbal reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务测量的是知觉速度，而不是言语推理。
senses.why: The word draws a line down the mind: on one side sit the senses with their maps, on the other the concepts built from them. Perceptual marks the first side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在心灵中划下一道线：一边是感官和它们的地图，另一边是由此建起的概念。perceptual 标记的是前一边。

senses.title: Contrasted with conceptual
senses.definition: describing information that comes through the senses, as opposed to information organized by categories and definitions
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过感官而来的信息，相对于按类别与定义组织的信息
senses.example: Infants begin with perceptual categories before they form concepts.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿先有知觉类别，之后才形成概念。
senses.why: A concept is taken together and held still; a percept is taken in and kept moving. The adjective marks the difference between the map as drawn and the map as reasoned about.
senses.whyCN: 概念是被聚在一起并固定住的东西，而知觉对象是被拿进来且仍在变动的东西。这个形容词标记的就是“画出来的地图”与“对地图进行推理”之间的差别。

senses.title: Of the psychology of perception
senses.definition: relating to the branch of psychology that studies how organisms detect patterns, depth, colour, and motion
senses.definitionCN: 属于心理学中研究生物如何辨别图案、深度、颜色与运动的分支
senses.example: Perceptual psychology explains why the lines seem to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉心理学解释了这些线条为什么看起来是弯的。
senses.why: When a discipline takes the taking-in as its object, its adjective becomes part of its name. Perceptual psychology studies the drawing of the map, not the land it represents.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把“拿进来”当作研究对象，它的形容词就进入了学科名称。知觉心理学研究的是地图怎么画，而不是它代表的那片土地。

senses.title: Of visual illusions and constancy
senses.definition: relating to visual effects in which the eye's interpretation differs from the measured reality, or stays constant despite changes
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛的解释与实测现实不符，或在变化中仍保持恒常的视觉效应
senses.example: The Müller-Lyer figure is a classic perceptual illusion.
senses.exampleCN: 缪勒—莱尔图形是经典的视觉错觉。
senses.why: The eye draws its map quickly and confidently, and sometimes draws it wrong. The adjective marks the gap between the quick drawing and the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛画地图又快又自信，有时会画错。这个形容词标记的就是“快速画出的图”与“尺子”之间的差距。

senses.title: Of hearing speech sounds
senses.titleCN: 与言语声音的听辨有关的
senses.definition: relating to the way listeners segment and identify speech sounds, often before any meaning is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 指听者切分并识别言语声音的方式，通常发生在赋予意义之前
senses.example: Perceptual training helps learners separate two similar vowels.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉训练帮助学习者区分两个相近的元音。
senses.why: The map here is drawn by the ear. Perceptual work is the parsing of a continuous stream into units, long before the mind asks what the units mean.
senses.whyCN: 这里的地图由耳朵来画。知觉工作是先把连续的声音流切分成单位，远在头脑追问这些单位是什么意思之前。

senses.title: Of a disorder in perceiving
senses.definition: relating to a disturbance in the way the senses register or interpret information, as in clinical diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 与感官登记或解释信息的方式出现紊乱有关，见于临床诊断
senses.example: The patient showed a perceptual deficit after the stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后，患者表现出知觉缺陷。
senses.why: The instrument can break. When the hand no longer takes in properly, the adjective names the fault in the apparatus rather than in the world.
senses.whyCN: 工具是会坏的。当那只手无法正常拿取时，这个形容词命名的是器械的故障，而不是世界的问题。

senses.title: The first stage of cognition
senses.definition: relating to the early stage of information processing that precedes memory, reasoning, and decision
senses.definitionCN: 指先于记忆、推理与决策的信息加工早期阶段
senses.example: The model separates a perceptual stage from a decision stage.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把知觉阶段与决策阶段分开。
senses.why: Information passes through rooms. The first room is where the senses draft the map; later rooms annotate it. Perceptual names the drafting room.
senses.whyCN: 信息要经过一个个房间。第一个房间是感官起草地图的地方，后面的房间才在上面加注。perceptual 命名的就是起草的那个房间。

senses.title: Of an effect on the senses
senses.definition: relating to the immediate sensory impression made by a design, artwork, or environment, before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指设计、艺术品或环境在解释之前造成的直接感官印象
senses.example: The building's perceptual impact comes from its low contrast, not its size.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的知觉冲击来自低对比度，而不是体量。
senses.why: Designers work on the drawing before meaning arrives. A perceptual effect is what the map does to the eye before anyone asks what the map is of.
senses.whyCN: 设计者在意义到来之前先处理这张图。知觉效果就是地图在任何人追问“这是什么”之前，先对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, from Latin -alis 'belonging to'. Percept is Latin perceptum, the neuter past participle of percipere 'to take in', itself per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'take'. The adjective is a modern psychological term: it appears in English in the 19th century, when experimental psychology separated sensation from perception and needed a word for the process itself.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual（拉丁 -alis“属于……的”）。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，即 percipere“拿进来”的中性过去分词，而 percipere 是 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取”。这个形容词是现代心理学术语：19 世纪实验心理学把感觉与知觉分开、需要一个词指知觉过程本身时，它才在英语中出现。

items.en: Perceptum is the neuter past participle of percipere: literally 'that which has been taken in'. Latin already used perceptio for both the receiving and the understanding.
items.cn: perceptum 是 percipere 的中性过去分词，字面即“已经被拿进来之物”。拉丁语早已用 perceptio 同时表示接收与理解。

items.en: Experimental psychology distinguishes sensation (raw stimulation) from perception (organized interpretation) and adopts perceptual for everything belonging to the second term.
items.cn: 实验心理学把感觉（原始刺激）与知觉（有组织的解释）区分开，并采用 perceptual 指属于后者的全部内容。

items.en: The -ual ending is the English form of Latin -alis, the same suffix that gives manual, visual, and conceptual. It marks belonging, so perceptual means 'of perception', never 'able to perceive'.
items.cn: -ual 词尾是拉丁 -alis 的英语形式，也是 manual、visual、conceptual 使用的同一个后缀。它表示归属，所以 perceptual 意为“知觉的”，绝不是“能感知的”。

items.en: The adjective spreads from psychology to design, music, and human factors research: perceptual load, perceptual salience, perceptual speed.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理学扩散到设计、音乐与人因研究：知觉负荷、知觉显著性、知觉速度。

items.en: Perceptive means the person is quick to notice; perceptible means the thing can be noticed; perceptual means the process of noticing. The three share the -cept- stem but split by the suffix.
items.cn: perceptive 指人察觉得快；perceptible 指事物可被察觉；perceptual 指察觉这一过程。三者共享 -cept- 词干，靠后缀分工。

items.en: Conceptual looks like perceptual but its stem is concept, from concipere 'take together' (con- + capere). It is the companion term, not the same branch: concept holds, percept takes in.
items.cn: conceptual 看起来像 perceptual，但词干是 concept，出自 concipere“聚在一起拿取”（con- + capere）。它是配套术语，却不是同一分支：概念握着，知觉拿进来。

note.en: The first group separates three adjectives from the same -cept- stem, then adds the conceptual companion and one different-root trap. The second group compares the adjectives for sensory input, thinking, observing, and what appears.
note.cn: 第一组分开同出 -cept- 词干的三个形容词，再补上 conceptual 这个配套词与一个不同词根的陷阱。第二组比较表示“感官输入”“思维”“观察”“显现”的几个形容词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand. It describes a person, while perceptual describes the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉与理解敏捷的。它描述人，而 perceptual 描述过程本身。

entries.definition: able to be seen, heard, or noticed at all. It is a possibility, not a property of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被看见、听见或察觉的。它表示的是一种可能性，而非过程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to concepts, the categories made by taking things together. It is the usual partner and opposite of perceptual in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 与概念有关的，即把事物聚在一起所形成的类别。在心理学里，它常与 perceptual 配对并相对。

entries.definition: a point of view or the art of showing depth. Its root is specere 'to look', not capere 'to take', so it belongs to the eye's position, not to the intake of information.
entries.definitionCN: 观点或表现深度的技法。它的词根是 specere“看”，不是 capere“拿取”，所以属于眼睛的位置，而非信息的接收。

entries.definition: relating to the sense organs and their input. It names the hardware, while perceptual names the organizing work done with that input.
entries.definitionCN: 与感觉器官及其输入有关的。它命名硬件，而 perceptual 命名对这些输入所做的组织工作。

entries.definition: relating to mental processes such as memory, reasoning, and problem-solving. It covers the whole mind, of which the perceptual stage is the entry.
entries.definitionCN: 与记忆、推理、解决问题等心理过程有关的。它覆盖整个心智，而知觉阶段是其中的入口。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording events, often deliberately. It is an activity of a researcher, not a process of the nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观看并记录事件的，常带有刻意性。它是研究者的活动，而不是神经系统的过程。

entries.definition: relating to experience as it appears to a subject, or simply extraordinary. The philosophical sense is close to perceptual experience, but the everyday sense is 'remarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 与主体所经验到的显现有关的，或仅指非凡的。其哲学义接近知觉经验，但日常义是“了不起的”。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -alis 'belonging to', perceptum, the 19th-century psychology split, the three -cept- adjectives, and the con- 'together' contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-alis“属于”、perceptum、19 世纪心理学的划分、三个 -cept- 形容词，以及 con-“一起”的对比。

normal.en: -ual means 'belonging to': perceptual belongs to perception, just as conceptual belongs to concept and visual to sight.
normal.cn: -ual 意为“属于”：perceptual 属于 perception，就像 conceptual 属于 concept、visual 属于 sight。

normal.en: Perceptum is 'what has been taken in'; perceptual describes the machinery that does the taking.
normal.cn: perceptum 是“已经被拿进来之物”；perceptual 描述执行拿取的那套机制。

normal.en: Perceptive is the person, perceptible is the thing, perceptual is the process: one stem, three suffixes, three jobs.
normal.cn: perceptive 是人，perceptible 是物，perceptual 是过程：一个词干，三个后缀，三种职责。

normal.en: Conceptual has con- 'together' inside: a concept holds things together, while a percept merely brings them in.
normal.cn: conceptual 里面有 con-“一起”：概念把事物握在一起，而知觉只是把它们拿进来。

normal.en: Psychology split sensation from perception in the 19th century, and perceptual became the adjective of the second half.
normal.cn: 19 世纪心理学把感觉与知觉分开，perceptual 成为后半部分的形容词。

abstract.en: A map is not the land, and the drawing style is not the landscape; perceptual is the style of the drawing.
abstract.cn: 地图不是土地，画法也不是风景；perceptual 指的是那种画法。

abstract.en: Two people read the same page: one sees letters, one sees words. The page never moved; the organizing did.
abstract.cn: 两个人读同一页：一个看见字母，一个看见单词。纸页没动，组织方式动了。

abstract.en: An illusion is a map drawn with confidence before the ruler is consulted.
abstract.cn: 错觉就是在还没问尺子之前，就被自信地画出来的地图。

examples.en: Perceptual learning lets the eye recognize the pattern faster.
examples.cn: 知觉学习让眼睛更快认出这个图案。

examples.en: The study compares perceptual and conceptual categories in children.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较儿童的知觉类别与概念类别。

examples.en: Perceptual judgments vary more than the physical measurements do.
examples.cn: 知觉判断的差异比物理测量值的差异更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破塞普图尔」——眼睛“破”开外面的世界，把东西“塞”进去，画成一张图，这张图的画法就是 perceptual → 知觉的；感知的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 perceptum「被拿进来之物」，出自 percipere「拿进来、把握」（per-「彻底」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ual（拉丁 -alis）表归属。核心是「地图的画法本身，而不是地图上的地名」。同族含 perceive、perception、percept、perceptive、perceptible；conceptual 共享 capere 但用 con-「一起」，perspective 的词根则是 specere「看」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of perceptual all describe the drawing of an inner map rather than the land it shows. What changes is which part of the drawing is in view: the process, the sensory side, the contrast with concepts, the psychology, the illusion, the disorder, or the effect on a viewer.
sensesIntro.cn: perceptual 的九个义项都描述内部地图的画法，而不是它所显示的土地。变化的是画法中哪一部分进入视野：过程本身、感官一侧、与概念的对照、心理学、错觉、障碍，还是对观看者的效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the drawing style of the inner map, not the place names written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：内部地图的画法本身，而不是写在地图上的地名。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: the receiving and organizing itself, and its place as the first stage of cognition.
branches.cn: 过程：接收与组织本身，以及它作为认知第一阶段的地位。

branches.en: THE SENSORY SIDE: experience through the senses, defined against conceptual thinking.
branches.cn: 感官一侧：通过感官获得的经验，以概念思维为对照来界定。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS SURPRISES: perceptual psychology and the illusions it explains.
branches.cn: 研究及其意外：知觉心理学，以及它所解释的错觉。

branches.en: EARS AND CLINICS: the parsing of speech sounds, and deficits in the perceiving apparatus.
branches.cn: 耳朵与临床：言语声音的切分，以及知觉器械的缺陷。

branches.en: THE DESIGNED EFFECT: what a visual or spatial arrangement does to the eye before interpretation.
branches.cn: 被设计的效果：视觉或空间安排在任何解释之前对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, the English form of Latin -alis. Percept is Latin perceptum, from percipere (per- 'thoroughly' + capere 'take'). The whole family is built by suffix change on one stem: -ion, -ive, -ible, -ual, and the bare -t.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual，即拉丁 -alis 的英语形式。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，出自 percipere（per-“彻底”+ capere“拿取”）。整个词族都在同一个词干上换后缀：-ion、-ive、-ible、-ual，以及零后缀的 -t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is capere 'take', percipere 'take in', perceptum 'the thing taken in'. Latin had no perceptual; the adjective is a modern extension of the participle stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 capere“拿取”、percipere“拿进来”、perceptum“被拿进来之物”。拉丁语并没有 perceptual，这个形容词是分词词干在现代的延伸。

items.meaning: belonging to the process of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 属于知觉过程的（-ual 表归属）
items.example: Perceptual errors are common in low light.
items.exampleCN: 光线不足时知觉错误很常见。

items.meaning: the act or result of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 知觉的行为或结果（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Her perception of the tone was accurate.
items.exampleCN: 她对语气的感知是准确的。

items.meaning: to take in through the senses or mind
items.meaningCN: 通过感官或心智拿进来；察觉
items.example: We perceived a slight shift in the light.
items.exampleCN: 我们察觉到光线有轻微变化。

items.meaning: the content taken in by the senses
items.meaningCN: 感官所拿进来的内容；知觉对象
items.example: The percept is not the object but the object as sensed.
items.exampleCN: 知觉对象不是物本身，而是被感觉到的物。

items.meaningCN: 察觉敏捷的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: She is perceptive about other people's moods.
items.exampleCN: 她对别人的情绪很敏锐。
这一差别几乎察觉不到。

items.meaningCN: 从知觉角度来说（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two colours are perceptually identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种颜色在知觉上是相同的。

items.meaning: belonging to concepts formed by taking things together
items.meaningCN: 属于把事物聚在一起所形成的概念的（con- 一起 + capere 拿取）
items.exampleCN: 概念模型指导这项实验。

items.meaningCN: 与感觉器官有关的（sentire 感觉 + -ory）
items.exampleCN: 感官过载会让注意力难以集中。

latinEntries.meaning: that which has been taken in

definition_zh: n. 氨；氨气；氨水（家用清洁剂）
definition_en: A colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a sharp smell, used in fertilisers and industry; its water solution is also called ammonia and used as a cleaner.
core_image: 一开盖就冲鼻子的那股刺鼻气味
scene: 她戴上手套才敢擦那面油腻的灶台。 The cleaner contains ammonia, so open a window first.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里的 ammonia 指含氨的清洁液，气味刺鼻，所以要先开窗通风。

senses.title: The gas and industrial chemical
senses.definition: a colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a sharp smell, made in bulk for fertilisers and refrigeration
senses.definitionCN: 由氮与氢构成、气味刺鼻的无色气体，大规模生产用于化肥与制冷
senses.example: The plant produces ammonia for fertiliser factories.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂为化肥厂生产氨。
senses.why: The name comes from sal ammoniac, a salt scraped near a desert shrine, so the word carries a place name into modern industry.
senses.whyCN: 名称来自 sal ammoniac「阿蒙神之盐」，那是在沙漠神殿附近刮取的盐，因此这个词把一个地名带进了现代工业。

senses.title: The household cleaner
senses.definition: a water solution of that gas, sold for cutting grease on glass and hard surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 该气体的水溶液，作为清除玻璃与硬表面油污的清洁剂出售
senses.example: Never mix ammonia with bleach in the same bucket.
senses.exampleCN: 绝不要把氨水与漂白剂混在同一只桶里。
senses.why: The same substance is meant, but the household sense names the bottle on the shelf rather than the molecule in the plant.
senses.whyCN: 指的是同一种物质，但家用义命指的是架子上的那瓶液体，而不是工厂里的分子。

intro.en: Ammonia is shortened from sal ammoniac, the salt of Ammon, collected near the desert shrine of the god Amun. Chemists kept the place name when they isolated the gas.
intro.cn: ammonia 由 sal ammoniac「阿蒙神之盐」缩略而来，那种盐是在阿蒙神的沙漠神殿附近采集的。化学家分离出这种气体时保留了那个地名。

items.en: The name Ammon comes from Greek Ammon, the Egyptian god Amun, whose desert shrine in Libya stood near deposits of a peculiar salt.
items.cn: Ammon 这个名字来自希腊语 Ammon，即埃及神阿蒙；他在利比亚的沙漠神殿附近有一种特殊盐的沉积。

items.en: Latin sal ammoniacus meant salt of Ammon, a crusty salt gathered from the ground near that shrine and used in medicine and metalwork.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sal ammoniacus 意为「阿蒙神之盐」，是在那座神殿附近地面采集的结壳盐，用于医药与金属加工。

items.en: Eighteenth-century chemists shortened sal ammoniac to ammonia once the gas had been isolated from that salt and recognised as a distinct substance.
items.cn: 18 世纪的化学家在从那种盐中分离出气体、并确认它是独立物质后，把 sal ammoniac 缩略为 ammonia。

items.en: English took ammonia in the late eighteenth century, first for the gas and soon for the watery solution sold as a household cleaner.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪后期借入 ammonia，先指气体，很快也指作为家用清洁剂出售的水溶液。

items.en: Ammonia now names a bulk industrial chemical, and the same base gives ammonium for the ion and amine for the wider family of compounds.
items.cn: ammonia 如今指一种大宗工业化学品，同一底座还产生表示离子的 ammonium 与表示更大家族化合物的 amine。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ammon- family and one similar opening; the near-meaning group lists other harsh cleaning chemicals.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ammon- 词族与一个相近开头；近义组列出其他刺激性清洁化学品。

entries.definition: The positive ion formed from ammonia.
entries.definitionCN: 由氨形成的正离子。

entries.definition: A compound derived from ammonia.
entries.definitionCN: 由氨衍生的一类化合物。

entries.definition: Containing or like ammonia.
entries.definitionCN: 含氨的或似氨的。

entries.definition: Loss of memory.
entries.definitionCN: 记忆丧失。

entries.definition: A strong alkaline solution used for cleaning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于清洁的强碱性溶液。

entries.definition: A chemical that removes colour and stains.
entries.definitionCN: 去除颜色与污渍的化学品。

entries.definition: A substance that burns organic tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 能烧伤有机组织的物质。

entries.definition: A liquid that dissolves other substances.
entries.definitionCN: 能溶解其他物质的液体。

normalIntro.en: Ammonia is the salt of Ammon shortened, so link the sharp smell to a desert shrine.
normalIntro.cn: ammonia 是「阿蒙神之盐」的缩略，所以把那股刺鼻气味与一座沙漠神殿联系起来。

normal.en: Ammonia is the gas and the bottle; ammonium is the ion.
normal.cn: ammonia 是气体也是那瓶液体，ammonium 是离子。

normal.en: It is uncountable: some ammonia, not an ammonia.
normal.cn: 它不可数：some ammonia，不说 an ammonia。

normal.en: Never mix ammonia with bleach; the fumes are dangerous.
normal.cn: 绝不要把氨水与漂白剂混合，产生的气体有毒。

normal.en: The smell is sharp and stinging, not sweet.
normal.cn: 气味刺鼻蛰人，不是甜的。

normal.en: Do not confuse ammonia with amnesia, loss of memory.
normal.cn: 别把 ammonia 与 amnesia「记忆丧失」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a bottle that makes your eyes water before you touch it.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶还没碰到就让你眼睛发酸的液体。

abstract.en: Imagine a white crust scraped from desert ground.
abstract.cn: 想象从沙漠地面刮下的一层白壳。

abstract.en: Think of a fertiliser plant breathing out a sharp cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一家化肥厂呼出一团刺鼻的雾。

examples.en: Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen under pressure.
examples.cn: 氨由氮与氢在加压条件下合成。

examples.en: The ammonia smell told us the tank was leaking.
examples.cn: 那股氨味告诉我们储罐在泄漏。

examples.en: She diluted the ammonia before wiping the glass.
examples.cn: 她把氨水稀释后再擦玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿摩尼亚」——阿摩（ammo）尼亚（nia）：一摩（摸）就「你呀」地叫起来，那股冲鼻子的味道就是氨。

root: 埃及神阿蒙之名经希腊语 Ammon 进入拉丁语 sal ammoniacus「阿蒙神之盐」，18 世纪化学家缩略为 ammonia 指从该盐分离出的气体，再引申指家用氨水。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one substance in two places: the molecule made in a plant, and the bottle kept under a sink.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种物质的两个所在：工厂里造出的分子，以及水槽下放着的那瓶液体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp smell that rushes at your nose
core.cn: 核心意象：一开盖就冲鼻子的那股刺鼻气味

branches.en: A plant making fertiliser feedstock.
branches.cn: 一家生产化肥原料的工厂。

branches.en: A leaking tank in a cold store.
branches.cn: 冷库里泄漏的储罐。

branches.en: A bottle under the kitchen sink.
branches.cn: 厨房水槽下的一瓶清洁剂。

branches.en: A window opened before wiping grease.
branches.cn: 擦油污前先打开的窗。

branches.en: One molecule, industrial then domestic.
branches.cn: 同一种分子，先工业用，再家用。

intro.en: Ammonia keeps the name root ammon- plus the substance ending -ia, and shifts to -ium for the ion.
intro.cn: ammonia 保留名称词根 ammon- 加物质词尾 -ia，变成离子时改用 -ium。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sal ammoniacus, salt of Ammon; New Latin cut it to ammonia, and chemistry added ammonium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 sal ammoniacus「阿蒙神之盐」；新拉丁语把它缩略为 ammonia，化学又加上 ammonium。

latinEntries.example: Sal ammoniacus is the old name.
New Latin cut the phrase short.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 新拉丁语把该短语缩略。

definition_zh: n. 咖喱；咖喱粉 v. 用马梳梳刷（马）
definition_en: a dish of meat or vegetables in a spiced sauce, or the powder used to make it
core_image: 一口咕嘟作响的锅，金黄的香料酱汁裹住每一块食材
scene: 厨房里飘出辛辣的香味，一锅炖菜正在咕嘟作响。 She cooked a chicken curry with rice.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：curry 指咖喱菜肴；句意是她做了一份鸡肉咖喱配米饭。

senses.title: Spiced dish
senses.definition: meat or vegetables cooked in a hot spiced sauce
senses.definitionCN: 用辛辣酱汁炖煮的肉或蔬菜
senses.example: We ordered a curry and two naan breads.
senses.exampleCN: 我们点了一份咖喱和两张馕。
senses.why: A golden pot bubbling on the stove.
senses.whyCN: 炉上一口咕嘟作响的金黄锅。

senses.title: Spice powder
senses.definition: a ready-made blend of ground spices
senses.definitionCN: 现成的混合香料粉
senses.example: Add a spoon of curry to the onions.
senses.exampleCN: 往洋葱里加一勺咖喱粉。
senses.why: A jar of yellow dust.
senses.whyCN: 一罐黄色粉末。

senses.title: Groom a horse
senses.definition: to rub a horse down with a special comb
senses.definitionCN: 用特制的梳子给马刷洗
senses.example: The groom curried the horse before the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 马夫在骑行前给马梳刷。
senses.why: A comb moving through a mane.
senses.whyCN: 一把穿过鬃毛的梳子。

intro.en: Curry comes from Tamil kari, a spiced sauce, carried into English by Portuguese traders.
intro.cn: curry 源自泰米尔语 kari（加香料的酱汁），经葡萄牙商人带入英语。

items.en: Kari meant a spiced sauce or relish.
items.cn: kari 意为加香料的酱汁或调味品。

items.en: Caril named the same dish in trade ports.
items.cn: caril 在贸易港口指同一道菜。

items.en: Correier meant to groom a horse.
items.cn: correier 意为梳刷马匹。

items.en: Curry entered English from colonial kitchens.
items.cn: 十七世纪 curry 从殖民地的厨房进入英语。

items.en: Curry powder was sold as a ready blend.
items.cn: 十八世纪咖喱粉作为现成混合香料出售。

items.en: Curry became an everyday favourite worldwide.
items.cn: 二十世纪咖喱成为全世界的日常最爱。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names saucy one-pot dishes.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组都是一锅炖的带汁菜。

entries.definition: To take something along.
entries.definitionCN: 搬运；携带。

entries.definition: To move or act fast.
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙。

entries.definition: Having a coat of fur.
entries.definitionCN: 毛茸茸的。

entries.definition: Meat and vegetables simmered slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 炖菜。

entries.definition: Food baked in a deep pot.
entries.definitionCN: 砂锅菜。

entries.definition: A blend of ground spices.
entries.definitionCN: 混合香料。

entries.definition: A well-seasoned slow stew.
entries.definitionCN: 浓味炖菜。

normalIntro.en: Curry sounds like carry: one pot carries a whole market of spices.
normalIntro.cn: curry 听起来像 carry：一口锅装着一整个香料市场。

normal.en: Carry means to take along.
normal.cn: carry 意为带着走。

normal.en: A curry carries many spices.
normal.cn: 一份咖喱带着许多香料。

normal.en: Curry powder carries the smell.
normal.cn: 咖喱粉带着那股香味。

normal.en: A currycomb carries dust off a horse.
normal.cn: 马梳把尘土从马身上带走。

normal.en: Curry and carry share the same sound shape.
normal.cn: curry 与 carry 读音形状相近。

abstract.en: A pot carrying a spice market.
abstract.cn: 一口装着香料市场的锅。

abstract.en: Yellow dust that wakes a kitchen.
abstract.cn: 唤醒厨房的黄色粉末。

abstract.en: A comb walking through a mane.
abstract.cn: 一把走过鬃毛的梳子。

examples.en: The curry was too hot for the children.
examples.cn: 这份咖喱对孩子们来说太辣了。

examples.en: She curried the pony until its coat shone.
examples.cn: 她给小马梳刷，直到毛色发亮。

examples.en: We keep a jar of curry powder beside the stove.
examples.cn: 我们在炉边放着一罐咖喱粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音像中文「咖喱」，本来就是音译词；再联想 carry，一锅 carrying 各种香料。

root: 泰米尔 kari（酱汁）→ 葡萄牙 caril → 英语 curry；梳刷义另源自古法语 correier

sensesIntro.en: From a spiced pot to a groomed horse.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一锅香料到一匹梳刷过的马。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden pot of spiced sauce bubbling
core.cn: 核心意象：一口咕嘟作响的金黄香料酱锅

branches.en: A pot carrying a spice market.
branches.cn: 一口装着香料市场的锅。

branches.en: Yellow dust that wakes a kitchen.
branches.cn: 唤醒厨房的黄色粉末。

branches.en: A comb walking through a mane.
branches.cn: 一把走过鬃毛的梳子。

branches.en: Powder that becomes a pot.
branches.cn: 变成一锅菜的粉末。

branches.en: A jar and a comb on the same shelf.
branches.cn: 同一层架上的罐子与梳子。

intro.en: Curry is a borrowing, so its parts are the roots it travelled with.
intro.cn: curry 是借词，它的构件是一路同行的词根。

latinIntro.en: Tamil kari means sauce; Latin salsus means salted, the source of sauce.
latinIntro.cn: 泰米尔语 kari 意为酱汁；拉丁语 salsus 意为加盐的，是 sauce 的来源。

definition_zh: 发芽；萌发；使发芽
definition_en: to begin to grow from a seed or spore, or to make such a thing begin to grow
core_image: 一粒豆子在湿纸巾里撑开种皮，白色的小根向下探
scene: 厨房里，一把湿纸巾裹着几粒豆子，放在温暖的窗边。 After five days in damp paper, the beans germinate and push a pale root out of their coats.
sceneCN: 这里 germinate 指「发芽」（第 1 个义项：种子开始长出幼根）；句意为在湿纸里放了五天后，豆子发芽，把白色的根顶出种皮。

senses.title: A seed begins to grow
senses.definition: of a seed, to break out of its coat and start growing
senses.definitionCN: 指种子突破种皮并开始生长
senses.example: The beans germinate in about five days.
senses.exampleCN: 豆子约五天发芽。
senses.why: the verb is intransitive here: the seed is the one that crosses the threshold, with no outside hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词是不及物的：跨过门槛的是种子自己，没有外来的手。

senses.title: Make seeds sprout on purpose
senses.definition: to cause seeds to begin growing before they are planted
senses.definitionCN: 在播种之前使种子开始生长
senses.example: Soak the peas and germinate them on a tray.
senses.exampleCN: 把豌豆泡水，然后在托盘上催芽。
senses.why: the transitive use adds an agent who controls the conditions, so the same verb takes a gardener as subject.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加了一个控制条件的施动者，因此同一个动词可以以园丁为主语。

senses.title: Sprout grain for malting
senses.definition: to start the growth of barley or other grain so that its starch changes
senses.definitionCN: 使大麦等谷物开始生长，从而改变其中的淀粉
senses.example: Maltsters germinate the barley for four days.
senses.exampleCN: 制麦师让大麦发芽四天。
senses.why: controlled sprouting is a manufacturing step, so the verb enters industry unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 受控发芽是一道制造工序，动词因此原样进入工业。

senses.title: A spore begins to grow
senses.definition: of a fungal or fern spore, to produce a first growth tube
senses.definitionCN: 指真菌或蕨的孢子长出第一根生长管
senses.example: The spores germinate only on a wet surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孢子只在湿润表面萌发。
senses.why: spores repeat the seed's gesture, so the botanical verb extends to them without a new word.
senses.whyCN: 孢子重复种子的动作，因此植物学动词不加新词便延伸到它们。

senses.title: A pollen grain grows a tube
senses.definition: of a pollen grain, to produce a tube after landing on a compatible stigma
senses.definitionCN: 指花粉粒落在亲和柱头后长出花粉管
senses.example: The pollen grains germinate within hours of landing.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉粒落地数小时内就萌发。
senses.why: the tube is the grain's root, so the verb keeps its literal growing sense inside a flower.
senses.whyCN: 花粉管就是花粉粒的根，因此动词在花内仍保留字面的生长义。

senses.title: Metaphor: an idea starts to develop
senses.definition: figurative, of a plan or feeling, to begin to develop from a small beginning
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指计划或情感从小处开始发展
senses.example: The idea germinated while she was walking home.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法在她走路回家时萌生了。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the threshold and the hidden start, so nothing is visible until it breaks out.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了门槛与隐蔽的起点，因此在破壳之前什么也看不见。

senses.title: Sprout under the right conditions
senses.definition: to begin growth when warmth, moisture and air allow it
senses.definitionCN: 在温度、水分与空气允许时开始生长
senses.example: These seeds germinate only when the soil reaches fifteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 这些种子只有在土温达到十五度时才发芽。
senses.why: conditions are the gate, so the verb often appears with an only-when clause.
senses.whyCN: 条件是闸门，因此这个动词常与「只有……才」从句连用。

senses.title: Chit seed potatoes before planting
senses.definition: to encourage short shoots on tubers before they go into the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在入土之前促使块茎长出短芽
senses.example: Gardeners germinate their seed potatoes in a cool, bright shed.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在阴凉明亮的棚里给种薯催芽。
senses.why: a tuber is not a seed but behaves like one at planting time, so the verb follows the practical resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 块茎不是种子，但在播种时表现得像种子，动词于是跟着实际相似性走。

intro.en: Germinate comes from Latin germinare 'to sprout', from germen 'sprout, bud, seed'. The deeper origin of germen is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: germinate 来自拉丁 germinare「发芽」，后者出自 germen「芽、胚、种子」。germen 的更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Germen named a sprout or bud, the living point from which a plant extends.
items.cn: germen 指芽或幼枝，即植物向外伸展的那个活的起点。

items.en: Source uncertain: the ancestry of germen before Latin is not settled; a link to a root meaning 'produce, beget' is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：germen 在拉丁语之前的谱系没有定论；把它连到意为「产生、生育」的词根属于重构，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Germinare 'to sprout' is a first-conjugation verb built on germen; its noun is germinatio.
items.cn: germinare「发芽」是建立在 germen 上的第一变位动词；其名词为 germinatio。

items.en: English germinate appears in the seventeenth century, first of plants and later of spores and pollen.
items.cn: 英语 germinate 于 17 世纪出现，先指植物，后指孢子与花粉。

items.en: Malting gave the verb a manufacturing sense, since controlled sprouting is how barley starch is made available.
items.cn: 制麦给了这个动词工业义，因为受控发芽正是让大麦淀粉变得可用的方式。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of germinate is not firmly established; the seventeenth-century placement is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：germinate 最早见于印刷的时间没有确证；归于 17 世纪只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates the germ- family by word class and spelling; group two separates sprouting from the stages before and after it.
note.cn: 第一组按词类与拼写区分 germ- 词族；第二组区分发芽与其前后阶段。

entries.definition: The process the verb names; the verb says what happens, the noun says what it is called.
entries.definitionCN: 动词所指的过程；动词说发生了什么，名词说它叫什么。

entries.definition: The embryo or a microbe; the verb needs a germ to act on, but the germ is not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 胚或微生物；动词需要有胚才能作用，但胚不是动作。

entries.definition: Relating to an early stage; it describes where something is, not that it is sprouting.
entries.definitionCN: 与早期阶段有关；描述事物所处的位置，而非它正在发芽。

entries.definition: From Latin germanus 'closely related', not germen; it means relevant, and the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 germanus「近亲的」，并非 germen；意为相关，相似纯属巧合。

entries.definition: The common verb for a shoot appearing; germinate is its technical counterpart, used in labs and seed testing.
entries.definitionCN: 嫩芽出现的日常动词；germinate 是它在实验室与种子检验中的术语对应词。

entries.definition: To form a bud, the small swelling that will become a shoot or flower; buds form after germination, not during it.
entries.definitionCN: 形成芽，即日后长成枝条或花的小突起；芽在发芽之后形成，而不在发芽之中。

entries.definition: To join gametes or feed soil; in a flower it happens before the seed can germinate.
entries.definitionCN: 使配子结合或给土壤施肥；在花中它发生在种子能够发芽之前。

entries.definition: To keep eggs or cultures at the right warmth so that development can proceed; it names the care, not the emergence.
entries.definitionCN: 把卵或培养物保持在合适温度，使发育得以进行；它指照料，而非破出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root, the real agricultural phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的农事搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: germen 'sprout' + -ate: to do the sprout thing.
normal.cn: germen「芽」+ -ate：做「发芽」这件事。

normal.en: The same root gives germ, germinal, germination.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 germ、germinal、germination。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: germinate seeds, germinate barley, germinate quickly.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：催芽、使大麦发芽、很快发芽。

normal.en: Water, warmth and air are the three gates the verb waits behind.
normal.cn: 水、温度与空气是这个动词所等待的三道闸门。

normal.en: Both seeds and spores take the same verb.
normal.cn: 种子与孢子都接受同一个动词。

abstract.en: Picture a parcel splitting at one seam and a small root slipping out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹沿一条缝裂开，一小段根滑了出来。

abstract.en: Picture a bare field that shows green only after the third warm day.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裸地，只在第三个暖日之后才露绿。

abstract.en: Picture a remark that stays quiet for months and then becomes a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话安静了几个月，然后变成一项计划。

examples.en: The seeds germinate within a week if kept moist.
examples.cn: 保持湿润的话，这些种子一周内发芽。

examples.en: Farmers germinate barley before it goes to the malt floor.
examples.cn: 农民在把大麦送去制麦之前先让它发芽。

examples.en: The idea germinated during a long walk.
examples.cn: 这个想法在一次长距离散步中萌生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「germ（芽）+ inate」——让芽从种皮里出来 → 发芽

root: 拉丁 germen, germinis「芽、胚、种子」→ germinare「发芽」→ 英语 germinate。germen 更早来源不确定，与「产生、生育」词根的联系属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of germinate all cross one threshold: something enclosed starts to grow, whether the grower is nature, a gardener, a maltster or a laboratory.
sensesIntro.cn: germinate 的八个义项都跨过同一个门槛：封闭之物开始生长，无论促成者是自然、园丁、制麦师还是实验室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat splits and a root reaches down.
core.cn: 核心意象：种皮裂开，一支根向下探。

branches.en: NATURAL START: the seed does it itself once the conditions allow.
branches.cn: 自然开始：条件许可时，种子自己完成。

branches.en: HUMAN START: a gardener can force the same event on a tray or a tuber.
branches.cn: 人为开始：园丁能在托盘或块茎上促成同样的事件。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL START: controlled sprouting makes grain starch usable.
branches.cn: 工业开始：受控发芽使谷物淀粉变得可用。

branches.en: OTHER GRAINS: spores and pollen repeat the gesture at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 其他颗粒：孢子与花粉在更小尺度上重复同一动作。

branches.en: METAPHOR: a plan crosses the same threshold quietly.
branches.cn: 比喻：计划同样安静地跨过这一门槛。

intro.en: Germinate is a Latin noun turned into a verb, and the same base yields the embryo, the act and the capacity.
intro.cn: germinate 是拉丁名词转成的动词，同一词基衍生出胚、动作与能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin germen 'sprout' gives germinare; English builds germ, germinate, germination and germinal from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 germen「芽」衍生 germinare；英语在同一词族上构成 germ、germinate、germination 与 germinal。

items.example: Germen names the point of new growth.
Germinate means to perform the sprouting.

items.meaning: tending to, having the power to
items.exampleCN: 有发芽力的种子容易发芽。

items.example: Each germ holds a tiny plant.
items.exampleCN: 每个胚里都藏着一株小小的植物。

items.meaning: of a germ or an early stage

items.exampleCN: 长期贮藏会使发芽能力下降。

definition_zh: 磨损；擦伤；磨掉表层
definition_en: to wear away or scrape off the surface of something by friction
core_image: 砂纸来回打磨，表层一点点消失
scene: 老师傅抓起工人的手看了看，皱起眉头说机器的毛边磨破了手套。 Rough rocks abraded the paint on the hull.
sceneCN: 这里 abrade 是「磨掉表层」（第 1 个义项：粗石磨损船壳漆面）；句意为粗粝的岩石磨掉了船壳上的漆。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「磨损处；擦伤」
由同一词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「磨损性的；（言行）粗鲁的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「磨损性；（性格）生硬」

senses.title: To wear away a surface by friction
senses.definition: to scrape or rub away the outer layer of a material or object
senses.definitionCN: 通过摩擦刮去或磨去材料、物体的表层
senses.example: Grit carried by the wind abraded the stone face of the monument.
senses.exampleCN: 风中夹带的砂粒磨蚀了纪念碑的石面。
senses.why: Latin ab- (off) plus radere (to scrape) keeps the image of something scraped away bit by bit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab-（去掉）加 radere（刮），保留了「一点点刮掉」的意象。

senses.title: To scrape or wound the skin
senses.definition: to rub off or damage skin by rough contact, usually superficially
senses.definitionCN: 因粗糙接触而擦脱或损伤皮肤，通常只伤表层
senses.example: The rope abraded his palms as he slid down.
senses.exampleCN: 他往下滑时绳子磨破了手掌。
senses.why: Skin is just another surface, so the scraping image transfers from stone to flesh without change.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤不过是另一种表面，刮擦意象由石头原样转移到血肉。

senses.title: To be worn away by friction
senses.definition: intransitive use: to undergo wearing away through rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 不及物用法：因摩擦而逐渐被磨损
senses.example: Old inscriptions abrade quickly in sandy climates.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的铭文在多沙气候里很快被磨蚀。
senses.why: English verbs of action often flip to let the patient stand alone as subject.
senses.whyCN: 英语的动作动词常可翻转，让受事者单独充当主语。

intro.en: Abrade comes from Latin abradere, built on ab- 'off' and radere 'to scrape'; the same root gave rat and rodent-like words their scraping sense in razors and rays.
intro.cn: abrade 来自拉丁语 abradere，由 ab-「去掉」加 radere「刮」构成；同一词根还出现在 razor 等刮擦类词中。

items.en: A reconstructed root *ras- or *red- meant to scrape or scratch, generally regarded as the source of the Latin family.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ras-／*red- 义为刮、擦，一般认为是拉丁词族的来源。

items.en: Radere meant to scrape; rasp, erase, and razor descend from related forms.
items.cn: radere 义为刮；rasp、erase 与 razor 均出自相关词形。

items.en: Abradere added ab- 'off', making the scraping complete: to scrape away.
items.cn: abradere 加上 ab-「去掉」，使刮擦彻底：刮掉、磨掉。

items.en: The past participle abrasus fed later noun forms like abrasio.
items.cn: 过去分词 abrasus 衍生出 abrasio 等名词形式。

items.en: The verb entered English through learned or scientific writing, first for physical wear.
items.cn: 动词经学术与科学著作进入英语，最初指物理磨损。

items.en: Medicine and engineering keep the word for surface scraping, while abrasive carries a social metaphor.
items.cn: 医学与工程仍用其表「刮擦表面」，abrasive 则衍生出社交隐喻。

note.en: The first group is the scraping root family; the second lists wear-related verbs.
note.cn: 第一组为刮擦词根家族；第二组为表磨损的动词。

entries.definition: the scraped spot or the process of wearing away.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损处或磨损过程。

entries.definition: scraping hard, or figuratively harsh in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损性的；引申指言语态度粗鲁。

entries.definition: to rub out writing; from e- plus the same scraping root.
entries.definitionCN: 擦除字迹；由 e- 加同一刮擦词根构成。

entries.definition: to repeal a law; only ab- is shared, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 废除法律；仅共享 ab- 前缀，词根不同。

entries.definition: to crush or wear down by friction, usually with force.
entries.definitionCN: 以摩擦碾碎或磨耗，通常用力较大。

entries.definition: to rub and make sore, especially skin.
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦致痛，尤指皮肤。

entries.definition: to eat away chemically rather than by friction.
entries.definitionCN: 以化学方式侵蚀，而非摩擦。

entries.definition: to drag something rough across a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用粗糙物在表面拖刮。

entries.definition: to make a surface smooth and shiny; the aim is opposite to abrade.
entries.definitionCN: 使表面光滑发亮；目的与 abrade 相反。

normalIntro.en: Break the word into ab- plus the scrape root.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词拆成 ab- 加刮擦词根来记。

normal.en: ab- = off; rad- = scrape; so scrape off.
normal.cn: ab- = 去掉；rad- = 刮；合起来即「刮掉」。

normal.en: Family: eraser erases by the same scraping idea.
normal.cn: 词族：eraser 靠同一「刮擦」观念擦字。

normal.en: razor and raze share the family image of shaving away.
normal.cn: razor 与 raze 同属「刮平、剃去」意象家族。

normal.en: -e verb ending: abrade → abraded → abrasion.
normal.cn: 动词以 -e 结尾：abrade → abraded → abrasion。

normal.en: Think sandpaper: its whole job is to abrade.
normal.cn: 想想砂纸：其全部职责就是磨蚀。

abstract.en: Hear the dry hiss of sandpaper on wood.
abstract.cn: 听砂纸打磨木头时干涩的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Feel rope fiber biting into a palm.
abstract.cn: 体会绳索纤维咬进掌心的感觉。

abstract.en: See a stone inscription slowly going faint.
abstract.cn: 看石碑铭文一点点变淡。

examples.en: Ceaseless tides abrade the base of the cliffs.
examples.cn: 不息的潮水磨蚀着崖基。

examples.en: Workers abraded the glossy layer before repainting the wall.
examples.cn: 工人们先把光亮层磨掉，再给墙重新刷漆。

examples.en: Long hikes had abraded the toes of his boots thin.
examples.cn: 长途跋涉把他的靴头磨薄了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我别锐的」——刀别太锐，来回一磨就磨损了。

root: 拉丁语 abradere：ab-（去掉）+ radere（刮、擦）。印欧词根一般认为重构为 *ras-/*red-「刮擦」，同族词含 erase、razor、rasp 等。动词经十七世纪学术英语定型，核心义始终是「以摩擦去掉表层」。

sensesIntro.en: One image of scraping spreads to materials, skin, and the wearing-away process itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 「刮擦」一个意象延伸到材料、皮肤与磨损过程本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sandpaper dragging a surface thinner stroke by stroke.
core.cn: 核心意象：砂纸一下一下把表面拖磨变薄。

branches.en: MATERIALS: wind, grit, and tools wear stone, paint, and metal.
branches.cn: 材料：风、砂粒与工具磨损石、漆、金属。

branches.en: BODY: ropes and rough cloth scrape the skin.
branches.cn: 身体：绳索与粗布擦伤皮肤。

branches.en: PATIENT SUBJECT: the worn thing itself takes the verb.
branches.cn: 受事主语：被磨损之物自身作主语。

branches.en: PROCESS VIEW: abrade names the slow mechanical loss of surface.
branches.cn: 过程视角：abrade 指表层缓慢的机械性损耗。

branches.en: MEDICINE: abrasion grades keep the scraping image in clinical use.
branches.cn: 医学：擦伤分级使刮擦意象进入临床用语。

intro.en: The scrape root rad- builds a wide family of rubbing words.
intro.cn: 刮擦词根 rad- 构建了一个庞大的摩擦词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives keep scraping visible in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词让「刮擦」在英语中处处可见。

items.meaning: to scrape or level to the ground
items.example: raze a building to the ground

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「磨损性的；粗鲁的」

definition_zh: 利润率；利润占销售收入的比重
definition_en: the share of sales revenue that a business keeps as profit after its costs are paid
core_image: 收支表最下面一行，收入数字旁边留出一小块空白，那一小块被红框框住并写上比例
scene: 会计把全年收入与各项成本写进表格，最后在收入旁边框出剩下的那一小块。 A thin profit margin forced the factory to raise its prices.
sceneCN: 这里这个词组指「利润占销售收入的比重」（第 1 个义项：毛利口径的利润率）；句意为微薄的利润率迫使工厂提价。图中可辨识物件：收支表、收入数字、被框出的一小块、红笔。

pos.zh: 利润率（可数；指利润占销售收入的比重）

forms.label: 相关形容词（边缘的；边际的）

senses.title: Gross margin, before overheads
senses.titleCN: 扣除日常开销之前的毛利率
senses.definition: the share left from sales after only the direct cost of the goods is subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 销售额在只扣除货物直接成本之后剩下的比重
senses.example: The bakery's gross profit margin stays near a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店的毛利率维持在三成左右。
senses.why: Margin first meant the edge of a page; the accounting sense is what is left at the edge of a sale.
senses.whyCN: margin 本指纸页的边缘；会计义指一笔销售走到边缘时剩下的部分。

senses.title: Net margin, after everything
senses.titleCN: 扣除一切之后的净利率
senses.definition: the share left after all costs, interest and tax have been paid
senses.definitionCN: 在支付全部成本、利息与税款之后剩下的比重
senses.example: After the loan was repaid the net profit margin fell to a few percent.
senses.exampleCN: 偿还贷款之后，净利率降到几个百分点。
senses.why: The edge moves inward as more layers of cost are peeled away.
senses.whyCN: 随着一层层成本被剥去，那道边缘就向内收。

senses.title: Operating margin, before financing
senses.titleCN: 融资成本之前的营业利润率
senses.definition: the share left from ordinary operations, before interest and tax are counted
senses.definitionCN: 日常经营剩下、尚未计入利息与税款的比重
senses.example: The operating profit margin improved when the old plant closed.
senses.exampleCN: 旧厂关闭之后，营业利润率有所提高。
senses.why: This is the edge of the trading itself, with the cost of money still outside the line.
senses.whyCN: 这是交易本身的边缘，资金成本还站在线外。

senses.title: Margin on a single product
senses.definition: the profit left by one item, measured against what that item sold for
senses.definitionCN: 一件商品带来的利润，相对该商品的售价来衡量
senses.example: The margin on each pair of shoes is smaller than on the bags.
senses.exampleCN: 每双鞋的利润率低于每只包的利润率。
senses.why: The same ratio can be narrowed from a whole firm to one line on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比率可以从整个公司缩小到货架上的一个品类。

senses.title: A thin industry average
senses.titleCN: 行业里微薄的平均水平
senses.definition: the low figure typical of a trade where competition keeps prices close to cost
senses.definitionCN: 竞争使价格紧贴成本的那种行业所常见的低水平
senses.example: Grocers survive on a thin profit margin and high volume.
senses.exampleCN: 杂货商靠微薄的利润率与高销量维持。
senses.why: When the edge is narrow, the word describes the whole trade rather than one firm.
senses.whyCN: 当那道边缘很窄时，这个词描述的是整个行业，而不只是一家公司。

senses.title: A buffer against shocks
senses.definition: the amount of profit that can absorb a rise in costs before losses begin
senses.definitionCN: 在开始亏损之前能够吸收成本上涨的利润额度
senses.example: A healthy profit margin let the airline survive the fuel spike.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的利润率让这家航空公司挺过了燃油价格暴涨。
senses.why: A margin is space at the edge, and space is exactly what absorbs a blow.
senses.whyCN: margin 是边缘上的余地，而余地正是吸收打击的东西。

senses.title: The figure that is not a markup
senses.titleCN: 与加价率不同的那个数字
senses.definition: profit measured against sales, as opposed to an addition measured against cost
senses.definitionCN: 以销售额为分母的利润，与以成本为分母的加价相对
senses.example: Managers often confuse the profit margin with the markup on cost.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者常把利润率与成本加价率混为一谈。
senses.why: The two numbers describe one gap from opposite ends, so they can never be equal.
senses.whyCN: 两个数字从两端描述同一个差额，因此永远不可能相等。

senses.title: A target set in a plan
senses.definition: a figure that a business aims to reach, written into a budget or a strategy
senses.definitionCN: 企业力争达到、写进预算或战略的数值
senses.example: The new plan sets a profit margin target for every region.
senses.exampleCN: 新计划给每个区域都设定了利润率目标。
senses.why: Once a ratio is chosen as a goal, the word shifts from description to intention.
senses.whyCN: 当一个比率被选为目标，这个词就从描述变成了意图。

intro.en: Profit comes from Latin profectus, progress or gain, built on proficere to accomplish; margin comes from Latin margo, edge or border. Their accounting pairing is modern.
intro.cn: profit 来自拉丁语 profectus「进展、收益」，由 proficere「完成、取得」构成；margin 来自拉丁语 margo「边缘、边界」。两者在会计上的搭配是近代的事。

items.en: Proficere joined pro- forward with facere to do, and meant to make progress or to accomplish something.
items.cn: proficere 由表示「向前」的 pro- 与 facere「做」构成，意为「取得进展、完成某事」。

items.en: The noun profectus named progress or an advance, and in commercial Latin it came to mean gain.
items.cn: 名词 profectus 指「进展、前进」，在商业拉丁语中逐渐指「收益」。

items.en: Old French profit carried the commercial sense into English, where profit named the gain from a transaction.
items.cn: 古法语 profit 把这个商业义带入英语，profit 指一笔交易带来的收益。

items.en: Margo meant an edge, a border or a brink, and it survives in English margin as the blank edge of a page.
items.cn: margo 意为「边缘、边界、崖沿」，在英语 margin 中保留为纸页的空白边缘。

items.en: Margin extended from the edge of a page to any difference or allowance, including the space between cost and price.
items.cn: margin 从纸页边缘扩展到任何差额或余量，包括成本与价格之间的空间。

items.en: Profit margin became a fixed accounting term once firms began reporting profit as a share of sales.
items.cn: 当企业开始把利润按占销售额的比例报告时，profit margin 成为固定的会计术语。

note.en: The first group holds the two words that make the phrase and their near forms; the second holds other measures of what a business keeps.
note.cn: 第一组是构成这个短语的两个词及其近形；第二组是衡量企业留存的其他指标。

entries.definition: The blank edge of a page, and by extension the difference between two figures; it carries the second half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 纸页的空白边缘，引申为两个数字之间的差；它构成短语的后半。

entries.definition: At the edge, hence small or barely worth doing; it describes size, not a percentage of sales.
entries.definitionCN: 处在边缘的，因此指微小或几乎不值得做；它描述大小，不指占销售额的比例。

entries.definition: The addition over cost; it uses cost as its base, which is the opposite base from a profit margin.
entries.definitionCN: 在成本之上的加价；它以成本为基数，与利润率的基数正好相反。

entries.definition: The money gained itself; a margin turns that money into a share of sales.
entries.definitionCN: 实际赚到的钱本身；利润率则把这笔钱变成占销售额的比重。

entries.definition: The gain measured against what was put in, often used for investments rather than for shop sales.
entries.definitionCN: 相对投入衡量的收益，常用于投资，而不常用于店铺销售。

entries.definition: The difference between a buying price and a selling price, common in trading and lending.
entries.definitionCN: 买入价与卖出价之间的差，常见于交易与借贷。

entries.definition: A firm's reported profit for a period, stated as an amount rather than as a share of sales.
entries.definitionCN: 企业某一期公布的利润，以金额而非占销售额的比例表示。

entries.definition: Money received before costs or tax are taken out; it is a total, while a margin is a ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 在扣除成本或税之前收到的钱；它是总额，而利润率是比率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Profit plus margin: the gain measured at the edge of a sale.
normal.cn: 「收益」加「边缘」：在销售的边缘上衡量的收益。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, margin and marginal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 profit、profitable、profitability、margin 与 marginal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the layers: gross profit margin, net profit margin, operating profit margin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层次：毛利率、净利率、营业利润率。

normal.en: Remember the base: a margin sits on sales, a markup sits on cost.
normal.cn: 记住基数：利润率坐在销售额上，加价率坐在成本上。

normal.en: A thin margin is a narrow ledge: there is little room left before a fall.
normal.cn: 微薄的利润率就是一条窄窄的台子：在跌落之前几乎没有余地。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose margin is the only white space left after the text of costs fills it.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被成本写满，只剩下页边那一点空白。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow ledge above a drop, wide enough for one foot only.
abstract.cn: 想象悬崖边一条窄窄的台子，只够放一只脚。

abstract.en: Picture the same gap seen from two shores, one calling it cost, the other calling it sales.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个缺口从两岸看过去，一岸称它成本，另一岸称它销售额。

examples.en: The firm's net profit margin has stayed above ten percent for five years.
examples.cn: 这家公司的净利率已连续五年保持在百分之十以上。

examples.en: Discounting can raise volume while shrinking the profit margin.
examples.cn: 打折可以提高销量，同时压缩利润率。

examples.en: Small farms work on a profit margin too thin to absorb one bad season.
examples.cn: 小农场的利润率太薄，承受不住一个坏季节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「收益（profit）留在页边（margin）」——卖出去的钱走到边缘时剩下的那一小块 → 利润率

root: profit 来自拉丁语 profectus「进展、收益」，由 pro-「向前」与 facere「做」构成；margin 来自拉丁语 margo「边缘、边界」，引申为差额与余量。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ratio as it is peeled inward: gross, net, operating, a single product, an industry average, a buffer, the contrast with a markup, and a target written into a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个比率向内剥：毛利、净利、营业、单件产品、行业平均、缓冲余地、与加价率的对照，最后是写进计划的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger page filled with costs, with one small boxed space left at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页写满成本的账簿，边缘还留着一小块被框住的空白。

branches.en: LAYERS OF COST: gross, net and operating differ only in how many layers have been peeled away.
branches.cn: 成本的层次：毛利、净利与营业利润的差别只在于剥去了几层。

branches.en: ONE ITEM: the same ratio narrowed from a firm to a single pair of shoes.
branches.cn: 单件商品：同一个比率从一家公司缩小到一双鞋。

branches.en: A WHOLE TRADE: a narrow ledge becomes the description of an industry.
branches.cn: 整个行业：一条窄台子成了对一个行业的描述。

branches.en: SPACE AS SHOCK ABSORBER: the width of the edge is what absorbs a rise in costs.
branches.cn: 作为缓冲的余地：边缘的宽度就是吸收成本上涨的东西。

branches.en: THE OTHER BASE AND THE GOAL: the ratio is distinguished from a markup and then fixed as a target.
branches.cn: 另一个基数与目标：这个比率先与加价率区分开，再被固定为目标。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of gain with a Latin noun of edge, so it reads as the gain that remains at the edge of a sale.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语中表示「收益」的名词与表示「边缘」的名词组合起来，读作「一笔销售走到边缘时留下的收益」。

latinIntro.en: Latin proficere and profectus supply profit; Latin margo supplies margin, which also stands behind marginal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proficere 与 profectus 提供 profit；拉丁语 margo 提供 margin，marginal 也出自同一词根。

items.example: The prefix turns doing into getting ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「做」变成「向前取得」。

items.example: The verb supplies the act at the heart of profit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「收益」一词核心处的行动。

items.example: The business profited steadily through the year.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业在一年中稳步获利。

items.example: The year's profit paid for the new roof.
items.exampleCN: 这一年的收益付了新屋顶的钱。

items.example: The route became profitable once freight returned.
items.exampleCN: 货运恢复之后，这条线路变得有利可图。
合并之后盈利能力有所提高。

items.example: The noun gave English its page edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给英语带来了「页边」。

items.structure: Latin margo, through Old French marge
items.meaning: an edge; a difference or allowance
items.example: The margin between cost and price widened.
items.exampleCN: 成本与价格之间的差额扩大了。

items.example: The second factory made only a marginal gain.
items.exampleCN: 第二家工厂只带来勉强可观的收益。

definition_zh: 甜言蜜语；奉承；哄诱
definition_en: flattering or coaxing words used to persuade someone
core_image: 有人捧着蜜罐在你耳边轻声劝诱
scene: 货郎把糖葫芦举到孩子面前，低声劝了半天。 She refused to listen to his blandishments.
sceneCN: 这里 blandishment 是「甜言蜜语」（第 1 个义项：以奉承哄劝使人就范）；句意是她拒绝听信他的花言巧语。

pos.zh: 甜言蜜语；哄诱（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: 词根动词，义为「奉承；哄诱」
同根形容词，义为「温和的；讨好的」

senses.title: Flattering speech to persuade
senses.titleCN: 以奉承劝诱的甜言蜜语
senses.definition: words of praise and coaxing used to win someone over
senses.definitionCN: 以称赞与哄劝来赢得他人同意的话
senses.example: She refused to listen to his blandishments.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝听信他的花言巧语。
senses.why: Soft Latin blandus meant caressing in speech, and the noun names the caress of words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 blandus 本指言辞的抚慰，名词所记的正是「言语的抚弄」。

senses.title: Coaxing meant to gain a favour
senses.definition: gentle urging aimed at obtaining a favour or concession
senses.definitionCN: 以温和劝诱谋取好处或让步
senses.example: After hours of blandishment, the manager granted the refund.
senses.exampleCN: 哄劝了几个小时后，经理同意了退款。
senses.why: The caress has an aim: softness is the tool, favour is the goal.
senses.whyCN: 抚弄自有目的：柔软是手段，好处是终点。

senses.title: The lure of fame or pleasure
senses.definition: the attractive pull of success, fame, or pleasure, treated as flattery
senses.definitionCN: 成功、名望或享乐如奉承般的吸引
senses.example: He could not resist the blandishments of the big city.
senses.exampleCN: 他抵挡不住大都市的种种诱惑。
senses.why: The city seems to whisper praise of what it offers, so its pull is a blandishment.
senses.whyCN: 城市仿佛在低声夸赞自己的馈赠，其吸引力因此成了甜言蜜语。

senses.title: Advertising and sales talk
senses.definition: persuasive commercial talk dressed as praise
senses.definitionCN: 包装成赞美之词的推销话术
senses.example: Ignore the blandishments of the sales brochure.
senses.exampleCN: 别理会宣传册里的花言巧语。
senses.why: Ads flatter the buyer while coaxing money out, the oldest use dressed new.
senses.whyCN: 广告一面奉承买主一面掏钱，是旧义披上新衣。

senses.title: Diplomatic or political coaxing
senses.definition: conciliatory language used in negotiation to soften resistance
senses.definitionCN: 谈判中用于软化对方抵制的安抚性言辞
senses.example: The envoy's blandishments eased the tense talks.
senses.exampleCN: 特使的安抚言辞缓和了紧张的谈判。
senses.why: Statecraft, like courtship, often prefers the soft touch to the threat.
senses.whyCN: 治国与求爱相通：常以软语代替威胁。

senses.title: Courtship talk
senses.definition: romantic coaxing addressed to a loved person
senses.definitionCN: 向心上人说的哄劝之语
senses.example: His letters were full of tender blandishment.
senses.exampleCN: 他的信里满是温柔缠绵的甜言蜜语。
senses.why: Love's persuasion is the home ground of the caressing word.
senses.whyCN: 求爱的劝诱正是「抚慰之语」的本源场域。

senses.title: Insincere praise from the ambitious
senses.definition: hollow flattery offered to a person of power for gain
senses.definitionCN: 为谋利而向权势者奉上的空洞赞美
senses.example: Courtiers survived on blandishment alone.
senses.exampleCN: 朝臣们单靠奉承度日。
senses.why: When praise is bought, the caress turns into currency.
senses.whyCN: 当赞美可以买卖，抚慰便变成了通货。

senses.title: Gentle enticement of things or comforts
senses.definition: the mild enticement of comfort, food, or ease
senses.definitionCN: 舒适、美食或安逸发出的温和引诱
senses.example: The warm fire made its own blandishment.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的炉火自有一种温柔的引诱。
senses.why: Comfort, too, seems to coax; the word stretches from speech to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 安逸同样会「哄人」，该词由言语伸展到感受。

intro.en: Blandishment grows from Latin blandiri, to caress with words.
intro.cn: blandishment 源自拉丁语 blandiri「以言语抚慰」。

items.en: the deeper root is uncertain; possibly tied to gentle, slow motion.
items.cn: 更早词根来源不确定，一般认为与「轻缓的动作」相关。

items.en: blandiri meant to flatter, coax, fondle with words, from blandus, caressing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 blandiri 意为「奉承、哄诱」，出自 blandus「抚慰的」。

items.en: blandissement carried the flattering sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 blandissement 承袭「奉承」之义。

items.en: English borrowed the word for coaxing and flattering speech.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪借入该词，指哄诱与奉承之语。

items.en: now usually plural, blandishments, for any seductive lure.
items.cn: 今多用复数 blandishments，泛指一切诱惑之辞。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bland- root; the near-meaning group gathers words of flattery and lure.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bland- 词根；近义组汇集奉承与诱惑类词。

normal.en: It can describe the lure of a city or of fame.

abstract.en: Feel a hand stroking your arm as it reaches for your purse.

sensesIntro.en: From courtly flattery to the lure of cities, blandishment names every soft word that pulls.
sensesIntro.cn: 从宫廷奉承到都市诱惑，blandishment 指一切具有拉力的软语。
