definition_zh: 公司的；法人的；团体的；共同组成的
definition_en: relating to a corporation or a large business, or shared by all members of a group
core_image: 许多人被铸成同一个法人身体
scene: 新员工在宣传片里看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号。 In the new recruitment film the staff saw the same tower, the same slogan, and the same corporate logo.
sceneCN: 这里 corporate 是「公司的」（第 1 个义项：与公司有关的）；句意：在新宣传片里，员工看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号和同一个公司标志。

derivatives.zh: 社团主义的；社团主义者

senses.title: Relating to a business corporation
senses.definition: connected with a corporation or a large company rather than an individual
senses.definitionCN: 与公司或大企业有关，而不是与个人有关
senses.example: The company moved its corporate headquarters downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把总部搬到了市中心。
senses.why: corporate is Latin corpus 'body' + -ate. A corporation is a group legally treated as one body, so corporate describes whatever belongs to that body.
senses.whyCN: corporate 是拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate。corporation 是被法律当作一个身体看待的群体，因此 corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切。

senses.title: Of large companies as a social force
senses.titleCN: 作为社会力量的大企业
senses.definition: relating to big business as a political, cultural, or economic power
senses.definitionCN: 与作为政治、文化或经济力量的大企业有关
senses.example: The film criticises corporate power.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片批评企业权力。
senses.why: When a legal body grows large, it acts almost like a person with interests. Corporate then names the collective actor, not just its paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当一个法律身体变大，它几乎像一个有利益的人那样行动。corporate 此时命名的是集体行动者，而不只是它的文件。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: belonging to or shared by all members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 属于或由群体全体成员共同拥有
senses.example: The report is a corporate effort, not one person's work.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是集体努力的结果，不是一个人的工作。
senses.why: The 'one body' image makes authorship collective. A corporate effort comes from the body as a whole, even if many hands made it.
senses.whyCN: “一个身体”的意象使作者身份变成集体的。集体努力来自整个身体，即使有许多只手参与。

senses.title: United in one legal body
senses.definition: in legal and historical usage, formed into a single body with legal personality
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与历史用法中，组成具有法人人格的单一团体
senses.example: The bishops met as a corporate body.
senses.exampleCN: 主教们以一个法人团体的身份开会。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a group is 'bodied' into one entity that can hold property and act in law. The body is not physical but legal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最老的义项：一群人被“结成身体”，成为一个能持有财产、在法律上行动的实体。这个身体不是物理的，而是法律的。

senses.title: Of corporate law, finance, and governance
senses.titleCN: 公司法、金融与治理层面的
senses.definition: relating to the legal and financial structure of companies, such as boards, shares, and mergers
senses.definitionCN: 与公司的法律和财务结构有关，如董事会、股份和并购
senses.example: Corporate law governs mergers and acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 公司法规范并购活动。
senses.why: A legal body needs organs and rules: a board, shareholders, meetings. Corporate marks the level at which the body itself, not its employees, is the subject.
senses.whyCN: 法律身体需要器官和规则：董事会、股东、会议。corporate 标记的是“身体本身”而非员工作为行为主体的层级。

senses.title: Corporate identity and branding
senses.definition: relating to the visual and verbal identity a company presents to the public
senses.definitionCN: 与公司向公众呈现的视觉和语言识别系统有关
senses.example: They redesigned the corporate logo and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们重新设计了公司标志和配色。
senses.why: A body needs a face. The logo, typeface and slogan give the collective body one recognisable appearance.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要一张脸。标志、字体和口号给这个集体身体一个可辨认的外观。

senses.title: Of a municipality or other incorporated body
senses.definition: relating to any group given legal personality, such as a city or a charity
senses.definitionCN: 与任何被赋予法人资格的群体有关，如城市或慈善机构
senses.example: The city is a corporate entity with its own powers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是一个拥有自身权力的法人实体。
senses.why: Incorporation is not limited to business. A city, university or charity can also be one body in law, and corporate describes that status.
senses.whyCN: 法人化并不限于商业。城市、大学或慈善机构也可以在法律上成为一个身体，corporate 描述的就是这种身份。

senses.title: Derived family: corporation and corporatism
senses.definition: in corporation and corporatism, the 'body' image is applied to a company or to a state organised by occupational groups
senses.definitionCN: 在 corporation 与 corporatism 中，“身体”意象被用于公司，或被用于按职业团体组织起来的国家
senses.example: Corporatism builds an economy out of corporate bodies such as guilds and employers' groups.
senses.exampleCN: 社团主义用行会、雇主团体这类法人团体来搭建经济。
senses.why: The same body image produces very different institutions: a company, a city, or a state built from occupational corporations. The suffix changes, the body stays.
senses.whyCN: 同一个身体意象产生很不同的制度：公司、城市，或由职业团体构成的国家。后缀变了，身体还在。

intro.en: Corporate comes from corpus 'body'. A corporation is a group made into one legal body, and corporate describes anything belonging to that body — business, city, or state.
intro.cn: corporate 来自 corpus“身体”。corporation 是被制成一个法律身体的群体，corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切——企业、城市或国家。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'united in one body'. The commercial sense 'of a business corporation' develops later.
items.cn: 15 世纪最早记录，意为“结成一体”。“属于商业公司”的义项后来才发展出来。

items.en: From Latin corporatus, past participle of corporare 'to form into a body', from corpus 'body'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 corporatus，即 corporare“使成为身体”的过去分词，后者来自 corpus“身体”。

items.en: corpus (genitive corporis) 'body' is traced to PIE *kwrep- 'body, form, appearance'; the reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: corpus（属格 corporis）“身体”被追溯到原始印欧语 *kwrep-“身体、形体、外观”；该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: The adjective corporate attaches to corporations and incorporated bodies. In the 19c. it becomes the everyday adjective of large business.
items.cn: 形容词 corporate 与 corporation 及法人团体绑定。19 世纪它成为大企业的日常形容词。

items.en: Corporate culture, corporate governance and corporate identity appear as management vocabulary; corporatism names a state organised by occupational bodies.
items.cn: corporate culture、corporate governance、corporate identity 作为管理词汇出现；corporatism 指按职业团体组织起来的国家。

items.en: Modern English uses corporate mainly as an adjective. The noun is corporation, and the verb incorporate keeps the literal 'put into a body'.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把 corporate 用作形容词。名词是 corporation，动词 incorporate 保留字面义“放进一个身体里”。

note.en: The first group shares corpus 'body'; the second group separates business, collective, institutional and commercial meanings.
note.cn: 第一组共享 corpus“身体”；第二组区分商业、集体、制度和营利这几种含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially physical punishment. It comes from corpus but means 'bodily', not 'of a company'.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指体罚。它来自 corpus，但意思是“身体的”，不是“公司的”。

entries.definition: having a physical body; tangible. It is the philosophical cousin of corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 有实体的；物质的。它是 corporate 的哲学近亲。

entries.definition: to include something as part of a whole, or to form a legal corporation.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物纳入整体，或组成法人公司。

entries.definition: related to buying and selling for profit. It focuses on trade, while corporate focuses on the legal body.
entries.definitionCN: 与营利性买卖有关。它聚焦交易，而 corporate 聚焦法律实体。

entries.definition: shared by a group. It is broader than corporate and does not imply a legal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 群体共同拥有的。它比 corporate 更宽泛，不暗示法律结构。

entries.definition: relating to an established organisation such as a university, bank, or hospital. It is wider than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与大学、银行、医院等已建立的组织有关。它比 corporate 范围更广。

entries.definition: relating to trade or a company, used before nouns such as business plan. It is plainer and less legal than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与交易或公司有关，用于 business plan 等名词前。它比 corporate 更日常、更少法律色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: corpus 'body' + -ate 'made'. Corporation, corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all belong to the body family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：corpus“身体”+ -ate“使成为”。corporation、corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都属于“身体”词族。

normal.en: corpus means body. A corporation is a group given one legal body, and corporate means belonging to that body.
normal.cn: corpus 意为身体。corporation 是被赋予一个法律身体的群体，corporate 表示属于这个身体。

normal.en: Corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all contain the body idea: a dead body, a body of troops, bodily, and put into a body.
normal.cn: corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都含“身体”：尸体、军队团体、身体的、纳入身体。

normal.en: A corporate logo is the face of the legal body; corporate law is its skeleton.
normal.cn: 公司标志是法律身体的脸；公司法是它的骨架。

normal.en: Corporate culture is the personality of the body, the habits its members share.
normal.cn: 企业文化就是这个身体的性格，是成员共享的习惯。

normal.en: Incorporate means 'put into the body', whether a clause into a contract or a business into a legal form.
normal.cn: incorporate 意为“放进身体里”，无论是把条款放进合同，还是把企业放进法律形式。

abstract.en: Imagine hundreds of employees welded into one silhouette. The silhouette signs contracts, owns buildings and speaks through one logo.
abstract.cn: 想象几百名员工被焊成一个人形轮廓。这个轮廓签合同、拥有大楼，并通过一个标志说话。

abstract.en: A corporation is a body without a heartbeat: it needs a board as its brain and a charter as its spine.
abstract.cn: 公司是一个没有心跳的身体：它需要董事会当大脑、章程当脊柱。

abstract.en: The same body image can be small as a shop or large as a state; only the scale of the silhouette changes.
abstract.cn: 同一个身体意象可以小到一家店铺，大到一个国家；变的只是轮廓的大小。

examples.en: The bank announced a major corporate restructuring.
examples.cn: 这家银行宣布了大规模的公司重组。

examples.en: Corporate responsibility includes how suppliers treat their workers.
examples.cn: 企业责任包括供应商如何对待工人。

examples.en: The city acts as a corporate body when it signs the contract.
examples.cn: 这座城市签署合同时，是以法人团体的身份行事。

dict_mnemonic.text: “考破瑞特”——考破瑞特把所有人并进同一个公司身体里 → corporate 公司的、团体的

root: 拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate，字面义“结成一体”，核心是“许多人合成一个法律上的身体”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of corporate, all one legal body: a company, a social power, a shared effort, a body in law, its law and finance, its face, a city, and the derived institutions built on the image.
sensesIntro.cn: corporate 的八个义项都是同一个法律身体：公司、社会力量、共同出力、法律上的团体、法律与财务、对外的脸、城市，以及由这个意象衍生的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many people are formed into a single body that can act in law.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多人被铸成一个能在法律上行动的身体。

branches.en: COMPANY: the body as a business and as a legal-financial structure.
branches.cn: 公司：作为企业、也作为法律—财务结构的身体。

branches.en: PUBLIC FACE: a large body with power, and a body with a logo.
branches.cn: 公众面孔：拥有权力的大身体，以及带着标志的身体。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE: work and authorship belong to the body, not one hand.
branches.cn: 集体：工作与署名属于身体，而不属于某一只手。

branches.en: LEGAL STATUS: bishops, cities and charities can all be one body.
branches.cn: 法律身份：主教团、城市、慈善机构都可以是一个身体。

branches.en: DERIVED INSTITUTIONS: corporation and corporatism extend the body to economy and state.
branches.cn: 衍生制度：corporation 与 corporatism 把身体扩展到经济与国家。

intro.en: Corporate takes corpus and the suffix -ate 'made, formed'. English builds corporation with -ion and incorpor- with in-. The body image is carried by the suffix change.
intro.cn: corporate 由 corpus 加后缀 -ate“使成为”构成。英语用 -ion 构成 corporation，用 in- 构成 incorpor-。身体意象随着后缀变化被带到新词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on corpus 'body': corpse, corps, corporal, corporeal and incorporate all describe a body or the putting of something into one.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 corpus“身体”上：corpse、corps、corporal、corporeal、incorporate 都描述身体，或把某物放进一个身体。

items.meaning: a company or group legally treated as a single body
items.meaningCN: 公司；法人团体（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The corporation employs thirty thousand people.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了三万人。

items.meaning: an economic or political system organised through occupational groups
items.meaningCN: 社团主义；合作主义（-ism 构成制度或意识形态）
items.example: Corporatism gave unions a formal role in the state.
items.exampleCN: 社团主义让工会在国家中获得正式角色。

items.meaning: a supporter of corporatism; relating to it
items.meaningCN: 社团主义者；社团主义的（-ist 表示人或属性）
items.exampleCN: 社团主义政策塑造了 20 世纪 30 年代。

items.meaning: to include something in a whole, or to form a legal corporation
items.meaningCN: 纳入；合并；组成法人（把某物放进身体）
items.example: The new rules were incorporated into the contract.

items.meaning: the act of forming a company, or of combining things into one body
items.meaningCN: 公司设立；并入（-ion 构成行为名词）

items.meaning: formed into a legal company, or combined into one body
items.meaningCN: 已注册为公司的；合并的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The firm is incorporated in Delaware.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在特拉华州注册。

items.meaning: relating to a body of people organized as one
items.meaningCN: 社团的；法团的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The corporative structure gave each guild a vote.
items.exampleCN: 这种社团结构让每个行会都有一票。

items.meaningCN: 无形的；非物质的（与 corpus“身体”同根）

latinEntries.meaning: a body of troops or a group with one role
latinEntries.meaningCN: 军团；团体（一群人的身体）
有实体的；物质的（拥有身体）

definition_zh: 畜牧经济；随畜群迁移的生活方式；以草场放牧为基础的社会形态；文学中的田园牧歌传统
definition_en: an economy and way of life built on raising livestock on open pasture, together with the tradition that idealizes it
core_image: 一片随季节移动的草场：毡房收起，羊群跟着水草走，人、畜、草绑在同一条路上。
scene: 天刚亮，毡房已经拆下捆好，羊群被赶向河边的新草场，牧人跟在后面。 The family lives by pastoralism, moving its flocks to fresh grass with every season.
sceneCN: 这里 pastoralism 指「以在开阔草场上放牧牲畜为主要生计的经济与生活方式」（第 1 个义项：人、畜、草随季节整体移动的谋生体系）；句意为这家人靠畜牧为生，每个季节都把羊群赶往新的草地。可辨识物件：毡房、捆好的木杆、羊群、牧人、河岸。

pos.zh: 畜牧经济；游牧生活方式；田园牧歌传统

collocations.zh: 畜牧与农耕（并存的生计）

derivatives.zh: pastor + -al（关系形容词后缀）→ 由「牧人」转为「牧人的、田园的」，并指田园诗
pastoral + -ist（从事者后缀）→ 以畜牧为生的人，也指研究畜牧的学者
pastoral + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以田园牧歌的方式
拉丁 pastoralis 经意大利语 → 田园曲，语义由牧人生活收窄为一种音乐体裁
agro-（田地）与 pastoral 复合 → 农牧结合的，语义落在耕作与放牧并行

senses.title: Raise livestock as the main livelihood
senses.titleCN: 以放牧牲畜为主要生计
senses.definition: to make a living chiefly by raising animals on pasture rather than by growing crops
senses.definitionCN: 主要靠在草场上饲养牲畜、而不是靠耕种来谋生
senses.example: Pastoralism shaped the economy of the steppe long before railways arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 在铁路出现之前很久，畜牧经济就已经塑造了草原的经济形态。
senses.why: pastor is a feeder of flocks and -ism names a whole system, so the word first labels an economy built on that role.
senses.whyCN: pastor 是「喂养畜群的人」，-ism 表示一整套体系，因此这个词首先指建立在这一角色上的经济。

senses.title: Move with the herds each season
senses.definition: a way of life in which people move their animals from one pasture to another as grass and water change
senses.definitionCN: 草与水发生变化时，人带着牲畜从一片草场迁到另一片草场的生活方式
senses.example: Pastoralism keeps the household on the move between winter and summer grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 畜牧生活让这个家庭在冬夏两处草场之间不断迁移。
senses.why: grazing land is renewed unevenly, so the flock must follow the grass, and the household follows the flock.
senses.whyCN: 草场的恢复并不均匀，畜群必须追着草走，而人家又必须跟着畜群走。

senses.title: Use grassland instead of ploughed fields
senses.titleCN: 以草场而非耕地为土地基础
senses.definition: a land-use system that draws its yield from grazing land rather than from cultivated fields
senses.definitionCN: 从草场而不是从耕地取得产出的土地利用方式
senses.example: Pastoralism suits the thin soils that would fail under repeated ploughing.
senses.exampleCN: 薄土反复耕作会退化，却适合畜牧。
senses.why: where rain is scarce and soil shallow, grass feeds animals as well as crops would feed people, so herding becomes the land use.
senses.whyCN: 在雨少土薄之处，草能养畜，其效率不亚于庄稼养人，于是放牧成了这片土地的用法。

senses.title: Share the customs of herder communities
senses.titleCN: 共享牧人群体的习俗与认同
senses.definition: the body of customs, skills and identity that herding families pass on to their children
senses.definitionCN: 放牧家庭传给下一代的习俗、技能与身份认同
senses.example: Their pastoralism includes a calendar of moves that no outsider learns in a single year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的畜牧生活包含一套迁移历法，外人一年之内学不会。
senses.why: a livelihood repeated for generations becomes a culture, so the same word covers the work and the way of living it.
senses.whyCN: 一种生计重复数代就会成为文化，因此同一个词既指活计，也指过这种活计的方式。

senses.title: Idealize shepherd life in art
senses.titleCN: 在文学艺术中美化牧人生活
senses.definition: a literary and artistic tradition that presents shepherd life as simple, peaceful and close to nature
senses.definitionCN: 把牧人生活写得朴素、安宁、贴近自然的文学与艺术传统
senses.example: The pastoralism of the poem owes more to city taste than to any real flock.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的田园情调更多来自城市口味，而不是真实的羊群。
senses.why: Latin pastoralis also named shepherd poems, and that poetic label survived as a term for idealized country life.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 pastoralis 也指牧人诗，这个诗学标签留存下来，用来指被理想化的乡野生活。

senses.title: Depend on wool, milk and meat
senses.definition: an economy whose cash and food come from animal products rather than from grain sales
senses.definitionCN: 现金与食物来自畜产品、而不是来自售粮的经济
senses.example: Pastoralism paid the family's taxes in wool and cheese rather than in coin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人的税是用羊毛和奶酪缴的，而不是用钱币。
senses.why: once the herd is the main capital, its products become the household's income, which is the economic face of the same system.
senses.whyCN: 一旦畜群成为主要资本，畜产品就成了家庭收入，这是同一体系的经济面孔。

senses.title: Serve as a subsistence model in anthropology
senses.titleCN: 人类学中的一种生计类型模型
senses.definition: an analytic category that compares herding societies with farming, fishing and hunting ones
senses.definitionCN: 把畜牧社会与农耕、渔猎社会相互比较的分析类别
senses.example: In the textbook, pastoralism is paired with agriculture as the two dryland options.
senses.exampleCN: 在教科书里，畜牧与农耕被并列为干旱地区的两种选择。
senses.why: researchers needed a neutral label for a whole livelihood, so they took the older word and turned it into a model.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要为整套生计找一个中性的标签，于是取来旧词，把它改造成分析模型。

senses.title: Live off a slowly renewed resource
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：依赖缓慢再生的资源
senses.definition: any arrangement in which a community lives off a resource that renews itself slowly and must be allowed to recover
senses.definitionCN: 任何依赖缓慢再生、且必须留出恢复时间的资源来维持群体的安排
senses.example: The same logic of pastoralism applies to a forest worked in long cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的畜牧逻辑也适用于按长周期采伐的森林。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the shape of the old economy: take a little, let it grow back, move on.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留了旧经济的骨架：取一点，让它长回来，再挪到下一处。

intro.en: Pastoralism joins Latin pastor 'shepherd', from pascere 'to feed, graze', to the English suffix -ism. The pastoral adjective entered English in the sixteenth century; the system noun is modern.
intro.cn: pastoralism 由拉丁 pastor「牧人」（出自 pascere「吃草、放牧」）加英语后缀 -ism 构成。形容词 pastoral 在 16 世纪进入英语，指体系的名词则是近代产物。

items.en: Pascere meant 'to feed, graze'. It is generally regarded as going back to a root meaning 'to feed, protect', but the Indo-European form given for it is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: pascere 意为「吃草、放牧」。一般认为它可追溯到表示「喂养、保护」的词根，但为其给出的印欧形式属重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Pastor, pastoris 'shepherd' is literally 'one who feeds', formed from the same verb; the religious sense of English pastor came later.
items.cn: pastor、pastoris「牧人」字面就是「喂养者」，由同一动词构成；英语 pastor 的宗教义是后来的事。

items.en: The adjective pastoralis 'of shepherds' covered both real herding and shepherd poetry, and that double scope passed into English.
items.cn: 形容词 pastoralis「牧人的」既指真实的放牧，也指牧人诗，这一双重范围一并传入英语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century English pastoral named shepherd verse first and rural scenery second; the noun pastoralism grew out of that adjective.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，英语 pastoral 先指牧人诗，后指乡村景色；名词 pastoralism 正是从这个形容词长出来的。

items.en: The suffix -ism marks a system, practice or doctrine. Added to pastoral, it produced a word for livestock economies and for the literary ideal built on them.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 标记体系、实践或主张。加在 pastoral 上，就造出了指畜牧经济以及建立其上的文学理想的词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the system noun is recorded only from the nineteenth century, and no exact first citation is agreed; the pre-Latin shape of pascere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：指体系的名词只能追溯到 19 世纪，最早书证并无定说；pascere 在拉丁语之前的形式仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same feeding root that are easily taken for synonyms; group two holds neighbouring livelihoods with a different centre of gravity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「喂养」词根、容易被当成同义词的词；第二组是重心不同的邻近生计词。

entries.definition: The adjective of shepherds and of shepherd poetry; it describes a scene or a genre, while pastoralism names the economy or the tradition as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 牧人与牧人诗的形容词，描写景色或体裁；pastoralism 则指整套经济或整个传统。

entries.definition: The person who feeds a flock; in modern English its religious sense, a minister, is far more common than the herding one.
entries.definitionCN: 喂养畜群的人；在现代英语里，它的宗教义「牧师」远比放牧义常用。

entries.definition: The ground the animals eat, and the act of putting them on it; it is the land, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 牲畜吃草的地面，也指把牲畜放上去的动作；它是土地，不是体系。

entries.definition: From Latin pastillus 'little loaf', through Italian, and unrelated to shepherds; only the opening sounds suggest a link.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pastillus「小面包」，经意大利语传入，与牧人无关，只是开头读音近似。

entries.definition: A way of life built on moving the whole community; nomads may hunt, trade or herd, so the term says nothing about livestock.
entries.definitionCN: 以整个群体迁移为基础的生活方式；游牧者可以狩猎、贸易或放牧，因此这个词不涉及牲畜。

entries.definition: Commercial raising of livestock on fenced or owned land; pastoralism usually implies open range and community rights.
entries.definitionCN: 在围起或私有的土地上商业化养畜；pastoralism 通常意味着开阔草场与群体权利。

entries.definition: A combined system in which a household both farms and herds; it is a hybrid, not pastoralism alone.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭既耕种又放牧的混合体系，是杂交形态，而非单纯的畜牧。

entries.definition: The daily work of driving and watching animals; pastoralism is the whole economy that this work supports.
entries.definitionCN: 每天驱赶与看管牲畜的劳动；pastoralism 是这项劳动所支撑的整套经济。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pastor 'shepherd' + -ism 'system': the shepherd's work raised to a whole way of living.
normal.cn: pastor「牧人」+ -ism「体系」：把牧人的活计放大成一整套活法。

normal.en: The family runs pastor, pastoral, pastoralist, pastoralism and pastorally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pastor、pastoral、pastoralist、pastoralism、pastorally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: nomadic pastoralism, sedentary pastoralism, commercial pastoralism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：游牧式畜牧、定居放牧、商业化畜牧。

normal.en: The same feeding root sits in pasture and pascere 'to graze'.
normal.cn: 同一个「喂养」词根也见于 pasture 与 pascere「吃草」。

normal.en: Anthropology pairs it with agriculture as the two dryland options.
normal.cn: 人类学把它与农耕并列为干旱地区的两种选择。

abstract.en: Picture a household that owns almost nothing except a moving herd and a route it has used for centuries.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家，除了会走的畜群和一条用了数百年的路线，几乎一无所有。

abstract.en: Picture a field of grass that is never asked for more than it can regrow in a season.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地，从不被索取超过一季能长回来的量。

abstract.en: Picture a poem about shepherds written by someone who has never smelled a sheep.
abstract.cn: 想象一首牧人诗，出自从未闻过羊味的人之手。

examples.en: Pastoralism survives in the highlands because ploughing there costs more than it returns.
examples.cn: 畜牧在高地得以延续，因为在那里开垦的代价高于收成。

examples.en: Scholars now treat pastoralism as one option among several, not as an earlier stage of farming.
examples.cn: 学者如今把畜牧视为若干选择之一，而不是农耕的早期阶段。

examples.en: The museum's pastoralism room explains how wool paid for salt and iron.
examples.cn: 博物馆的畜牧展厅解释羊毛如何换来盐和铁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pastor（牧人）+ ism（主义）」——把放羊当成一整套活法 → 畜牧经济、田园牧歌传统

root: 拉丁 pascere「吃草、放牧」→ pastor「牧人」→ pastoralis「牧人的」+ 英语 -ism（体系后缀）；pascere 的印欧来源属重构形式。英语 pastoralism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circuit: a household feeds a herd, the herd follows the grass, and the whole arrangement is then read as land use, culture, an ideal, an income, a research model and finally a general rule for slow resources.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条循环展开：人家养畜群，畜群追草，整套安排再依次被读作土地利用、文化、理想、收入、研究模型，最后读作一条关于缓慢资源的通则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herder, a flock and a grass route bound into one moving unit.
core.cn: 核心意象：牧人、畜群与一条草地路线绑成一个会移动的整体。

branches.en: LIVELIHOOD AND INCOME: the herd is both the workplace and the household's purse.
branches.cn: 生计与收入：畜群既是干活的地方，也是这户人家的钱袋。

branches.en: MOVE AND GRAZE: following the grass turns a way of living into a way of using land.
branches.cn: 迁移与放牧：追着草走，把一种活法变成了土地的用法。

branches.en: CUSTOM AND DREAM: what is inherited as skill is also exported as poetry.
branches.cn: 习俗与梦想：当作技艺传下来的东西，也被写成诗传出去。

branches.en: RESEARCH MODEL: the whole livelihood is abstracted into a category for comparison.
branches.cn: 研究模型：整套生计被抽象成一个可供比较的类别。

branches.en: SLOW RESOURCE: strip away the sheep and one rule remains, take little and let it grow back.
branches.cn: 缓慢资源：抽掉羊群，只剩一条规则，少取一点，让它长回来。

intro.en: Pastoralism is built from a Latin noun and two suffixes, so its whole family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: pastoralism 由一个拉丁名词与两个后缀构成，因此整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin pascere gives pastor, pastoralis and pastura; English adds -al, -ist and -ism to build the modern family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pascere 衍生 pastor、pastoralis 与 pastura；英语再加 -al、-ist 与 -ism 构成现代词族。

items.example: The root names the act of putting animals on grass.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指把牲畜放到草上的动作。

items.example: The noun names the person who does the feeding.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指执行喂养的人。

items.example: The adjective covers both real flocks and shepherd verse.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既指真实的羊群，也指牧人诗。

items.example: Pastor plus -al yields the English adjective pastoral.
items.exampleCN: pastor 加 -al 得出英语形容词 pastoral。

items.meaning: of shepherds; rural; a shepherd poem
items.example: The pastoral scene hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 那幅田园画挂在壁炉上方。

items.meaning: a person who lives by herding
items.example: The pastoralist knew every well along the route.
items.exampleCN: 这位畜牧者熟悉沿线每一口井。

items.example: The valley is pastorally quiet in early spring.
items.exampleCN: 初春时这道山谷安静得像田园牧歌。

definition_zh: v. 围攻，围困（城镇、要塞）；团团围住；使应接不暇
definition_en: to surround a place with an army in order to capture it; to crowd around someone closely; to overwhelm someone with demands
core_image: 城墙外层层扎营的帐篷，把一座城连水带粮一起掐断
scene: 敌军在城外扎营三个月，切断了所有补给。 The enemy army besieged the town for three months, cutting off every supply line.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：besiege 指军队围攻城镇；句意是敌军围城三个月，切断了一切补给。

senses.title: To surround a place with an army
senses.definition: to surround a town or fortress with armed forces so that nothing can get in or out
senses.definitionCN: 以武装力量包围城镇或要塞，使人无法进出
senses.example: Supply wagons never reached the walls while the city was besieged.
senses.exampleCN: 城池被围期间，补给车始终没能抵达城下。
senses.why: Siege first meant a seat, the place an army set itself down in front of a wall.
senses.whyCN: siege 最初意为「座位」，即军队在城墙前安营落座之处。

senses.title: To crowd around someone
senses.definition: to press closely around a person or place, as a crowd does
senses.definitionCN: 像人群那样紧紧围住某人或某处
senses.example: Fans besieged the singer the moment she stepped out.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手一走出来，粉丝就把她团团围住。
senses.why: A crowd around a person looks like an army around a town, so the military image transfers to daily life.
senses.whyCN: 把人群围住某人想成军队围城，军事意象就自然转到日常生活。

senses.title: To overwhelm with requests
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with questions, letters or demands
senses.definitionCN: 用问题、来信或要求把人淹没
senses.example: The office was besieged with complaints after the change.
senses.exampleCN: 改版之后，办公室被投诉淹没了。
senses.why: The sense of the walls being pressed from outside becomes mental: requests crowd the mind with no gap.
senses.whyCN: 城墙被从外面挤压的感觉变成心理上的：请求密密麻麻，毫无缝隙。

intro.en: Besiege is the prefix be- laid over siege, a word that began as the seat an army takes in front of a wall.
intro.cn: besiege 是前缀 be- 加在 siege 上，而 siege 原本指军队在城墙前「落座」的地方。

items.en: Latin sedere means to sit, the root behind siege and session.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为「坐」，是 siege 与 session 的共同词根。

items.en: Old French siege means a seat, then the place where an army sits down.
items.cn: 古法语 siege 意为座位，后指军队安营落座之处。

items.en: English siege names the act of sitting down before a fortified place.
items.cn: 英语 siege 指在设防之地前「坐定」围困。

items.en: Adding be- makes a verb: to put an army all around the walls.
items.cn: 加上 be- 构成动词：把军队布满城墙四周。

items.en: The verb extends to crowds that press around a person.
items.cn: 该动词扩展到把某人团团围住的人群。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of being flooded with demands.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上「被要求淹没」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps other be- verbs so the prefix pattern stays in view; the near-meaning group moves from the physical ring to the abstract pressure.
note.cn: 形近组保留其他 be- 动词，让前缀规律一直可见；近义组由实体的包围圈走到抽象的压力。

entries.tag: same be- to trouble on all sides
entries.definition: To trouble or attack from every side.
entries.definitionCN: 从四面八方困扰或袭击。

entries.definition: To confuse someone completely.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全迷惑。

entries.tag: same be- to make a friend of
entries.definition: To become a friend to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人结为朋友。

entries.definition: To make someone or something seem small.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低某人或某物。

entries.tag: the plain verb for a ring
entries.definition: To be all around something.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕在某物四周。

entries.definition: To form a circle around something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物围成一圈。

entries.definition: To seal a place so nothing passes.
entries.definitionCN: 封锁某地，使任何东西都无法通行。

entries.definition: To attack continuously with shells or words.
entries.definitionCN: 以炮弹或言语连续攻击。

normalIntro.en: Siege began as a seat, so besiege is an army parking itself around a wall until the gates give in.
normalIntro.cn: siege 起初是「座位」，所以 besiege 就是军队在城墙外一坐不起，直到城门屈服。

normal.en: Siege means a seat, so a siege is an army sitting down outside a wall.
normal.cn: siege 意为座位，围城就是军队在城墙外坐下不走。

normal.en: Be- means all around, so be-siege is sitting all around the town.
normal.cn: be- 意为「四周」，be-siege 就是四面八方坐下来围住城。

normal.en: The tents do not move until the bread runs out.
normal.cn: 帐篷一直不动，直到面包吃完。

normal.en: A crowd around a celebrity copies the same ring of tents.
normal.cn: 围住明星的人群，就是同一圈帐篷。

normal.en: Being besieged with letters feels like walls closing in.
normal.cn: 被来信围住，就像城墙向内收拢。

abstract.en: A ring drawn in the dust that nothing may cross.
abstract.cn: 在尘土里画下的一个圈，任何东西都不得穿过。

abstract.en: Patience used as a weapon against a gate.
abstract.cn: 把耐心当作攻门的武器。

abstract.en: Attention pressed from every side until there is no gap left.
abstract.cn: 四面压来的目光，直到不留一丝缝隙。

examples.en: The city was besieged for two years before it fell.
examples.cn: 这座城被围困两年才陷落。

examples.en: Reporters besieged her as she left the courtroom.
examples.cn: 她离开法庭时，记者把她团团围住。

examples.en: The helpline was besieged with calls after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，求助热线被电话淹没。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「必死机」——城门被围得水泄不通，守军插翅难飞，怎么挣扎都像卡死的机器。

root: be-（围绕）+ 古法语 siege（座位、围困）→ 把军队「坐」满城的四周

sensesIntro.en: Three strands run from one image: the army that will not leave, the crowd that will not step back, and the requests that will not stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 三条义项都从同一个意象延伸：不肯撤走的军队、不肯后退的人群、不肯停下的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tents packed in rings around a wall, cutting every road into the town
core.cn: 核心意象：帐篷一圈圈围住城墙，切断通往城里的每条路

branches.en: A walled town with smoke rising inside.
branches.cn: 城墙之内升起炊烟。

branches.en: Supply carts turned back at the gate.
branches.cn: 被挡回城门的补给车。

branches.en: Microphones pushed toward one face.
branches.cn: 麦克风一齐伸向一张脸。

branches.en: A desk buried under unopened letters.
branches.cn: 被未拆信件淹没的办公桌。

branches.en: Pressure that will not let anything through.
branches.cn: 不留一丝通路的压力。

intro.en: Besiege is the prefix be- on a French noun; the endings below build its forms, and the roots below explain why a siege is a seat.
intro.cn: besiege 是前缀 be- 加一个法语名词；下面这些词缀构成它的各种形式，后面的词根解释了为什么 siege 是「座位」。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit and sedes a seat; both stand behind siege, session and sediment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为「坐」，sedes 意为座位；二者分别是 siege、session 与 sediment 的背景。

latinEntries.exampleCN: sedere 产生 siege 与 session。

latinEntries.example: Sedes is the seat inside siege.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sedes 就是 siege 里那个「座位」。
obsidere 演变为军事上的围城。

definition_zh: 鸟类学；鸟类学论著；大学里的鸟类学课程；对鸟类的系统描述与分类研究
definition_en: the scientific study of birds, and by extension the body of work, the course, or the specialised branch through which that study is pursued
core_image: 一张长桌上并排放着鸟皮标本、卡尺与一本翻旧了的鸟类名录
scene: 选课手册翻到生物系那几页，一门课注明每次上课都要在日出前到湿地集合。 She chose ornithology because the class met at a marsh before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 ornithology 是「鸟类学课程」（第 3 个义项：大学课程与院系里开设的鸟类学）；句意为她选了鸟类学，因为这门课的上课地点是黎明前的湿地。

pos.zh: 鸟类学；不可数（指学科），可数（指论著或课程）

forms.label: 复数（多部论著或多门分支）

derivatives.zh: 鸟类学的；与鸟类研究有关的
从鸟类学角度；就鸟类学而言
古鸟类学（研究化石鸟类）
鸟疫（鸟类中的一种衣原体感染）

senses.title: The Scientific Study of Birds
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies birds: their anatomy, classification, behaviour, ecology and evolution
senses.definitionCN: 研究鸟类的生物学分支，涵盖其解剖、分类、行为、生态与演化
senses.example: Ornithology began as a branch of natural history before it became a biology of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类学起初是博物学的一支，后来才成为独立的生物学。
senses.why: ornis is Greek for 'bird' and -logia means 'the study of', so the word names a discipline before it names anything else.
senses.whyCN: ornis 在希腊语中意为「鸟」，-logia 意为「对……的研究」，因此这个词首先命名的是一门学科。

senses.title: A Published Work on Birds
senses.definition: a book or monograph that treats a region's or a group's birds in a systematic way
senses.definitionCN: 系统论述某一地区或某一类群鸟类的书籍或专著
senses.example: His ornithology of the Punjab is still cited for its careful measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 他那部旁遮普鸟类学著作仍因其细致的测量而被引用。
senses.why: a discipline's name can stand for a book that embodies it, so a single volume can be called an ornithology, used countably.
senses.whyCN: 学科名可以代表体现该学科的一本书，因此单独一册也可称为一部鸟类学，此时可数。

senses.title: The Subject as Taught
senses.titleCN: 大学课程与院系里的鸟类学
senses.definition: the subject as it appears in a curriculum, a lecture course or a department's teaching programme
senses.definitionCN: 出现在课程表、讲座课程或院系教学计划中的这门学科
senses.example: Ornithology is offered in the biology department every other autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 生物系每隔一个秋季开设鸟类学课程。
senses.why: once a discipline is taught, its name also labels the slot in the timetable, which is the sense students meet first.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科一旦被教授，其名称也标注课程表上的那一格，这是学生最先遇到的义项。

senses.title: Describing and Naming Species
senses.titleCN: 描述与命名的分类学分支
senses.definition: the taxonomic side of the field: describing new forms, fixing type specimens and revising classifications
senses.definitionCN: 该领域的分类学侧面：描述新形态、确定模式标本、修订分类
senses.example: Descriptive ornithology still names several new species each year.
senses.exampleCN: 描述性鸟类学每年仍会命名若干新物种。
senses.why: this is the oldest layer of the discipline, where a bird must first be described before anything else can be said about it.
senses.whyCN: 这是该学科最古老的一层：必须先描述一只鸟，之后才能谈别的事情。

senses.title: Where Amateurs and Professionals Meet
senses.titleCN: 业余观鸟与专业研究的交界
senses.definition: the shared field in which skilled volunteers and salaried researchers contribute records to the same datasets
senses.definitionCN: 熟练的志愿观察者与受薪研究者把记录汇入同一批数据的共同领域
senses.example: The journal bridges amateur birding and academic ornithology.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊把业余观鸟与学院鸟类学连接起来。
senses.why: much of what the discipline knows arrives as counts from non-professionals, so the name covers the whole collaborative practice, not only its paid core.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科知道的许多事情来自非专业人士的计数，因此该名称覆盖整个协作实践，而不只是有薪的核心。

senses.title: Birds as Models for Behaviour and Ecology
senses.titleCN: 以鸟为模型的行为生态研究
senses.definition: the strand that uses birds to test general questions about mating, foraging, migration and life history
senses.definitionCN: 用鸟类来检验关于求偶、觅食、迁徙与生活史等普遍问题的研究方向
senses.example: Modern ornithology asks why clutch sizes vary with latitude.
senses.exampleCN: 现代鸟类学追问窝卵数为何随纬度变化。
senses.why: birds are visible, countable and widely banded, so the discipline became a testing ground for ideas that apply far beyond birds.
senses.whyCN: 鸟类可见、可计数且被广泛环志，这门学科因此成为检验那些远超鸟类本身的观念的试验场。

senses.title: The Museum and Literature Tradition
senses.titleCN: 博物馆标本与文献传统
senses.definition: the tradition that works from study skins, egg sets, sound archives and old printed descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 依托鸟皮标本、卵标本、声音档案与旧印刷描述开展工作的传统
senses.example: Museum ornithology depends on skins collected a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆鸟类学依赖一个世纪前采集的鸟皮标本。
senses.why: the discipline's evidence is stored rather than only seen alive, so its name also covers the cabinets and libraries that hold the record.
senses.whyCN: 该学科的证据被储存起来，而不只是活体观察，因此名称也覆盖保存记录的那些标本柜与图书馆。

senses.title: Bird Study in the Service of Protection
senses.titleCN: 应用于物种保护的研究
senses.definition: the applied form of the field, where surveys and population data are produced to guide conservation decisions
senses.definitionCN: 该领域的应用形态，产出调查与种群数据以指导保护决策
senses.example: Conservation ornithology supplied the evidence behind the wind-farm ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 保护鸟类学为风电场选址裁决提供了证据。
senses.why: when a discipline's counts start to decide where turbines may stand, its name naturally extends to that applied work.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科的计数开始决定风机可以立在何处，其名称自然延伸到这项应用工作。

intro.en: Ornithology is Greek ornis 'bird' (genitive ornithos) plus -logia 'the study or account of', from logos 'word, reason'. English took it through scientific Latin ornithologia; the deeper origin of ornis is not settled.
intro.cn: ornithology 是希腊 ornis「鸟」（属格 ornithos）加 -logia「对……的论述、研究」，后者源自 logos「言说、道理」。英语经科学拉丁 ornithologia 引入；ornis 更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Ornis is a Greek noun of the third declension meaning 'bird', with the genitive ornithos; it covered birds generally and survives in the combining form ornitho-.
items.cn: ornis 是希腊语第三变格名词，意为「鸟」，属格为 ornithos；它泛指鸟类，并以构词形式 ornitho- 留存至今。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'; the suffix -logia named a reasoned account of a subject, not merely a collection of facts.
items.cn: logos 意为「言说、叙述、道理」；后缀 -logia 指对某一主题的成体系论述，而不只是事实的堆叠。

items.en: Ornithologia was formed in early modern scientific Latin from the two Greek pieces; the coining is generally attributed to Aldrovandi's Ornithologiae (1599), though earlier uses may exist.
items.cn: ornithologia 在近代早期科学拉丁语中由两个希腊成分构成；一般认为出自阿尔德罗万迪 1599 年的《鸟类学》，但可能另有更早的用例，此处不选定论。

items.en: English ornithology is recorded from the seventeenth century, at first for a descriptive catalogue of a region's birds rather than for a research programme.
items.cn: 英语 ornithology 自 17 世纪有记录，最初指某一地区鸟类的描述性名录，而非一项研究纲领。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the word narrowed into a recognised branch of zoology, with Linnaean naming, study skins and dedicated journals.
items.cn: 在 18、19 世纪，这个词收窄为动物学中一个被承认的分支，配有林奈式命名、鸟皮标本与专门期刊。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first English citation is not established, and the pre-Greek origin of ornis has no agreed reconstruction; only the general Greek derivation is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的英语首见书证尚未确定，ornis 在希腊语之前的来源也没有公认的重构；可靠的只有其希腊语来源这一层。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes: two carry the same Greek ornis stem in different compounds, two only resemble the spelling. Group two places the field beside its neighbours on a scale from narrow to broad.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词：两个在不同复合词中带同一希腊词干 ornis，两个只是拼写相像。第二组把该学科放在由窄到宽的邻近学科之间。

entries.tag: same greek root different second e
entries.definition: A dinosaur group named from Greek ornis 'bird' plus pous 'foot'; it shares the stem but refers to dinosaurs, not to the study of birds.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟脚类恐龙，名称取自希腊 ornis「鸟」加 pous「脚」；词干相同，但指的是恐龙，而非鸟类研究。

entries.definition: From ornis plus pteron 'wing': a machine that flies by flapping wings; the stem is shared, the referent is an aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ornis 加 pteron「翼」构成：靠扑翼飞行的机器；词干相同，所指却是飞行器。

entries.definition: An American dialect adjective from ordinary, meaning stubborn or bad-tempered; it has no Greek root and no link to ornis.
entries.definitionCN: 美式方言形容词，源自 ordinary，意为脾气坏、固执；没有希腊词根，与 ornis 无关。

entries.definition: From Latin ornamentum 'equipment, adornment', from ornare 'to fit out'; the shared opening is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ornamentum「装备、装饰」，再上溯 ornare「配备」；开头的相像出于偶然。

entries.definition: The leisure activity of watching and listing birds; ornithology is its scientific counterpart, though the two share field skills.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录鸟类的休闲活动；ornithology 是其科学对应物，两者共享野外技能。

entries.definition: The study of animal behaviour in general; bird behaviour is one of its strongest traditions but not its whole scope.
entries.definitionCN: 对动物行为的总体研究；鸟类行为是其中最强的传统之一，但不是它的全部范围。

entries.definition: The study of animals as a whole; ornithology is a branch of it, restricted to one class.
entries.definitionCN: 对整个动物的研究；ornithology 是它的一个分支，只限于一个纲。

entries.definition: The study of birds' eggs and nests; a small specialty inside ornithology rather than a rival to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究鸟卵与鸟巢的学问；是 ornithology 内部的一个小专门方向，而非与之并列。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real institutional usage and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊构词成分、真实的机构用法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ornith- 'bird' + -logy 'study of': the discipline's name is literally 'bird account'.
normal.cn: ornith-「鸟」+ -logy「对……的研究」：学科名直译就是「关于鸟的论述」。

normal.en: The genitive ornithos explains why the stem is ornitho- and not orni- in longer words.
normal.cn: 属格 ornithos 说明了为什么在更长的词里词干是 ornitho- 而不是 orni-。

normal.en: Real phrases fix the branches: field, museum and conservation ornithology.
normal.cn: 真实搭配固定了各分支：野外、博物馆与保护鸟类学。

normal.en: The adjective is ornithological and the person is an ornithologist, with -ical and -ist added to the same base.
normal.cn: 形容词是 ornithological，人称是 ornithologist，都是在同一词基上加 -ical 与 -ist。

normal.en: Aldrovandi's Ornithologiae of 1599 is the usual anchor for the Latin term, though the attribution is not a proof.
normal.cn: 阿尔德罗万迪 1599 年的《鸟类学》通常被当作拉丁术语的锚点，但这一归属并非证明。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet drawer pulled open, each skin tagged with a place and a date.
abstract.cn: 想象拉开一只标本柜抽屉，每张鸟皮都挂着地点与日期的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a seminar room where half the students carry binoculars instead of notebooks.
abstract.cn: 想象一间研讨室，一半学生拿的不是笔记本而是望远镜。

abstract.en: Picture a coastline map with turbine sites crossed out after a survey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张海岸地图，调查之后几处风机点位被划掉。

examples.en: He read an old ornithology from cover to cover before his first field trip.
examples.cn: 第一次野外实习之前，他把一部旧鸟类学著作从头读到尾。

examples.en: Bird study grew from cabinet collecting into modern ornithology.
examples.cn: 鸟类研究从标本柜收藏发展为现代鸟类学。

examples.en: The conference drew both academic ornithologists and weekend birders.
examples.cn: 这次会议既吸引了学院里的鸟类学家，也吸引了周末观鸟者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「奥尼索罗吉」——「奥尼」听成清晨的一声鸟鸣，末尾的「罗吉」就是「学」→ 鸟类学

root: 希腊 ornis「鸟」（属格 ornithos，第三变格）+ -logia「对……的论述、研究」（源自 logos「言说、道理」）；经科学拉丁 ornithologia 进入英语，一般认为该拉丁词形出自阿尔德罗万迪 1599 年的著作。ornis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all descend from one phrase, 'the account of birds'. That account can be a discipline, a book, a course, a naming practice, a shared field culture, a research programme, a cabinet tradition, or an applied survey.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都源自同一个说法：「关于鸟的论述」。这份论述可以是一门学科、一部书、一门课、一套命名实践、一种共享的野外文化、一项研究纲领、一个标本柜传统，或一次应用调查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where skins, calipers and an old checklist lie side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌上，鸟皮标本、卡尺与一本旧名录并排放着。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: a branch of biology, and the naming work that began it.
branches.cn: 学科：生物学的一个分支，以及开启它的命名工作。

branches.en: EMBODIED FORMS: the account as a book, and as a slot in the timetable.
branches.cn: 具体载体：作为一本书的论述，以及作为课程表一格的论述。

branches.en: SHARED PRACTICE: volunteers and researchers feeding one dataset; birds as model organisms.
branches.cn: 共享实践：志愿者与研究者供给同一批数据；鸟作为模式生物。

branches.en: STORED EVIDENCE: the answer may be a skin in a drawer, not a bird in the bush.
branches.cn: 储存的证据：答案可能是抽屉里的一张鸟皮，而不是枝头的一只鸟。

branches.en: APPLIED SURVEY: counts that end up deciding where a turbine may stand.
branches.cn: 应用调查：最终决定风机可以立在何处的那些计数。

intro.en: Ornithology is three pieces: the Greek stem for bird, a linking vowel, and the suffix for a reasoned study. Longer relatives replace the last piece or add a prefix.
intro.cn: ornithology 是三段式：表「鸟」的希腊词干、连接元音，以及表示「成体系研究」的后缀。更长的同族词则替换末段或加前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek forms behind the word are ornis (genitive ornithos), logos, pteron 'wing' and pous 'foot'; the compound ornithopod and ornithopter reuse two of them.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的希腊词形是 ornis（属格 ornithos）、logos、pteron「翼」与 pous「脚」；复合词 ornithopod 与 ornithopter 各复用了其中两个。

items.structure: ornis (Greek noun, third declension, genitive ornithos)
items.example: The stem ornith- supplies 'bird' to every compound in the family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 ornith- 为这一词族的每个复合词提供「鸟」义。

items.example: The -o- lets ornith- join a second element smoothly.
items.exampleCN: 这个 -o- 让 ornith- 与第二个成分顺畅相接。

items.meaning: the study or reasoned account of
items.meaningCN: 对……的研究或成体系论述
items.example: Ornithology is the reasoned account of birds.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类学就是关于鸟的成体系论述。

items.example: Ornithology covers anatomy, behaviour and classification.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类学涵盖解剖、行为与分类。

items.meaning: relating to the study of birds
items.example: The library keeps an ornithological journal collection.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆收藏着一批鸟类学期刊。

items.example: An ornithologist checked the identification of the specimen.
items.exampleCN: 一位鸟类学家核对了这份标本的鉴定。

items.example: Ornithopods walked on three toes, like many birds.
items.exampleCN: 鸟脚类恐龙像许多鸟一样以三趾行走。

items.example: The ornithopter flew for eleven minutes on its best trial.
items.exampleCN: 这架扑翼机最好的一次试飞持续了十一分钟。

items.example: Palaeornithology relies on a handful of complete skeletons.
items.exampleCN: 古鸟类学依赖少数几具完整骨架。
